# Waivers and consent

Send a waiver to each person before an event or an activity. Each one signs on their own phone and you have a record for every one.

## Flip through the pages first.

Each card is the real document: its pages, its fields, its wording.

- [Liability waiver template](/templates/liability-waiver-template)
- [Photo release form](/templates/photo-release-form)
- [Media release form](/templates/media-release-form)

## The documents people collect most.

**Liability waiver.** Risk and responsibility, signed before an activity.

**Photo and media release.** Permission to use pictures, recordings and names.

**Permission slip.** A parent or guardian agrees to an activity.

## How it goes.

For example, a climbing gym emails its waiver to each guest before their visit, each guest signs on their own phone, and the gym can find any signed waiver by name.

1. **Send**: To each guest
2. **Sign**: On their phone
3. **Saved**: A record each
4. **Find**: By name

## A copy you can stand behind.

**Sealed copy.** One PDF with every signature, sealed so a later change shows.

**Certificate.** Who signed, when and from where, on the last page.

**Audit log.** Each step in order, exportable as a CSV.

## One participant, two pages, one signature.

The participant fills in who they are and ticks what they agree to, then signs and dates.


## Send it to everyone on the list.

Upload the guest list and send the waiver to each person. Each one signs on their own phone and gets a sealed copy of their own.

**Everyone saved.** Names and emails join your People list.

**Reminders.** Reminders go out until each person has signed.

## Find any waiver in seconds.

Every submission is a row with a date, a name and a sealed copy you can download.

**Export.** The audit log of each document downloads as a CSV.

## Four documents for activities, pictures and children.

Each can be sent to a whole list, so every person gets their own copy to sign.

**Photo release form.** Permission to use someone's picture. Subject signs, over 2 pages and 16 fields, about 7 minutes in all.

**Liability waiver template.** Risk and responsibility, signed before an activity. Participant signs, over 2 pages and 9 fields, about 4 minutes in all.

**Media release form.** A guardian lets you use a child's image and name. Parent or guardian signs, over 3 pages and 19 fields, about 8 minutes in all.

## What the document asks for.

Read from the template itself, so this list is what the signer will see.

**What the photo release form asks for.** Your full name, Organization or photographer, Event or occasion, Date, On the Organization’s website, On the Organization’s social media accounts, In printed material such as flyers, brochures and reports, In news stories and press releases, In paid advertising, My name may be used in captions, How long this lasts, Your email, Organization’s email, Printed name, and 2 more. Each box sits where it belongs on the page and belongs to one person, so nobody fills in a part that is not theirs.

**What the liability waiver asks for.** Event name, Your full name, Date, Organizer, Governing law (state), I have read this waiver and I understand it. I know that I am giving up some legal rights by signing it., Printed name, Participant signature, Participant date signed. Each box sits where it belongs on the page and belongs to one person, so nobody fills in a part that is not theirs.

**What the media release form asks for.** Organization, Event or activity, Child’s full name, Child’s date of birth, Inside the Organization, such as displays, newsletters and noticeboards, On the Organization’s website, On the Organization’s social media accounts, In news stories and press releases, In training or teaching material, Write “first name allowed” if it may, Organization’s email, An earlier end date, if I want one, Your full name, Your relationship to the child, and 5 more. Each box sits where it belongs on the page and belongs to one person, so nobody fills in a part that is not theirs.

## Before you send it.

A waiver is only as useful as the record behind it, so decide what you will keep.

**A list, not one at a time.** Upload the guest list and send the waiver to everyone at once. Each person gets their own copy and signs it, and each signature becomes its own signed record.

**Minors need a guardian.** For anyone under 18, use the media release or permission slip, where a parent or guardian signs on the child's behalf. Say clearly in the document whose permission is being given.

## While people sign.

The busy moment is the half hour before an event, and the signing page is built for it.

**Any phone, no account.** People sign on their own phone in a minute, with nothing to install and no password to forget.

**See who is missing.** The document list shows who has signed and when, so you can check it against the attendee list before the activity starts.

## Keeping the record.

The point of a waiver is being able to show it later.

**One sealed record per person.** Every signature is sealed on its own PDF with a certificate, so you can find one person's waiver without sorting through a pile.

**Export what happened.** The audit log records each step and exports as a CSV, which is handy for an insurer or a venue that asks for proof.

**Counted when sent.** Each document counts when it is sent, so plan for the number of people you expect. Free includes 15 a month; Pay as you go is $0.50 for each one past 15.

## Questions

**Do people need an account?**

No. They open the link and sign.

**Can I send to a whole group?**

Yes. Send to a list from a spreadsheet and each person gets their own copy to sign, with its own signed record. Free sends to up to 15 at a time.

**Where do the signed copies go?**

Into your document list and People list, each with its certificate.

# HR paperwork and onboarding

Send the offer, then the first-day paperwork, to each new person as a package they can sign in one sitting.

## Flip through the pages first.

Each card is the real document: its pages, its fields, its wording.

- [Offer letter template](/templates/offer-letter-template)
- [New hire paperwork](/templates/new-hire-paperwork)
- [Non-solicitation agreement](/templates/non-solicitation-agreement)

## Three steps for a new person.

**Offer letter.** Role, pay and start date, for the candidate to accept.

**New hire paperwork.** The forms to fill on day one, in one send.

**To a whole group.** Send to a list from a spreadsheet, on every plan.

## How it goes.

For example, a shop sends an offer letter and the first-day paperwork together, and the new hire signs both from a phone the night before they start.

1. **Offer**: Offer letter
2. **Accept**: Candidate signs
3. **Paperwork**: First-day forms
4. **File**: Sealed copies

## A copy you can stand behind.

**Sealed copy.** One PDF with every signature, sealed so a later change shows.

**Certificate.** Who signed, when and from where, on the last page.

**Audit log.** Each step in order, exportable as a CSV.

## The Employer fills in the terms. The Candidate signs.

Role, pay, start date and a few choices are fields the Employer completes. The Candidate adds a signature and a date.


## See every new person's paperwork at a glance.

One row per document, with its state. Remind the people who have not signed in one press.

**Send to many.** Send one template to a list from a CSV, on every plan.

## HR sees HR. A manager sees their team.

Roles and teams keep each group's documents apart.

**Named.** Every action is in the audit log with a name.

## An offer letter and a first-day pack.

One goes to a candidate to accept, the other to a new hire to fill in before day one.

**Offer letter template.** Role, pay and start date, for a candidate to accept. Employer and Candidate each sign their own boxes, over 3 pages and 26 fields, about 10 minutes in all.

**New hire paperwork.** The forms to fill on day one, in one send. Company and New starter each sign their own boxes, over 6 pages and 50 fields, about 16 minutes in all.

## What the document asks for.

Read from the template itself, so this list is what the signer will see.

**What the offer letter asks for.** Company name, Date of this letter, Candidate’s full name, Company’s legal name, Job title, Manager’s name, Start date, Place of work, or remote, Pay, with how often, How often you are paid, Classification, Paid time off, Hours or schedule, Background check, and 12 more. Each box sits where it belongs on the page and belongs to one person, so nobody fills in a part that is not theirs.

**What the new hire paperwork asks for.** Company name, Your full name, Start date, Role, Manager’s name, the people team contact, the IT contact, I have received and read the staff handbook, Handbook initials, I understand that I must treat colleagues, customers and suppliers with respect, and that harassment and discrimination , the person for raising concerns, I will keep the company’s and its customers’ private information private, during and after my employment, Privacy initials, I agree, and 36 more. Each box sits where it belongs on the page and belongs to one person, so nobody fills in a part that is not theirs.

## Before you send the paperwork.

Paperwork should not be the first thing a new person does on their first morning.

**Send early, send once.** The new hire pack gathers the usual paperwork into one send, so the person gets one email and fills everything in from a phone before they start.

**Keep the offer simple.** An offer letter states the role, the pay and the start date and asks for one signature. Anything long belongs in the agreement that follows, not in the offer.

## While the person decides.

A candidate with an offer is waiting on you as much as you are waiting on them.

**Nothing to install.** The candidate opens the link, reads the offer and signs, on a phone or a computer, without making an account.

**Reminders that are not awkward.** Reminders go out automatically until the person has signed, so you are not the one who has to ask twice.

**Send a batch.** When several people start together, send one template to a list from a CSV and each person gets their own copy to sign.

## After the person signs.

Hand off the signed copy and move on to the first day.

**A sealed copy for the file.** The signed PDF is sealed and carries a certificate of completion, ready to go into the person's file.

**Hear about it in your own tools.** A signed document can raise a signed webhook event, so your own systems know to start the next step.

**Team roles.** Give the people who send offers a role, and keep who can see what under control. Pro is one flat price for the whole workspace, and Pay as you go is $5 per team member a month.

## Questions

**Can the candidate sign on a phone?**

Yes. No app and no account.

**Can a manager approve first?**

Yes. Add an approver before the candidate.

**Is anything sent for me?**

No. Nothing goes out until you press send.

# Leases and rental applications

Collect the application, then send the addendum and the deposit agreement. The tenant signs first and the landlord is told when it is their turn.

## Flip through the pages first.

Each card is the real document: its pages, its fields, its wording.

- [Rental application form](/templates/rental-application-form)
- [Lease addendum template](/templates/lease-addendum-template)
- [Deposit agreement](/templates/deposit-agreement)

## Three documents for a rental.

**Rental application.** The applicant fills it in and signs.

**Lease addendum.** A change to the lease, signed in order.

**Deposit agreement.** The deposit, its terms and when it comes back.

## How it goes.

For example, a landlord sends a lease addendum, the tenant signs first, and the landlord is told it is their turn.

1. **Apply**: Rental application
2. **Sign**: Lease addendum
3. **Pay deposit**: Inside the document
4. **Keep**: Sealed copy

## A copy you can stand behind.

**Sealed copy.** One PDF with every signature, sealed so a later change shows.

**Certificate.** Who signed, when and from where, on the last page.

**Audit log.** Each step in order, exportable as a CSV.

## Landlord and Tenant, in order.

The Landlord describes the change. The Tenant signs first, and the Landlord is told when it is their turn.


## From the application to the kept copy.

**Send the application.** The applicant fills in the rental application and signs from their phone.

**Sign the addendum.** The tenant signs first. The landlord is told when it is their turn.

**Pay the deposit.** The deposit is a payment field inside the agreement, charged through your own Stripe account.

**Keep the record.** Both get the sealed PDF and a certificate.

## Applications and addenda for property work.

The paperwork that passes between a landlord, a manager and the person who rents.

**Rental application form.** The applicant fills it in and signs. Applicant signs, over 4 pages and 43 fields, about 18 minutes in all.

**Lease addendum template.** A change to a lease, signed in order. Landlord and Tenant each sign their own boxes, over 3 pages and 24 fields, about 9 minutes in all.

**Deposit agreement.** The deposit, its terms and when it comes back. Business and Customer each sign their own boxes, over 3 pages and 18 fields, about 7 minutes in all.

## What the document asks for.

Read from the template itself, so this list is what the signer will see.

**What the rental application form asks for.** Property address, Move-in date, Monthly rent, if listed, Full name, Date of birth, Phone, Email, Current address, How long at this address, Current landlord’s name and phone, Why you are moving, How many, including you, Other occupants, Pets, and 29 more. Each box sits where it belongs on the page and belongs to one person, so nobody fills in a part that is not theirs.

**What the lease addendum asks for.** Property address, Date of this addendum, Landlord’s name, Tenant’s name, Date of the original lease, What it is about, Write the new terms, Effective date, Type, breed and size, Pet’s name, Pet deposit or fee, in US dollars, Extra amount, in US dollars, When it is due, Space number or area, and 10 more. Each box sits where it belongs on the page and belongs to one person, so nobody fills in a part that is not theirs.

**What the deposit agreement asks for.** Date of this agreement, Business name, Customer’s full name, What the deposit holds, Pay deposit, How the deposit is held, Refund within, the condition for a refund, Date after which the deposit is kept, Remaining balance and when it is due, Governing law (state), Printed name, Title or capacity, Business signature, and 4 more. Each box sits where it belongs on the page and belongs to one person, so nobody fills in a part that is not theirs.

## Before you send it to a tenant or applicant.

Two different documents, two different ways of sending.

**An application goes to one applicant.** Send the rental application to each applicant, who fills in their details and signs from a phone. Each application is saved on its own, so you are not sorting a shared inbox.

**An addendum goes to named people.** A lease addendum goes to the tenants on a lease, each by email, with the signing order you choose. Put the names and addresses in before sending so they only have to read and sign.

## While tenants sign.

People sign at home in the evening, so make it easy on a phone.

**Sign from the sofa.** The signing page works on a phone with no app and no account, and the signer can draw a signature with a finger.

**Reminders until it is back.** Reminders go out automatically until everyone on the lease has signed.

**Collect a fee in the same step.** A payment field can take an application fee or a deposit as the last step of signing, through your own Stripe account. Paying comes after the signature.

## After the lease is signed.

A lease runs for a year or more, so the record matters.

**Payments in one list.** Every payment taken while signing appears on the Payments page with who paid, for which document, and its status.

**A record for every step.** The audit log shows when each tenant received, opened and signed, which settles most questions about who saw what and when.

## Questions

**Can a deposit be paid inside the document?**

Yes. Add a payment field. It goes to your own Stripe account.

**Can two tenants sign?**

Yes. Add each as a signer, in order or together.

**Is a lease template included?**

Not yet. A full lease is not in the library today, but you can upload your own lease and add the signing boxes.

# Permission slips and school forms

Send a permission slip to every family at once. Each parent signs from a phone and you see who is still missing.

## Flip through the pages first.

Each card is the real document: its pages, its fields, its wording.

- [Permission slip template](/templates/permission-slip-template)
- [Photo release form](/templates/photo-release-form)
- [Volunteer agreement template](/templates/volunteer-agreement-template)

## Three documents for a school year.

**Permission slip.** A parent agrees to a trip or an activity.

**Photo release.** Permission to use a child's picture.

**Volunteer agreement.** Terms for an adult who helps out.

## How it goes.

For example, a teacher sends a permission slip to every family from a list, and checks that evening who has not yet signed.

1. **Send to a list**: Every family at once
2. **Check**: Who has signed
3. **Parent signs**: On a phone
4. **Keep**: A record each

## A copy you can stand behind.

**Sealed copy.** One PDF with every signature, sealed so a later change shows.

**Certificate.** Who signed, when and from where, on the last page.

**Audit log.** Each step in order, exportable as a CSV.

## A parent signs for one child, once.

The parent or guardian fills in the details, ticks what they allow and signs.


## Every family, from one list.

Send the permission slip to the class list. Each family fills it in on their own phone and gets their own sealed copy.

**Saved.** Names and emails join your People list for the next trip.

## The email is in the school's name.

The email goes out under the school's name, with its logo and its reply-to address.

**Reminders.** Reminders go out until each family has signed.

## Documents for trips and activities.

Built to be sent to a whole class or a whole club in one go.

**Permission slip template.** A parent agrees to a trip or an activity. Parent or guardian signs, over 2 pages and 20 fields, about 8 minutes in all.

**Volunteer agreement template.** Terms for an adult who helps without pay. Organization and Volunteer each sign their own boxes, over 3 pages and 23 fields, about 7 minutes in all.

## What the document asks for.

Read from the template itself, so this list is what the signer will see.

**What the permission slip asks for.** School or group, Trip or activity, Date, Child’s full name, Child’s date of birth, Class or year, Health notes, My child will bring medicine, Dietary needs, Emergency contact’s name, Their phone, My phone, If I cannot be reached, I agree that the adults in charge may get urgent medical help for my child, How the group travels, and 6 more. Each box sits where it belongs on the page and belongs to one person, so nobody fills in a part that is not theirs.

**What the volunteer agreement asks for.** Organization name, Organization’s legal name, Volunteer’s full name, Role, Start date, Hours or schedule, Supervisor’s name, Expenses covered, if any, Emergency contact’s name, Their phone, Printed name, Volunteer signature, Volunteer date signed, Title or capacity, and 9 more. Each box sits where it belongs on the page and belongs to one person, so nobody fills in a part that is not theirs.

## Before you send it home.

A permission slip works best when it is specific and arrives early.

**Say what, when and who to call.** A good slip names the activity, the date and a person to call. The template has a place for each, so a parent can answer in one read.

**One list for the whole class.** Upload the class list and send the slip to every family at once. Each parent gets their own copy and signs it on their own phone.

## While the slips come back.

The question every teacher asks is who has not answered yet.

**No paper to chase.** A parent opens the email, signs with a finger and is done. There is no account, no app and nothing to print or send back in a bag.

**See the gaps.** The document list shows who has signed and when, so you can follow up with the families who have not answered.

## Keeping the record.

A signed slip is the answer to a question you may be asked months later.

**A sealed copy for each child.** Each signed slip is its own sealed PDF with a certificate of completion, so one family's answer is easy to find.

**An export for the office.** The audit log exports as a CSV, so the school office can keep the list with the trip file.

**Free to start.** A document counts when it is sent, and the Free plan includes 15 documents a month, with a list send of up to 15 at a time.

## Questions

**Can I send to a whole class?**

Yes, from a spreadsheet, on every plan. Free sends to up to 15 at a time.

**Can both parents sign?**

Yes. Add each as a signer.

**Can I see who has not signed?**

Yes. The document list shows each person's status, and a reminder goes out by hand or on a schedule.

# Statements of work and client agreements

Send the scope, then each change to it, then the deposit. Clients sign and pay in the same sitting.

## Flip through the pages first.

Each card is the real document: its pages, its fields, its wording.

- [Statement of work template](/templates/statement-of-work-template)
- [Change order template](/templates/change-order-template)
- [Service agreement template](/templates/service-agreement-template)

## Three documents for a client job.

**Statement of work.** What will be done, by when, for how much.

**Change order.** A signed change to the scope or the price.

**Deposit agreement.** The deposit, paid as it is signed.

## How it goes.

For example, an agency sends a statement of work with a deposit field, and the client signs and pays in the same sitting.

1. **Scope**: Statement of work
2. **Sign**: Client signs
3. **Pay deposit**: Inside the document
4. **Changes**: Change orders

## A copy you can stand behind.

**Sealed copy.** One PDF with every signature, sealed so a later change shows.

**Certificate.** Who signed, when and from where, on the last page.

**Audit log.** Each step in order, exportable as a CSV.

## The longest template we have, with every field placed.

Scope, deliverables, schedule and fees are all fields the Agency fills in. The Client reads, initials and signs.


## Take the first payment as the client signs.

Add a payment field to the agreement. The client pays on Stripe's page and cannot sign until it is paid.

**Your account.** Money goes to your own Stripe account.

## Every client's documents in one list.

Filter by state or date. Send a change order from the same template list.

**Status.** See what is signed and what is stuck.

## A scope for the job and a record for each change.

Two documents agencies reach for again and again, one for the work and one for when the work moves.

**Statement of work template.** What will be done, by when, for how much. Agency and Client each sign their own boxes, over 6 pages and 77 fields, about 26 minutes in all.

**Change order template.** A signed change to the scope or the price. Provider and Client each sign their own boxes, over 3 pages and 24 fields, about 9 minutes in all.

**Payment plan agreement template.** Payments by date, written into the agreement. Business and Customer each sign their own boxes, over 3 pages and 29 fields, about 11 minutes in all.

**Invoice approval form.** A signed yes before an invoice is paid. Sender and Approver each sign their own boxes, over 2 pages and 23 fields, about 8 minutes in all.

## What the document asks for.

Read from the template itself, so this list is what the signer will see.

**What the statement of work asks for.** Project name, Date of this SOW, Agency’s legal name, Client’s legal name, Date of the master agreement, if any, State the objective in a few sentences, Say how the Client will know it worked, Start date, End date, List what the Agency is assuming, the Agency’s project lead, How often the sides check in, the Client’s project lead, Review period, and 63 more. Each box sits where it belongs on the page and belongs to one person, so nobody fills in a part that is not theirs.

**What the change order asks for.** Project name, Date of this change order, Provider, Client, Date of the original agreement, Change order number, Describe what is changing, Reason for the change, Price before, Change in cost, with currency, Price after, Finish date before, New finish date, Explain how the extra cost or time was worked out, and 10 more. Each box sits where it belongs on the page and belongs to one person, so nobody fills in a part that is not theirs.

**What the payment plan agreement asks for.** Date of this agreement, Business name, Customer’s full name, The balance, with currency, what it is for, Any agreed reduction, such as a discount for paying on time, Number of installments, How often, First payment due, Installment 1 due, Installment 1 amount, Installment 2 due, Installment 2 amount, Installment 3 due, and 15 more. Each box sits where it belongs on the page and belongs to one person, so nobody fills in a part that is not theirs.

**What the invoice approval form asks for.** Invoice number, Supplier, Invoice date, Amount, with currency, Due date, Cost center or project, What the invoice is for, The goods or services were received, and the invoice matches the order or contract, The price and quantities match the order or contract, The goods or services were delivered or carried out as described, The invoice has not been paid already and is not a duplicate, There is budget for it, and the right cost center or project is recorded, Decision, Note, if any, and 9 more. Each box sits where it belongs on the page and belongs to one person, so nobody fills in a part that is not theirs.

## Before you send the scope.

Disputes about extra work almost always start with a scope that was never written down.

**One scope per job.** Use the statement of work for each job under a larger agreement, so every job has its own deliverables, dates and price, signed by the client.

**Describe it instead of filling it in.** If a job does not fit a template, describe it in plain words and Scribe writes the document and places the fields; you review it before it is sent. Scribe never sends on its own.

## While the client reviews.

The client is often busy, and the quicker the scope is signed the sooner the work can start.

**The client signs anywhere.** A link on a phone or a computer, no account, and a signature drawn or typed.

**Reminders on autopilot.** Reminders keep going until the client has signed, without you writing the third nudge.

**Send from your own system.** If your project tool already knows the client and the job, send the template from code and hear about the result through a signed webhook.

## When the scope changes.

The change order is the document that keeps the first agreement honest.

**Name the agreement it changes.** A change order records what changes, what it costs and when, and refers back to the agreement it changes. Send it before the extra work begins, not after.

**Get paid inside the document.** A payment field can take a deposit as the last step of signing, through your own Stripe account. The fee is 2% on Free and Pay as you go and 0% on Pro, on top of Stripe's.

**One price for the studio.** Pro is $35 a month flat for the whole workspace, so adding another account manager never changes the bill.

## Questions

**Can the client pay when they sign?**

Yes. Add a payment field. It goes to your own Stripe account.

**Can I put my own branding on it?**

Yes. Your logo and colour appear on the document and the emails, on every plan.

**Can I send through the API?**

Yes. See Sending from your code.

<!-- https://docustay.app/developers -->
# The e-signature API you own. One flat price for every user.

Open source and self-hostable. Pro is $35 a month for your whole team: no per-seat fees, unlimited people and documents. Signers can pay while they sign, straight into your own Stripe account, and Pro adds no fee.

Docustay is the open source e-signature API (AGPL-3.0): one OpenAPI 3.1 file with 64 operations, test mode on from the first call, signed webhooks, six clients (JavaScript, TypeScript, Python, Go, PHP, C#), a command line and an MCP server.

- [Quickstart](/docs/quickstart)
- [REST API](/developers/api)
- [Webhooks](/developers/webhooks)
- [Test mode](/developers/test-mode)
- [SDKs](/developers/sdks)
- [CLI](/developers/cli)
- [Agents and MCP](/developers/agents)
- [Embedding](/developers/embedding)
- [Keys and security](/developers/keys-and-security)

Send: POST /api/v1/documents/send with an Authorization bearer key, an Idempotency-Key of 8 to 200 characters, and a templateId with parties. Webhooks use the Standard Webhooks headers and are retried after 1 minute, 5 minutes, 30 minutes, 2 hours and 12 hours. The limit is 600 requests a minute for each key.

---

<!-- https://docustay.app/developers/api -->
# REST API

POST a template and a party; read back the state. Bearer keys with scopes, an Idempotency-Key on every create.

## The parts you use.

**Auth.** Authorization: Bearer <key>. Twelve scopes you tick per key, from documents:read and documents:write to one-job scopes such as templates:read. A missing scope answers like a wrong key.

**Idempotency.** Creates take an Idempotency-Key of 8 to 200 characters. The same key and body returns the first answer.

**Errors.** { error: { kind, message, requestId, retryable } }. Kinds: invalid, unauthenticated, forbidden, not_found, conflict, rate_limited, dependency, timeout.

## What you will call first.

- **POST**: /api/v1/documents/send
- **POST**: /api/v1/documents
- **POST**: /api/v1/documents/{id}/embed-session
- **POST**: /api/v1/plays

- **GET**: /api/v1/documents?state=executed
- **GET**: /api/v1/documents/{id}
- **GET**: /api/v1/documents/{id}/signed.pdf
- **GET**: /api/v1/usage

## The same send in code.

```
import { Docustay } from "@docustay2026/sdk";

const docustay = new Docustay(process.env.DOCUSTAY_API_KEY, process.env.DOCUSTAY_URL ? { baseUrl: process.env.DOCUSTAY_URL } : {});
const doc = await docustay.sendDocument({
  templateId: process.env.DOCUSTAY_TEMPLATE_ID,
  parties: [{ seat: "signer_1", name: "Rosa Alvarez", email: "rosa@example.com" }],
});
console.log(doc.id, doc.state);
```

- **Rate**: 600 requests a minute per key; 429 with Retry-After
- **Fees**: No per-call or per-API-document fee on any plan
- **Retries**: Safe with the same Idempotency-Key

## Make a document from text you wrote.

A document is words plus people. Roles are words from the text, never seat numbers. It stays a draft until you send it.

```
curl -X POST https://app.docustay.app/api/v1/documents \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $DOCUSTAY_API_KEY" -H "Idempotency-Key: $(uuidgen)" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "title": "Retainer agreement",
    "source": { "type": "doc", "content": [
      { "type": "heading", "attrs": { "level": 1 }, "content": [{ "type": "text", "text": "Retainer agreement" }] },
      { "type": "paragraph", "content": [{ "type": "fieldTag", "attrs": { "name": "Client signature", "type": "signature", "role": "Client" } }] }
    ] },
    "people": [{ "name": "Dana Whitfield", "email": "dana@example.com", "role": "Client" }]
  }'
```

## Seven statuses, one error shape.

| Status | Usually means |
| --- | --- |
| 400 | A field is not valid; the message says which and why |
| 401 | The key is missing, wrong, revoked or lacks the scope (one answer for all four) |
| 403 | The workspace's plan or a setting does not allow this |
| 404 | No such document, template or seat |
| 409 | The request is fine but the state is wrong, such as voiding a finished document |
| 429 | Over the rate limit; wait the Retry-After seconds |
| 5xx | Our side; safe to retry with the same Idempotency-Key |

Every error is { error: { kind, message, requestId, retryable } }. Quote the requestId when you ask for help.

## Read your usage from code.

**Same numbers.** The billing page reads the same figures.

**Scope.** A key with documents:read.

## Know what an action will cost before you do it.

**Reads only.** Nothing is sent, charged or stored. The answer carries the same reason code the real action would fail with.

**Scope.** A key with documents:read.

## What happens between your request and the email.

| Topic | Detail |
| --- | --- |
| The key | The Authorization: Bearer header names the key; the key decides the workspace and the scopes. A missing scope answers exactly like a wrong key. |
| The retry guard | The Idempotency-Key header (8 to 200 characters) makes the create safe to repeat: the same key and body returns the first answer instead of sending twice. |
| The seats | templateId is the template's uuid, and each seat in parties is one of its seat keys. Seats appear in the order roles first appear in the document: signer_1, then signer_2. |
| The answer | 201 with the document id and state sent, plus emailed and notEmailed, so you know whether each person was emailed. |
| After the send | Everything after that is a GET on the document, or a webhook that tells you without asking. |
| The count | A sent document counts once; drafts, reminders, resends and test-mode documents never count. There are no per-call fees on any plan. |

## From sent to a sealed copy.

state moves sent, then partially_signed, then executed (or declined, expired, void). The sealed PDF is made a few seconds after the last signature.

```
curl https://app.docustay.app/api/v1/documents/$DOCUSTAY_DOCUMENT_ID \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $DOCUSTAY_API_KEY"
```

## Find a document again, by your own id.

| Parameter | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| limit and cursor | limit is 1 to 200; the answer carries page.nextCursor, which is null on the last page |
| state | Only documents in one state, such as executed |
| externalId | Your own id for the document, set when you sent it |
| metadata[key]=value | Up to 20 short key and value pairs you attached; both come back in webhooks |

The SDKs follow the cursor for you with eachDocument and each_document.

## What every answer carries.

| Where | What |
| --- | --- |
| RateLimit-Limit, RateLimit-Remaining, RateLimit-Reset | On every answer, in seconds for the reset; over the budget you get 429 with Retry-After |
| Docustay-Version | A date on every answer. A change that could break a caller gets a new date and is announced in the changelog first; additions do not change it |
| 403 with error.detail.code | plan_document_limit or plan_template_limit, with used, limit and resetsAt (the first of next month, UTC). Everything already made keeps working |
| Request body size | 1 MB through the API. A file goes in as base64, so about 700 KB is the most one request can carry; a bigger one is refused with 413 |
| Rate limit | 600 requests a minute per key. Retried POSTs with the same Idempotency-Key never send twice |

The OpenAPI 3.1 file at /api/openapi.json describes every operation.

## Where to go from here.

| Next | Why | Page |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Get told, do not ask | Seven signed events instead of polling, with replay from the delivery log. | Webhooks: /developers/webhooks |
| Choose your scopes | Make one key per integration and tick only what it needs. | Keys and security: /developers/keys-and-security |
| Practise safely | A test key emails only you and counts for nothing. | Test mode: /developers/test-mode |

## Questions

**Does a response contain a signing link?**

No. No response contains a signing link or an access code. A key cannot sign for anyone.

**Can I page through lists?**

Yes. The SDKs page for you with eachDocument and each_document.

**Is there a spec file?**

Yes. OpenAPI 3.1 at /api/openapi.json and a Postman collection at /api/docustay.postman_collection.json.


## Keep reading

- [Webhooks](/developers/webhooks)
- [Keys and security](/developers/keys-and-security)
- [SDKs](/developers/sdks)

<!-- https://docustay.app/developers/sdks -->
# SDKs

JavaScript, TypeScript and Python clients. Idempotency keys, retries, typed errors and webhook verification are built in. Go, PHP and C# clients are generated from the OpenAPI file: `go get github.com/docustay/docustay-go/docustay`, `composer require docustay/docustay-php`, `dotnet add package Docustay.Api`.

```
# npm install @docustay2026/sdk
import { Docustay } from "@docustay2026/sdk";
const d = new Docustay(process.env.DOCUSTAY_API_KEY);
const doc = await d.sendDocument({ templateId, parties });
console.log(doc.id, doc.state);
```

## What each client does for you.

- **Idempotency**: Adds an Idempotency-Key to every POST and reuses it on retries
- **Retries**: Retries 429 and 5xx and honours Retry-After
- **Errors**: Throws DocustayError with status, kind, message and requestId
- **Paging**: eachDocument and each_document walk every page

- **JavaScript**: @docustay2026/sdk · Node 18+, browser, Deno, Bun
- **TypeScript**: Types ship inside the package
- **Python**: docustay · Python 3.9+, standard library only
- **Others**: Generate a client from the OpenAPI 3.1 file

## One call.

```
import { Docustay } from "@docustay2026/sdk";

const docustay = new Docustay(process.env.DOCUSTAY_API_KEY, process.env.DOCUSTAY_URL ? { baseUrl: process.env.DOCUSTAY_URL } : {});
const doc = await docustay.sendDocument({
  templateId: process.env.DOCUSTAY_TEMPLATE_ID,
  parties: [{ seat: "signer_1", name: "Rosa Alvarez", email: "rosa@example.com" }],
});
console.log(doc.id, doc.state);
```

## Every call exists in the API, both SDKs and the MCP server.

| API | JavaScript | Python | MCP tool |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| POST /documents | createDocument | create_document | create_document |
| POST /documents/check | checkDocument | check_document | check_document |
| GET /documents/{id}/source | getDraftSource | get_draft_source | get_draft_source |
| POST /documents/{id}/revise | reviseDocument | revise_document | revise_document |
| POST /documents/{id}/send | sendDraft | send_draft | send_draft (asks first) |
| POST /templates/{id}/documents | useTemplate | use_template | use_template |
| POST /templates/{id}/defaults | setTemplateDefaults | set_template_defaults | set_template_defaults |

Everything the screens do, a key can do.

## Page through everything without writing the loop.

**Both clients.** each_document does the same in Python.

**No loop.** You never touch the cursor.

## Point the same client at a self-hosted install.

Both clients talk to https://app.docustay.app unless you say otherwise.

```
const docustay = new Docustay(process.env.DOCUSTAY_API_KEY, { baseUrl: "https://sign.example.com" });
```

## Every setting you can pass to the client.

| Setting | JavaScript | Python | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Server address | baseUrl | base_url | https://app.docustay.app |
| Retries on 429 and 5xx | maxRetries | max_retries | 2 |
| Request timeout | timeoutMs | timeout | 30,000 ms (JavaScript), 30 seconds (Python) |
| Your own fetch | fetch | not applicable | global fetch |

A retry waits for Retry-After when the answer has one, and every retry of one call reuses the same Idempotency-Key.

## Catch the typed error and read its fields.

Both clients throw DocustayError with status, kind, message and the request id. A plan limit is a 403 whose code says which limit.

```
import { Docustay, DocustayError } from "@docustay2026/sdk";
const docustay = new Docustay(process.env.DOCUSTAY_API_KEY);
try {
  await docustay.sendDocument({ templateId, parties });
} catch (e) {
  if (!(e instanceof DocustayError)) throw e;
  if (e.code === "plan_document_limit") console.log("limit reached, resets", e.detail.resetsAt);
  else console.log(e.status, e.kind, e.requestId, e.retryable);
}
```

## What was run before this page said it.

| Topic | Detail |
| --- | --- |
| The retry | A local server answered the first send with 429 and Retry-After: 1. The client waited, sent again with the same Idempotency-Key and got the 201: two attempts, one key, one document. |
| The receiver | Webhook verification is in the same package, so a receiver needs no second library. The webhooks page shows one that was run the same way. |
| The pager | eachDocument and each_document follow page.nextCursor until it is null, so you never write the loop. |

## The edges.

| Item | Detail |
| --- | --- |
| Install | npm install @docustay2026/sdk, or pip install docustay; Go, PHP and .NET: go get github.com/docustay/docustay-go/docustay, composer require docustay/docustay-php, dotnet add package Docustay.Api |
| Runtime | Node 18 or newer, a browser, Deno or Bun; Python 3.9 or newer, standard library only |
| Other languages | The OpenAPI 3.1 file at /api/openapi.json and a Postman collection |

## Frameworks and the other languages.

| Package | What it is for |
| --- | --- |
| @docustay2026/react, @docustay2026/vue, @docustay2026/angular | Wrappers around the embedded signing element; they emit completed, declined and the rest as events |
| Go, PHP and C# | Plain HTTP with each language's own standard library, shown on the sign-a-document pages; or generate a client from the OpenAPI 3.1 file, and try each call by hand with the Postman collection |
| docustay (CLI) | Send a test document, forward webhooks and verify signatures from a terminal |

## The same call in JavaScript and Python.

```
import { Docustay } from "@docustay2026/sdk";
const docustay = new Docustay(process.env.DOCUSTAY_API_KEY);
const doc = await docustay.sendDocument({ templateId: process.env.DOCUSTAY_TEMPLATE_ID, parties: [{ seat: "signer_1", name: "Rosa Alvarez", email: "rosa@example.com" }] });
console.log(doc.id, doc.state);
```

## What each error kind asks of you.

| kind | What to do |
| --- | --- |
| validation | Fix the request; the message says which field and why |
| unauthenticated, forbidden | Check the key and its scopes; a 403 can also be a plan limit with a code |
| not_found, conflict | The id is wrong, or the document is in a state that does not allow it, such as voiding a finished one |
| rate_limited, dependency, timeout | Retried for you up to the limit; past it the error is thrown with retryable set |



## Where to go from here.

| Next | Why | Page |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Send your first test document | Make a key, send with a test key and read the state back. | Test mode: /developers/test-mode |
| Verify a delivery | verifyWebhook and verify_webhook take the raw body and the three headers. | Webhooks: /developers/webhooks |
| Use another language | The OpenAPI 3.1 file describes every operation; generators can build a client. | REST API: /developers/api |

## Questions

**Can I use another language?**

Yes. Call the REST API, or build a client from the OpenAPI 3.1 file.

**Which frameworks have wrappers?**

React, Vue and Angular wrappers for the embedded signer are MIT-licensed.

**Where is the source?**

On GitHub: https://github.com/Docustay/docustay (the sdk/ folder; the Go, PHP and C# clients have their own repositories, docustay-go, docustay-php and docustay-csharp).


## Keep reading

- [REST API](/developers/api)
- [Embedding](/developers/embedding)
- [Sign documents from code](/sign-pdf)

<!-- https://docustay.app/developers/webhooks -->
# Webhooks

Every document event, from sent and opened to signed, completed, declined and voided, signed with the Standard Webhooks headers. Verify the raw body, then fetch the document.

```
documents.document.sent
documents.document.opened
documents.document.signed
documents.document.executed
documents.document.declined
documents.document.expired
documents.document.voided
```

## Four steps.

1. **Read**: Raw body, as bytes
2. **Verify**: Three headers
3. **Dedupe**: webhook-id
4. **Answer 200**: Queue the work

## Refuse a changed body, a wrong secret, an old timestamp.

```
import { verifyWebhook } from "@docustay2026/sdk";
const event = await verifyWebhook(process.env.DOCUSTAY_WEBHOOK_SECRET, req.headers, rawBody);
```

## Delivery you can debug.

**Retries.** A failed delivery is retried, and every attempt is in the delivery log.

**Replay.** Send again replays an event as often as you like, so you can fix the receiver without making another document.

**Rotation.** Rotate an endpoint's secret without recreating the endpoint.

## Change one byte and the signature stops matching.

Each delivery carries a signature over its id, its timestamp and its raw body. A body that was changed on the way fails the check.

**Raw body.** Verify the bytes you received, not re-serialised JSON.

**Fresh.** A timestamp more than five minutes old is refused.

**Once.** Use webhook-id to ignore a repeat.

## Every event, and when it fires.

| Event | When |
| --- | --- |
| documents.document.sent | The document went out |
| documents.document.opened | Someone opened their link |
| documents.document.signed | One person signed |
| documents.document.executed | Everyone signed and the sealed copy exists |
| documents.document.declined | A person declined |
| documents.document.expired | It lapsed before everyone signed |
| documents.document.voided | The sender cancelled it |

Events carry facts about the document, never a signing link or a code.

## Trigger an event and check the signature locally.

**Replay.** Send again replays an event from the delivery log, as often as you like.

**Same code.** verify uses the same code as the SDK.

## Verify, ignore repeats, answer fast.

Read the raw body, verify the three headers against it, skip a webhook-id you have seen, answer 200 and do slow work afterwards.

```
import http from "node:http";
import { verifyWebhook } from "@docustay2026/sdk";
const seen = new Set();
http.createServer((req, res) => {
  const chunks = [];
  req.on("data", (c) => chunks.push(c));
  req.on("end", async () => {
    const raw = Buffer.concat(chunks).toString("utf8");   // the bytes you received
    let event;
    try { event = await verifyWebhook(process.env.DOCUSTAY_WEBHOOK_SECRET, req.headers, raw); }
    catch (e) { res.writeHead(400).end(e.message); return; }
    const id = req.headers["webhook-id"];
    if (seen.has(id)) { res.writeHead(200).end("repeat"); return; }
    seen.add(id);
    console.log(event.topic, event.subject_id);          // then queue the work
    res.writeHead(200).end("ok");
  });
}).listen(3000);
```

## What happens when your server is down.

| Attempt | Sent |
| --- | --- |
| 1 | Straight away |
| 2 | 1 minute after the first fails |
| 3 | 5 minutes later |
| 4 | 30 minutes later |
| 5 | 2 hours later |
| 6 | 12 hours later; after this one fails the delivery is marked as given up |

Six attempts in all. Any 2xx counts as delivered. Every attempt is in the delivery log, where Send again replays it.

## Add an endpoint and rotate its secret without a gap.

eventTypes come from GET /api/v1/webhooks/topics. The signing secret is in the answer once.

```
curl -X POST https://app.docustay.app/api/v1/webhooks \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $DOCUSTAY_API_KEY" \
  -H "Idempotency-Key: $(uuidgen)" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{ "url": "https://example.com/hooks/docustay", "eventTypes": ["documents.document.executed"] }'
```

## Three things people get wrong.

| Topic | Detail |
| --- | --- |
| Raw body only | Verify the bytes you received. A framework that parses JSON and re-serialises it changes the bytes, and the signature will not match. |
| A public address | Docustay posts only to a public https address. localhost, 127.0.0.1 and home or office network addresses are refused when you add the endpoint. Use docustay listen while you build. |
| Events are hints | They can repeat and arrive out of order. Fetch the document with GET /api/v1/documents/{id} rather than treating an event as the final word. |

## What an event carries.

| Field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| topic | The event name, such as documents.document.executed |
| subject_id | The id of the document the event is about |
| source | "sent" for a document your team sent |
| documents.template.fields_detected | A template made from an uploaded file had its fields looked for; the payload says how many were found, how many signers, how many it was unsure of and how many were placed |
| documents.ai.allowance_low | The workspace's AI drafts reached 80% of the period's allowance; sent once per period |
| documents.usage.threshold | A budget alert: the workspace used 50%, 80% or 100% of its monthly budget (kind "budget"), or the month closed (kind "summary"); each budget alert is sent once a month |

Events carry facts about the document, never a signing link or a code.

## Where to go from here.

| Next | Why | Page |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Build with the relay | docustay listen forwards signed events to your laptop; nothing is opened to the internet. | CLI: /developers/cli |
| Test the whole flow | A test key makes documents that fire the same events. | Test mode: /developers/test-mode |
| Read the document back | The REST API page covers states and the sealed copy. | REST API: /developers/api |

## Three commands that stand in for a public server.

From the command line, with a test key.

**listen.** docustay listen forwards real, signed webhook deliveries to an address on your own computer, such as http://localhost:3000/webhooks, so you never have to open a port.

**trigger.** docustay trigger sends a test event to the listening endpoint. Choose the event with --topic, for example documents.document.executed.

**verify.** docustay verify checks a signature the way your server should, from the secret, the webhook-id, the timestamp, the signature and the body.

## Questions

**Can I send to localhost?**

No. Endpoints must be public https addresses. Use a tunnel, or npx docustay listen --forward-to.

**Does an event carry a signing link?**

Never. Events carry facts about the document, not links or codes.

**Which event means finished?**

documents.document.executed: everyone signed and the sealed copy exists.

<!-- https://docustay.app/developers/test-mode -->
# Test mode

Send with a dsk_test_ key. The email goes only to you, the pages carry a TEST watermark, and nothing counts toward usage.

## What a test document does.

**Emailed only to you.** The subject carries [TEST]. The person you named is never emailed.

**Watermarked.** Its pages carry TEST, and the API says test: true.

**Left out.** Usage and billing ignore it, so you can practise as much as you like.

## Pick one.

**A test key.** Use a key that starts dsk_test_.

**A send option.** Send with send_options.test: true from the app.

**A setting.** Turn on Settings → Documents → Test mode for the workspace.

## The email comes to you, marked [TEST].

The person you named is never emailed. Every page of the document carries a TEST watermark.

**The API.** Documents carry test: true.

**The app.** A Test chip, and a banner on the signing page.

## Send with a test key, then read it back.

```
curl -X POST https://app.docustay.app/api/v1/documents/send \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $DOCUSTAY_TEST_KEY" \
  -H "Idempotency-Key: $(uuidgen)" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{ "templateId": "'"$DOCUSTAY_TEMPLATE_ID"'", "parties": [{ "seat": "signer_1", "name": "Practice Person", "email": "someone@example.com" }] }'
```

## What is different, line by line.

|  | Test | Live |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Who is emailed | Only the sender, subject marked [TEST] | The people you named |
| The pages | A TEST watermark | Clean |
| Usage and billing | Left out | Counted |
| Signing records | No real signature event | A real record |
| Payments | Not tested against real cards | Paid through your connected Stripe account |

Use test mode to check your whole flow before anything real is sent.

## Finish a test document without opening an email.

POST /api/v1/documents/{id}/test-sign signs one seat with sample answers through the same code a person's signature uses: consent, signing order, the audit trail and your webhooks all happen.

```
curl -X POST https://app.docustay.app/api/v1/documents/$DOCUSTAY_DOCUMENT_ID/test-sign \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $DOCUSTAY_TEST_KEY" \
  -H "Idempotency-Key: $(uuidgen)" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{ "seat": "signer_1" }'
```

## Pick how a document becomes a practice run.

| Topic | Detail |
| --- | --- |
| A test key | Everything a dsk_test_ key sends is a practice run, whether or not the workspace setting is on. |
| A send option | send_options.test: true from the app's own send step marks that one document. |
| A workspace setting | Settings, Documents, Test mode makes everything the workspace sends a practice run until you turn it off. |

## A test key sees only test data.

| Question | Answer |
| --- | --- |
| Can it read a live document? | No. Any other document answers 404 |
| Where do the emails go? | Only to the sender, with [TEST] in the subject |
| What do the pages look like? | A TEST watermark on every page |
| Does it count? | No. Left out of usage and billing |
| Is a signature recorded as real? | No. Signing it records nothing as a real signature event |

Use it to check that your template places fields where you expect and that your receiver verifies a delivery.

## What test mode cannot tell you.

| Topic | Detail |
| --- | --- |
| Real cards | Test mode does not test payments against real cards, so a flow that takes money needs a Stripe test card on top. |
| Real inboxes | A test document goes only to you, so it cannot show how a recipient's mail provider treats the message. Send one live document to an address of your own for that. |
| Going live | Switch to a dsk_live_ key, or turn the workspace setting off. Nothing in your code changes except the key. |

## A full practice run in five steps.

| Step | What you do |
| --- | --- |
| 1. Key | Make a dsk_test_ key with documents:read and documents:write |
| 2. Send | POST /api/v1/documents/send with a template and a party you invent; the answer has "test": true |
| 3. Read | Open the [TEST] email in your own inbox; the person you named is never emailed |
| 4. Sign | Sign from the email, or call test-sign on the seat |
| 5. Check | GET the document until state is executed, and watch your webhook receiver verify the event |

Nothing in a practice run is counted or billed.

## Where to go from here.

| Next | Why | Page |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Watch the events | A test document fires the same webhooks as a live one. | Webhooks: /developers/webhooks |
| Run it from a terminal | docustay send --test refuses a live key unless you say --live. | CLI: /developers/cli |
| Know your key | Scopes, expiry and address limits for the key you ship with. | Keys and security: /developers/keys-and-security |

## Questions

**Does test mode charge a card?**

No, and it does not test payments against real cards.

**Does a test signature count as real?**

No. Signing a test document records no real signature event.

**Can I tell a test document from a real one?**

Yes. The API says test: true and the app shows a Test chip and a banner.


## Keep reading

- [Webhooks](/developers/webhooks)
- [REST API](/developers/api)
- [Command line](/developers/cli)

<!-- https://docustay.app/developers/cli -->
# Command line

Log in, send a test document, forward signed webhooks to your laptop, verify a PDF, read the logs.

```
$ npx docustay login
$ npx docustay send --test
$ npx docustay listen --forward-to http://localhost:3000/webhooks
$ npx docustay verify signed.pdf
$ npx docustay logs
```

## Five commands.

- **login**: Store a key for this machine
- **send --test**: Send a practice document to yourself
- **listen**: Forward real signed events to a local URL and print the secret

- **verify**: Check a signed PDF
- **logs**: Read recent API calls

## Send, then read the logs.

**Safe by default.** send --test refuses a live key unless you also say --live.

**Machine-readable.** Add --json to any command.

## What each one does.

| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| docustay login | Save your API key for this machine, readable only by you |
| docustay whoami | Check the saved key |
| docustay send --test | Send a test document from a template |
| docustay listen | Forward signed webhooks to your own computer |
| docustay trigger | Send a test event to the listen webhook |
| docustay verify | Check a webhook's signature the way your server should |
| docustay logs | Recent email log, or a webhook's recent deliveries |

MIT licensed. Node 18 or newer.

## Keys come from the environment.

DOCUSTAY_API_KEY and DOCUSTAY_URL override the saved ones.

```
export DOCUSTAY_API_KEY=dsk_test_…
export DOCUSTAY_URL=https://sign.example.com   # only for a self-hosted install
npx docustay send --test $DOCUSTAY_TEMPLATE_ID --party signer_1="Rosa Alvarez <rosa@example.com>" --json
```

## Build a receiver without a public address.

listen makes a relay webhook once and fetches its signed deliveries to your computer. The signature your code checks is the real one.

```
npx docustay login
npx docustay listen --forward-to http://localhost:3000/webhooks --events documents.document.executed
```

## The rest of what docustay does.

| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| detect <file.pdf> | Find the fields on a PDF; nothing is stored |
| templates [library / customize <slug>] | List the built-in templates; customize <slug> makes your own copy |
| search <words> | Documents, templates and people, best first |
| documents [list / show / remind / void] | Your documents, one document's people and events, a reminder, or cancel one that is out for signature |
| webhooks [list / create / test / rotate / delete / deliveries] | Where Docustay posts events; the signing secret is shown once |
| payments [list / refund <id>] | Payments taken while signing; a refund never runs without --yes |
| playbooks [list / on / off] | Switch a playbook on or off |
| ai usage | AI drafts used, left, and when they reset |

Add --json to any command for machine-readable output.

## Where it keeps things.

| Topic | Detail |
| --- | --- |
| The saved key | login keeps your key in ~/.config/docustay/config.json, readable only by you. DOCUSTAY_API_KEY and DOCUSTAY_URL override it, which is what CI should use. |
| Same code as the SDK | verify uses the SDK's own check: pass the secret, the webhook id, timestamp and signature, and a body file or - for standard input. |
| Built from source | MIT licensed, Node 18 or newer. Install it with npm install -g docustay, or run any command with npx docustay; the source is in sdk/cli in the repository. |

## The flags that change what a command does.

| Flag or variable | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| --json | Machine-readable output from any command |
| --live | Lets send use a live key; without it send --test refuses one |
| --yes | Required for payments refund to run without a typed yes |
| --rotate | With listen, makes a new signing secret |
| --events a,b | With listen, forward only those event names |
| DOCUSTAY_API_KEY, DOCUSTAY_URL | Override the saved key and server address; use them in CI and for a self-hosted install |



## Use it in a shell script.

```
export DOCUSTAY_API_KEY=dsk_test_…
npx docustay templates library --json > templates.json
npx docustay search "services agreement" --per 3 --json
npx docustay documents list --state completed --json
```

## Nothing opens to the internet.

| Part | What happens |
| --- | --- |
| First run | listen makes a relay webhook once (relay: true on POST /api/v1/webhooks) and prints its signing secret a single time |
| Delivery | It fetches the signed deliveries from Docustay and forwards each to your --forward-to address, so your receiver sees the real signature |
| Sample events | trigger sends a sample event of the topic you name, default documents.document.executed |
| After the fact | logs --webhook WEBHOOK_ID shows that webhook's recent deliveries |



## Verify a saved body.

verify takes the secret, the three header values and the raw body from a file, or - for standard input.

```
npx docustay verify --secret whsec_… --id msg_1 --timestamp 1790000000 --signature "v1,…" --body body.json
```

## Where to go from here.

| Next | Why | Page |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Understand the events | Which seven events exist and what each payload carries. | Webhooks: /developers/webhooks |
| Practise safely | Why send --test refuses a live key. | Test mode: /developers/test-mode |
| Call it from code | The SDKs wrap the same routes the commands use. | SDKs: /developers/sdks |

## The commands, as the command line itself lists them.

Run docustay help for the full text and flags.

**Sign in and check.** login saves your API key, readable only by you, and whoami checks it. DOCUSTAY_API_KEY and DOCUSTAY_URL override what is saved.

**Send and listen.** send --test sends a test document from a template, listen forwards webhooks to your computer, trigger sends a test event and verify checks a signature.

**Look things up.** search finds documents, templates and people, best first. documents lists, shows, reminds and voids. logs shows the recent email log or a webhook's deliveries.

**Templates and playbooks.** templates library lists the built-in templates and templates customize makes your own copy of one. playbooks lists what is on and switches a playbook on or off.

**Payments.** payments lists payments taken while signing and can refund one with a reason.

**Fields and AI.** detect finds the fields on a PDF without storing anything, and ai usage shows the AI drafts used, the drafts left and when they reset.

## Questions

**Why use listen?**

Endpoints must be public https addresses, and listen forwards signed events to localhost so you can build a receiver.

**Does it print my key?**

No. A key is stored for the machine and never printed.


## Keep reading

- [Webhooks](/developers/webhooks)
- [Test mode](/developers/test-mode)
- [REST API](/developers/api)

<!-- https://docustay.app/developers/agents -->
# AI agents and MCP.

An assistant can list templates, draft a document and ask to send it. A person approves the send.

```
agent  → start_draft  template: services-agreement
agent  → answer_questions  3 answers
agent  → get_draft_source  draft_id
agent  → request_send  draft_id
←  202 · waiting for your approval
```

## Where a human stays in the loop.

1. **Agent**: Reads and drafts
2. **Draft**: In your workspace
3. **Your approval**: Settings → Developers → Approvals
4. **Send**: Only after you say so

## Every tool is draft-only.

- **Read**: list_templates, get_template, list_documents, get_document, get_draft_source
- **Plays**: list_plays, get_play, start_draft, answer_questions
- **Draft**: use_template
- **Ask**: request_send

- **Lasts**: 90 days, then it stops
- **Limit**: 100 drafts a day
- **Shown as**: Connector: the assistant's name, in Settings → Developers → API keys
- **Revoke**: Revoke the key and the connector stops at once

## Connect it, call it, cut it off.

**Hosted connector.** Add one address to the assistant, sign in once and press Allow. Sign-in uses OAuth with PKCE.

**Plays API (Pro).** List and publish plays, and call them from code.

**Revoke any time.** Every use is in the audit log with the key's name. Revoking takes effect at once.

## The local MCP server runs on your computer.

```
{ "mcpServers": { "docustay": { "command": "npx", "args": ["-y", "@docustay2026/mcp"],
  "env": { "DOCUSTAY_API_KEY": "dsk_test_…" } } } }
```

## The first call previews. The second acts.

send_document does nothing the first time: it returns a plain-words preview of who would be emailed. Only a call with confirm: true acts.

```
{ "name": "send_document", "arguments": { "templateId": "6f1c1f0e-7a0c-4d1d-9b5e-2f0a7b1c3d4e", "parties": [{ "seat": "signer_1", "name": "Sam", "email": "sam@example.com" }] } }
```

## What an assistant can and cannot do.

|  | Allowed | How |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Read templates and documents | Yes | With the scopes on its key |
| Draft a document | Yes | A draft only; nothing in it sends |
| Send, remind or void | Asks first | A preview, then confirm: true |
| Run read-only | Yes | DOCUSTAY_READ_ONLY=1 removes every changing tool |
| Sign for someone | Never | No tool does it |
| See a signing link or a code | Never | No tool returns one |

A key without the scope gets the same plain 401 as any bad key.

## Every call carries the key's name.

Every use is in the audit log, and revoking a key takes effect at once.

**Revoke.** One key per assistant, so you can cut one off alone.

## Add the server to your assistant.

@docustay2026/mcp runs on your own computer with your own key. Start with a test key, and a read-only run if you only want it to look.

```
{ "mcpServers": { "docustay": { "command": "npx", "args": ["-y", "@docustay2026/mcp"], "env": { "DOCUSTAY_API_KEY": "dsk_test_…" } } } }
```

## Which tool needs which scope.

| Tool | Changes things? | Scope (any one) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| list_documents, get_document | No | documents:read |
| send_document, remind, void_document | Yes | documents:write |
| create_template_from_html | Yes | templates:write |
| start_draft, answer_questions | Yes (drafts only) | drafts:write |
| list_plays, list_playbooks | No | plays:read |
| get_ai_usage, get_payments_status | No | account:read |

The full table is derived from the server's own route table and checked by a test. A key without the scope gets the same plain 401 as any bad key.

## Let the agent ask; a person decides.

A draft-only key can make and edit drafts. Asking it to send answers 202, the document stays a draft, and a person approves or declines in Developers, Approvals.

```
const draft = await docustay.createDocument({ title: "Services agreement", source, people });
const check = await docustay.checkDocument({ source, people });   // read every problem it lists
const r = await docustay.sendDraft(draft.id);   // 202, state "draft", approval.status "pending"
```

## The connector, for assistants that cannot run a program.

| Fact | Detail |
| --- | --- |
| The key | Docustay makes a draft-only key when you approve; it lasts 90 days and allows 100 drafts a day |
| Where you see it | In Developers, API keys, named Connector and the assistant's name; revoke it there and the connector stops at once |
| Sign-in | OAuth with PKCE (S256 only) and dynamic client registration; no client secret is stored |
| Its tools | list_templates, get_template, list_documents, get_document, list_plays, get_play, start_draft, answer_questions, use_template, get_draft_source, request_send |

Every tool is one call to the same /api/v1 routes the SDKs use, so scopes, limits and the draft-only rule apply as anywhere else.

## Where to go from here.

| Next | Why | Page |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Make the key | Pick the scopes the assistant needs and nothing else. | Keys and security: /developers/keys-and-security |
| Practise first | A test key keeps every email to you. | Test mode: /developers/test-mode |
| Browse the templates | The same library is on the API and in the tools. | Plays and templates: /developers/plays |

## Questions

**Can I make it read-only?**

Yes. Set DOCUSTAY_READ_ONLY=1 and every tool that changes anything is removed.

**Which assistants work?**

Any that speaks the Model Context Protocol and can use OAuth or a bearer key.

**Where are the skills?**

The Claude Code plugin bundles the server and five skills: sending, text tags, embedded signing, webhooks and agent safety.

**Does a tool return a signing link or a key?**

Never. No tool returns a signing link, a code or the key.


## Keep reading

- [Plays and Playbooks API](/developers/plays)
- [Keys and security](/developers/keys-and-security)
- [Scribe](/features/scribe)

<!-- https://docustay.app/developers/embedding -->
# Embedding the signer

Put the signing form in your own page with one element. Your key stays on your server.

## From your server to the signer.

1. **List the site**: Settings → Developers → Embedding
2. **Send**: embedded: ["signer_1"]
3. **Session**: POST …/embed-session
4. **Show**: <docustay-sign url>

## The element.

- **url**: The session address
- **height**: Pixels or any CSS length
- **auto-height**: Follow the form's own height
- **title**: Accessible name

- **ready**: The form loaded
- **completed**: The signer finished
- **declined**: The signer declined
- **error**: The link was refused
- **resize**: detail.height changed

## One element, or a wrapper for your framework.

Give the session url to the element. The API key stays on your server.

```
<script type="module" src="https://docustay.app/embed/index.js"></script>
<docustay-sign url="https://…/sign/pdf?t=…&embed=1" height="720"></docustay-sign>
```

## Four rules the embed enforces.

| Rule | What it means |
| --- | --- |
| Your sites only | The form can be framed only by the websites you listed; Docustay sends a frame-ancestors header naming exactly those |
| Embedded seats only | An ordinary emailed link is never frameable, even with embed=1 added |
| One parent | The form sends its events to one parent origin, the one in the link |
| One hour | A session link works for an hour; ask again on each page load |



## Let your people build templates inside your page.

The same editor Docustay uses, in a frame on your website. Your server asks for a session.

```
POST /api/v1/embedded/builder-session
{ "origin": "https://app.example.com", "name": "Services agreement" }
```

## How the pieces fit.

| Topic | Detail |
| --- | --- |
| List your website | In Developers, Embedding add each site, one per line, such as https://app.example.com. http://localhost:3000 is allowed while you build; no path and no other plain http. |
| Send embedded seats | Add embedded: ["signer_1"] to the send request on your server. Nobody is emailed for those seats. |
| Ask for a session | Call POST /api/v1/documents/{id}/embed-session with the seat and origin. The answer is url and expiresAt, good for one hour. |
| Show it | Give the url to the docustay-sign element, or to a wrapper for React, Vue or Angular. The browser sees only the url. |

## Send, then ask for the session.

The embed-session call needs an Idempotency-Key and a key with the embedded:write scope (documents:write opens it too). The API key never leaves your server.

```
curl -X POST https://app.docustay.app/api/v1/documents/send \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $DOCUSTAY_API_KEY" -H "Idempotency-Key: $(uuidgen)" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{ "templateId": "'"$DOCUSTAY_TEMPLATE_ID"'", "embedded": ["signer_1"], "parties": [{ "seat": "signer_1", "name": "Rosa Alvarez", "email": "rosa@example.com" }] }'
```

## What the element tells your page.

| Event | When |
| --- | --- |
| ready | The form has loaded |
| waiting | It is not this person's turn yet |
| completed | The signer finished |
| declined | The signer declined |
| error | The link was refused: expired, wrong, or the website is not on the list |
| resize | The form's height changed (detail.height) |

Attributes are url, height, auto-height and title. Events do not bubble.

## Treat completed as a prompt.

| Topic | Detail |
| --- | --- |
| Confirm on your server | Treat completed as a prompt, not proof: confirm with GET /api/v1/documents/{id} on your server and look for state executed. |
| Only your listed websites | The signing page can be framed only by the websites you listed under Developers, then Embedding. With no websites listed it cannot be framed anywhere. |

## Let your people build templates in your page.

| Part | Detail |
| --- | --- |
| Server call | POST /api/v1/embedded/builder-session with the origin and a name; the website must already be on your allowed list or you get 409 |
| Element | docustay-builder, with url and height; it fires ready, saved ({ templateId, name, fields }) and error |
| The key inside the link | Made for this session only, kept in the #fragment so no server log sees it, expires in an hour, and can read and write templates and nothing else |
| After saving | Use the templateId to send documents from your server as usual |



## The rules for the website list.

| Entry | Accepted? |
| --- | --- |
| https://app.example.com | Yes: a scheme and a host |
| http://localhost:3000 | Yes, while you develop |
| https://app.example.com/page | No: no path |
| http://app.example.com | No: no plain http outside localhost |

Add them in Developers, Embedding, one per line. A site not on the list makes the element fire error and a builder session answer 409.

## Where to go from here.

| Next | Why | Page |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Make the key | embedded:write is its own scope; give it to one key. | Keys and security: /developers/keys-and-security |
| Practise | Embed a test document and sign it with test-sign. | Test mode: /developers/test-mode |
| Confirm on the server | Read the document state after completed. | REST API: /developers/api |

## Questions

**Is anyone emailed for an embedded seat?**

No. Nobody is emailed for seats you mark embedded.

**Can I develop on localhost?**

Yes. http://localhost:3000 is allowed while you build.

**Which licences?**

The React, Vue and Angular wrappers are MIT.


## Keep reading

- [REST API](/developers/api)
- [Keys and security](/developers/keys-and-security)
- [SDKs](/developers/sdks)

<!-- https://docustay.app/developers/keys-and-security -->
# API keys and security

Scopes, expiry and an address allow-list. A key is shown once and every use is in the audit log.

```
dsk_test_…   practice data only
dsk_live_…   real documents
whsec_…      webhook secret, shown once
```

## What a key can do.

- **Twelve scopes**: You tick the scopes a key carries, from the broad documents:read and documents:write down to one-job scopes such as templates:read.
- **documents:read**: List and read documents and templates, the audit log, signed copies
- **documents:write**: Send, make templates, remind, void, start an embedded session
- **The full table**: In the docs under Authentication

- **Sign**: A key cannot sign for anyone
- **Links**: No response contains a signing link or a code
- **Scopes**: A key holds only scopes its creator holds

## Keep a key safe.

**Server only.** Never put a key in a web page or a mobile app.

**One per integration.** Revoke one without breaking another; revoking takes effect at once.

**Audited.** Every use is in the audit log with the key's name.

## What each scope lets a key do.

| Scope | Lets the key |
| --- | --- |
| documents:read | List and read documents and templates, read the audit log, download signed copies, read teams |
| documents:write | Send documents, make templates, remind, void, start an embedded signing session |
| templates:read | List and read templates and the built-in template library |
| templates:write | Make and change templates and their defaults; make a draft from, or customize, a built-in template |
| account:read | Read plan usage, payment status and teams |
| webhooks:read | List your webhook addresses and what was sent to them |
| webhooks:write | Add, change, test and remove webhook addresses; make a new signing secret |
| embedded:write | Start an embedded signing session for a seat you marked as embedded |
| plays:read | Read skills and playbooks |
| plays:write | Make and change skills and playbooks |
| drafts:write | Make drafts only; nothing in it sends a document |
| people:read | List the people in your workspace by name |

A key can only carry scopes its creator holds. A request without the scope gets the same 401 as a wrong key, on purpose.

## From key to answer.

List executed documents with a key that has documents:read.

```
curl https://app.docustay.app/api/v1/documents?state=executed \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $DOCUSTAY_API_KEY"
```

## The log says which key made which call.

A 401 after it used to work means the key was revoked, expired or lost a scope. Make a new key, update the one integration that used it.

**Test keys.** dsk_test_ keys act on test data only.

## Four rules for every key.

| Topic | Detail |
| --- | --- |
| Server only | Keep a key on your server. Never put one in a web page or a mobile app. |
| One per integration | Make a key per integration so one can be revoked alone, and tick only the scopes it needs. |
| Named in the log | Every use of a key is in the audit log with the key's name, and revoking takes effect at once. |

## What can be limited on a key.

| Option | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| dsk_test_ prefix | Test mode: practice runs only, sees only test documents |
| dsk_live_ prefix | Acts on real documents |
| Address list | The key works only from the addresses you list |
| Expiry | The key stops working on the date you set |
| Draft only | Can make and edit drafts but cannot send; a send request waits for a person |
| Daily limits | Exact limits on drafts and sends; past them the key gets 429 |

A key can only carry scopes its creator holds.

## Tell a bad key from a missing scope.

You cannot, from the answer, and that is deliberate: nothing tells a guesser which half was right. Check the log, not the response.

```
try {
  await docustay.listDocuments({ state: "executed" });
} catch (e) {
  if (e.status === 401) console.log("revoked, expired, wrong or missing documents:read:", e.requestId);
  else throw e;
}
```

## What no key can do.

| Topic | Detail |
| --- | --- |
| No links | No response contains a signing link or an access code. |
| No signing for anyone | A key cannot sign for a person. A test key can sign a test document with test-sign, nothing else. |
| One exception | For seats you mark as embedded when you send, a key can ask for a one-hour session to show your own signer the form on a website you listed. |

## Scopes for the job in front of you.

| Job | Scopes |
| --- | --- |
| Read templates only | templates:read |
| Send and follow documents | documents:read, documents:write |
| Manage webhook endpoints | webhooks:read, webhooks:write |
| Show a signing form in your page | embedded:write, plus documents:write to send |
| An agent that drafts | drafts:write, documents:read, templates:read; tick Draft only |
| List your people by name | people:read |

If a key leaks, make a new one, update the one integration that used it, and revoke the old; revoking takes effect at once.

## Where to go from here.

| Next | Why | Page |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Hand a key to an agent | A draft-only key can prepare documents and cannot send. | Agents: /developers/agents |
| Call the API | Send with the key you just made. | REST API: /developers/api |
| Rotate a webhook secret | A new secret can overlap the old for up to 168 hours. | Webhooks: /developers/webhooks |

## Questions

**What does a 401 mean?**

The key is missing, wrong, revoked or lacks the scope. One answer covers all four on purpose.

**Can a key expire?**

Yes. Set an expiry when you make it.

**Can I limit where it is used?**

Yes. A key can be limited to addresses.


## Keep reading

- [REST API](/developers/api)
- [Security](/trust#security)
- [Agents](/developers/agents)
