<!-- https://docustay.app/developers/plays -->
# Plays and Playbooks API

List the built-in templates, draft from one, and publish your own Plays and Playbooks.

## The routes.

- **GET**: /api/v1/templates/library: the built-in templates
- **GET**: /api/v1/templates/library/{slug}
- **POST**: /api/v1/templates/library/{slug}/documents
- **POST**: /api/v1/templates/library/{slug}/customize

- **GET**: /api/v1/plays: skills
- **POST**: /api/v1/plays: publish your own
- **GET**: /api/v1/playbooks: packs of templates and skills
- **POST**: /api/v1/drafts: a draft from a template

## List the built-in templates.

The built-in templates, with what each asks and who signs.

```
curl https://app.docustay.app/api/v1/templates/library \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $DOCUSTAY_API_KEY"
```

## Which scope does which job.

| Scope | Lets the key |
| --- | --- |
| plays:read | Read skills and playbooks |
| plays:write | Make and change skills and playbooks |
| templates:read | Read the template library |
| templates:write | Make a draft from, or customize, a built-in template |
| drafts:write | Make drafts only; nothing in it sends a document |

Reading and using the template library is on every plan; skills and playbooks of your own are on Pro.

## It asks its questions, then drafts.

Each built-in template carries its own questions. Pick one and answer them; you review the draft before anything is sent.

**Free to use.** Built-in templates and skills are free. Your own skills and playbooks are on Pro.

## The calls, by what you want to do.

| You want to | Call | Scope |
| --- | --- | --- |
| List the built-in templates | GET /api/v1/templates/library | templates:read |
| One built-in with its fields and guidance | GET /api/v1/templates/library/{slug} | templates:read |
| A draft from a built-in | POST /api/v1/templates/library/{slug}/documents | templates:write |
| Your own copy of a built-in | POST /api/v1/templates/library/{slug}/customize | templates:write |
| A draft that asks the template's questions | POST /api/v1/drafts | drafts:write |

documents:read and documents:write open the same routes.

## Draft from a built-in, or make a copy.

Drafting from a built-in makes no copy, so it does not count toward the Free plan's new templates. Customizing makes your own template, which does.

```
const { templates } = await docustay.listLibraryTemplates();
const draft = await docustay.draftFromLibraryTemplate("mutual-nda");   // not a new template
const mine = await docustay.customizeLibraryTemplate("mutual-nda", { name: "Our NDA" });   // a new template
```

## Start a draft that asks its own questions.

POST /api/v1/drafts replies needs_input with up to four questions, each with two to four options, until the must-ask ones are answered. Then it replies draft. Nothing is sent.

```
curl -X POST https://app.docustay.app/api/v1/drafts \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $DOCUSTAY_API_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{ "template": "services-agreement", "people": [{ "name": "Ana Client", "email": "ana@example.com", "role": "Client" }] }'
```

## Skills and playbooks.

| Topic | Detail |
| --- | --- |
| Skill | Guides how a document is written, such as a late fee or Plain English. It never picks a template. Served at /api/v1/plays. |
| Playbook | A pack of templates and skills for one job. The built-in packs are free to switch on; your own are Pro. Served at /api/v1/playbooks. |

## What uses up the Free plan's new templates.

| Action | Counts? |
| --- | --- |
| Customize a built-in into your own copy | Yes, it is a new template |
| Send or draft straight from a built-in | No, no copy is made (the sent document counts as a document) |
| A new version of a template you have | No |
| Deleting a template | Does not give one back |
| On Pay as you go, Pro, Lifetime or a self-hosted install | No template limit |

At the limit the API answers 403 with error.detail.code plan_template_limit.

## Every built-in is an ordinary template.

|  | A built-in template |
| --- | --- |
| Who it goes to | The people you name |
| How you use it | Send straight from it, or draft from it |
| Where the list is | GET /api/v1/templates/library |
| Same list in | The SDKs, the CLI and the MCP server |

An owner or admin can hide the built-in library in Settings, Templates; a built-in that you already use keeps working.

## Where to go from here.

| Next | Why | Page |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Hand it to an assistant | The same library is available as tools. | Agents: /developers/agents |
| Pick the right scope | plays:read, plays:write and drafts:write are separate scopes, so a key can do one job. | Keys and security: /developers/keys-and-security |
| Send what you drafted | A draft becomes a document through the send call. | REST API: /developers/api |

## The same library, in two commands.

Useful when you want a template without opening the app.

**templates library.** Lists the built-in templates. Add --json for something a script can read.

**templates customize.** Makes your own copy of a built-in template, by its slug, with a name you choose. The original never changes, and the copy is a new template.

**playbooks on and off.** playbooks list shows the packs of templates and skills, and playbooks on or off switches one by name. Your own skills and playbooks are on Pro.

## Questions

**What is a skill?**

A reusable instruction for how a document is written, such as a late-fee clause or Plain English. Templates carry their own questions.

**Which are free?**

The built-in templates, add-ons and house styles are free to list and use on every plan. Your own skills and playbooks are on Pro.

- [Scribe](/features/scribe)
- [Agents](/developers/agents)
- [REST API](/developers/api)

<!-- https://docustay.app/trust -->
# Trust centre

What is in place today, and what is not, on one page. We write claims as facts about what the product does.

## What we do, and what we do not.

- **Separate**: Each workspace's rows are separated in the database itself
- **Seal**: A digital signature over every finished PDF
- **Record**: Each action with its time, address and browser
- **Back up**: The database is backed up daily to a separate location; we do not test restores on a schedule

- **Certify**: No audit or certification is done and none is claimed
- **Read**: Docustay staff do not read your documents
- **Sell**: We do not sell data or train a model on your documents
- **Advise**: Nothing here is legal advice

## What is in place.

Data in transit travels over TLS, and the site tells browsers to use it every time (HSTS).

Each workspace's data is separated from every other's by row-level rules in the database itself, forced on for every table that holds workspace data, not only in the application. The application connects as a role that cannot switch them off.

People sign in with a password, an emailed code or a passkey. Everyone can turn on two-step sign-in with an authenticator app, and an owner can require it for the whole team. Sessions can be listed and ended, and a workspace can sign people out after a period without activity.

Signed documents are sealed with a digital signature.

Secrets we store for you (webhook signing secrets, two-step secrets) are sealed with AES-256-GCM under a key kept apart from the database. Requests are rate-limited. Signing links are single-purpose tokens that are not kept in the address bar after load.

Every file we store for a workspace (uploaded PDFs, the signed and sealed copies, certificates and printed templates) is encrypted with AES-256-GCM before it is written to storage, under a data key that belongs to that workspace alone. Each workspace's key is itself sealed under a platform key kept outside the database, and a file is bound to its workspace and its place in storage, so a file copied into another workspace, or to another path, does not open. Keys can be rotated: a background job moves a workspace's files onto the new key, and the old key is kept so an older backup still opens. A restored copy of the database together with a copy of the storage opens the files; either one alone does not, and neither does the database with a different platform key.

Server logs leave out email addresses and credentials. A dependency check runs before each release and stops it on a known serious flaw that reaches the code.

The database is backed up every day to a separate storage location, and those backups are deleted after 30 days. We do not currently test restores on a schedule. When a backup is restored, the recorded deletions are carried out again, so a deleted person or workspace does not come back.

Not yet: no outside audit, certification or penetration test has been done and none is claimed. There is no bug-bounty programme. The file encryption above does not cover the database itself (that depends on the disk the host provides), staff photos, brand logos or data exports, and the platform key protects the workspace keys only as well as the place it is kept.

## People, roles and two-step sign-in, from one screen.

Two-step sign-in is offered to everyone; an owner can require it for the whole team, and sessions can be listed and ended.

**Roles.** Each person has the access you assign.

## Keys, scopes and signed webhooks.

- **Shown once**: A key is shown when it is made and stored only as a digest, so we cannot read one back.
- **Scopes**: You tick the scopes a key carries, from documents:read down to one-job scopes.
- **Limits**: A key can expire and can be limited to addresses. Each key has its own per-minute budget; over it the API answers 429 with Retry-After.
- **Test keys**: dsk_test_ keys act on test data only.

- **Signed**: Every delivery carries the Standard Webhooks headers and an HMAC-SHA256 signature you check with the endpoint's secret.
- **Public only**: Webhooks go only to a public https address; local and office network addresses are refused.
- **Idempotent**: Send an Idempotency-Key and a retried POST does the work once.
- **Audited**: Every use of a key is in the audit log with the key's name.

## What we collect, where it lives, how long it stays.

We collect four kinds of information. Your account details. The documents you upload. The names and email addresses you type for signers. The record of each signing: time, address, browser and the wording agreed. Payment card details are never collected by Docustay; payments use Stripe's hosted page.

Your workspace's people see what you assign them. Signers see only their own document. Docustay staff do not read your documents.

The hosted service runs in the United States on Railway. You cannot yet choose a region. The self-hosted edition runs wherever you run it.

A signed document is kept for the period you set, or indefinitely if you leave it empty, and cannot be deleted one by one inside that period. Unsigned drafts are yours to delete. The API call log is kept 30 days.

Take it with you. Download any signed copy as a PDF. Export a document's audit log, the workspace's audit log, and the people list as CSV. Read everything through the API.

Removing it. A member can delete their own account, with a 14-day cooling-off period. An owner can delete the whole workspace, with a 14-day cooling-off period; then everything in it is removed. Backups are deleted after 30 days, and recorded deletions are carried out again after a restore. A record that a deletion happened is kept as a hash, a date and a request id, with no names or addresses.

We do not sell data. We do not use your documents to train a model.

## Where each kind of data is kept.

| Data | Kept at | Also handled by | How long |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Documents, PDFs and field values | Railway (US) | Anthropic, only when a person uses an AI feature | While your workspace exists |
| Audit trail and certificates | Railway (US) | No one else | With the document |
| Sign-in identity | Google (Firebase) | No one else | Until the account is deleted |
| Emails | Resend | No one else | Resend's send log |
| Payments | Stripe | No one else | Stripe's own records |
| Product analytics | PostHog | No one else | Set by PostHog's retention for our project |
| Backups | A separate storage location | No one else | 30 days |

## Docustay is not for protected health information yet.

Docustay is not for protected health information yet. We do not sign Business Associate Agreements, so please do not send protected health information through Docustay.

There is no health mode and no health setting. Every workspace gets the same protections: data travels over TLS, two-step sign-in is offered to everyone, and an owner can require it for the whole team.

Every view, download and export by the team is written to an access log that owners and admins can download, in every workspace.

Running it yourself? The self-host hardening guide is the checklist for sensitive documents: what to switch on, what to keep private and what to check. This is not legal advice.

## What is inside a signed PDF.

- [The record](/features/proof): Every signature is a row in an append-only record whose hash covers the one before it.
- [The seal](/features/proof): A detached PKCS#7 digital signature over the whole file; any later change makes it fail.
- [The certificate](/features/proof): The last page lists each person, the time and address of each act and the SHA-256 fingerprint.

## Each signature's hash covers the one before it.

Change one record and every later hash stops matching.

**Who and when.** The seat, name, email, time, address and browser.

**What was agreed.** The wording the person agreed to.

## A trusted time, and a check anyone can run.

The seal is stamped by a time-stamping authority (RFC 3161), so the time it was sealed is vouched for by someone other than us. If the authority cannot be reached the document is still sealed, and the certificate page says it was not timestamped.

By default the seal comes from a certificate Docustay makes for the deployment, so a reader may say the signer is unverified. Self-hosters set their own.

Anyone can drop a signed PDF on the verify page. It reads the seal and the fingerprint from the file itself and says whether it is intact. The file is not uploaded.

This is a simple electronic signature with a strong evidence record and a tamper-evident seal. It is not a qualified electronic signature and does not check anyone's identity beyond their email address or an access code you share.

## Sign it, seal it, check it.

When the last person signs, the PDF gets a digital signature over the whole file. Anyone can drop the copy on the verify page, with no account.

**Seal.** A digital signature over every finished PDF.

**Check.** The verify page reads the file in your browser; it is not uploaded.

## Nine companies.

- **Railway**: Application and database hosting. All data you store.
- **Google Cloud and Firebase**: Sign-in and supporting infrastructure. Account email and sign-in identifiers.
- **Stripe**: Payments and billing. Billing details and payment references; card numbers go to Stripe directly.
- **Resend**: Sending email. Recipient email address and the message.
- **Anthropic**: The AI model behind Scribe and Find fields with AI. The text or page pictures of a document, only when a person uses an AI feature, and only for that request.
- **Cloudflare**: Delivery of the website and the signing pages, and the bot check on the sign-up page. The visitor's address and browser. Page traffic passes through it in transit.
- **PostHog**: Product analytics. Events about how the website and the service are used, tied to an account id, never document content.
- **Google Analytics**: Website visit statistics, only after you press Accept in the cookie choice. Page visits and a browser identifier, never document content or signer details.
- **A public time-stamp authority (DigiCert by default)**: Trusted timestamp on a signed file. A hash of the document only, never its contents.

## Told before it changes.

Services you connect yourself, such as your own Stripe account, or your own mail server on a self-hosted install, are your choice and are not Docustay sub-processors. When this list changes we update this page and tell workspace owners before the change takes effect.

## Write to us; we read every report.

Found a security problem? Write to security@docustay.app with what you found and how to see it. The same address is in /.well-known/security.txt. Please give us time to fix it before you tell anyone else, and do not read, change or delete other people's data while you test.

A privacy question, or a request about your data: privacy@docustay.app. If a breach affects your workspace, we tell its owners by email and in the product, with what happened, what data and what we have done.

## Questions

**Is there a bug bounty?**

No.

**Do you sell data?**

No.

**Is my data used to train a model?**

No.

**Does Docustay hold a certification?**

No certification of any kind is claimed, and Docustay is not for protected health information yet.

**Can a record be edited?**

Not a signature. Each signature's hash covers the one before it, so a change breaks the chain.

**Does test mode appear?**

Test documents are marked TEST, mailed only to the sender and left out of usage and billing.

**Can I check a signed PDF?**

Yes. Drop it on the verify page. It needs no account.

## The full wording.

- [Privacy policy](/legal/privacy-policy): What we collect and why.
- [Data processing addendum](/legal/dpa): For workspaces that need one.

<!-- https://docustay.app/trust/legal-validity -->
# Is an electronic signature legal?

In the United States, federal and state law generally treat an electronic signature as acceptable for many documents. Here is what the ESIGN Act and UETA look for in plain words, and what a Docustay signature is.

## What makes an electronic signature hold up.

1. **Intent**: A deliberate act to sign
2. **Consent**: Agreed to sign electronically
3. **Association**: Tied to the record
4. **Records**: Kept and reproducible

## Each element, and what is kept.

- **Intent**: The signer opens the document, fills the fields, ticks that they agree to sign electronically, draws or types a signature and presses Finish and sign. The act, its time, address and browser are stored.
- **Consent**: Before the first signature the signer ticks a statement that they agree to receive and sign the document electronically. Its wording and version are stored with the time, address and browser of the acceptance.
- **Statement**: It says the signer can read the whole document first, can keep or print a copy and can ask the sender for a paper copy. If they do not agree they can close the page and nothing is recorded.

- **Attribution**: The invitation goes to the signer's email as a single-use link, optionally with a code. Attribution rests on control of that address and the code.
- **Association**: The signature is placed on the document and the finished file is sealed with a digital signature over the whole file, including the certificate page. A SHA-256 fingerprint is printed on the certificate.
- **Keeping**: The sealed PDF and the audit trail are stored with the workspace. A signed document cannot be deleted one by one; only the owner deleting the whole workspace removes it.
- **Time**: Local time and UTC are printed, and a trusted RFC 3161 timestamp is added when the time service answers.

## The ESIGN Act and UETA, in plain words.

- **What it is**: A US federal law about electronic signatures and records
- **In short**: A signature or record is not denied effect only because it is electronic, for many kinds of document
- **Consumers**: A consumer must agree to electronic records after a disclosure

- **What it is**: A model law that most US states have adopted in some form
- **In short**: The same idea at state level: an electronic signature can satisfy a signature requirement when the people meant to sign
- **Differences**: States differ in the details

## What a Docustay signature is, and when you may need something else.

- **Kind**: A simple electronic signature with a strong evidence record and a tamper-evident seal
- **Check**: Anyone can check a signed copy on the verify page with no account

- **Qualified**: Docustay does not produce qualified electronic signatures
- **Identity**: It does not check identity documents; it rests on control of an email address and any code you share
- **Excluded documents**: Some kinds of document are excluded by law in many places, and Docustay does not decide which
- **The seal**: The sealing certificate is Docustay's own, so some PDF viewers show validity as unknown until told to trust it

## What the signer does, and what we keep.

The signer opens the document, fills the fields, ticks that they agree to sign electronically, draws or types a signature and presses Finish and sign. The act, its time, address and browser are stored.

**Consent.** A disclosure is shown first; its text and version are frozen into the record.

## A certificate page ends every signed copy.

Each person, the time and address of each act, the document's SHA-256 fingerprint and the audit trail.

**Not legal advice.** This is general information about how signing works. It promises no legal outcome.

## Questions

**Is it valid everywhere?**

We do not say that. Rules differ by place and by document. See the figures above.

**Can I check a signed PDF?**

Yes. Drop it on the verify page. It needs no account.

**Is this legal advice?**

No. It is general information about how signing works. It does not promise any legal outcome for any document. If a document matters, ask someone qualified where you are.

# About Docustay

The e-signature API you own. One flat price for every user. Open source and self-hostable. Pro is $35 a month for your whole team: no per-seat fees, unlimited people and documents. Signers can pay while they sign, straight into your own Stripe account, and Pro adds no fee. Docustay sends documents for signature and keeps the proof. We build it, and we read every message. The facts, last checked 12 October 2026, are further down.

## A signing tool with its work shown.

Docustay is a way to send a document, get it signed on any device, and keep the signed copy with a certificate of who signed when.

The code is licensed under the AGPL-3.0. The repository will be public when we publish it, and this site will link to it then.

## With checks.

We write what a page says from a list of things the product does, and the build fails when a page names something that is not on the list.

Every code sample on this site was run before it was published.

## Five promises.

We will not sell your data. We will not read your documents. We will not claim a certification we do not hold. We will not show social proof we do not have. We will not make you talk to a salesperson to see a price.

## What each plan costs.

| Item | Detail |
| --- | --- |
| Free | $0, for one person. 15 documents and 5 new templates a month, and 10 AI drafts a month. API, webhooks and test mode included. |
| Pay as you go | $5 per team member a month. 15 documents a month included, then $0.50 each. 10 AI drafts included, then $0.30 each. |
| Pro | $35 a month, flat for the whole workspace, with unlimited team members, signers, documents and templates. 100 AI drafts a month, then $0.30 each. |
| Lifetime | $299 once, for any workspace. Pro for as long as Docustay runs the hosted service, with 50 AI drafts a month. |
| Your budget | $50 a month unless you change it, with alerts at 50%, 80% and 100%. Sending and AI drafting pause at 100%. |
| Self-host Community | Free under the AGPL-3.0, on your own server. |
| Self-host Pro | $390 per install, for your own business. |
| Commercial licence | From about $3,000 a year, to embed, white-label, resell or keep a private fork. |
| Payments in a document | Docustay adds 2% on Free and Pay as you go and 0% on Pro and Lifetime, on top of Stripe's fees. |

## What the plans allow.

| Item | Detail |
| --- | --- |
| Documents a month | Free: 15, then sending stops. Pay as you go: 15 included, then $0.50 each. Pro and Lifetime: unlimited. A document counts when it is sent. |
| New templates a month | Free: 5. Every other plan and self-hosted installs: no limit. |
| Sending to a list | On every plan. Free sends to up to 15 people at a time. |
| Team members | Free: one, the owner. Pay as you go: $5 per team member a month. Pro and Lifetime: unlimited. |
| Emails a day | Free and Pay as you go: 25. Pro and Lifetime: 500. |

| API | 600 requests a minute for each key. |
| AI drafts a month | Free: 10, then drafting stops. Pay as you go: 10, then $0.30 each. Pro: 100, then $0.30 each. Lifetime: 50, then $0.30 each. A failed or empty draft is never charged. |
| Language | The app, the signing page, the emails and this website are in English. |

| Embedding, white-label, resale, private fork | Needs a commercial licence. |

## How to build on it.

| Item | Detail |
| --- | --- |
| REST API | OpenAPI 3.1 at https://docustay.app/openapi.json, with idempotency keys, key scopes, key expiry, an address allowlist and an API log. |
| SDKs | JavaScript, TypeScript and Python. Clients for Go, PHP and C# are generated from the API description. |
| Command line | Login, send --test, listen, verify and logs. |
| Webhooks | Seven signed document events, replay from the log and secret rotation. |
| Test mode | Test keys send nothing except to the sender, and carry a TEST watermark. |

## What protects a signed document.

| Item | Detail |
| --- | --- |
| Seal | The finished PDF is sealed with a digital signature over the whole file. |
| Certificate | A certificate of completion as the last page: who signed, when, and a hash of the file. |
| Audit log | Every step on a document, with a CSV export. |
| Sign-in | Two-step sign-in with an authenticator app or a passkey, which an owner can require for the whole team. |
| What a signature is | A simple electronic signature with a strong record and a digital seal. No qualified signatures, no identity checks, no legal advice. |
| Certifications | Docustay holds no security certification and claims none. |

# Open source and roadmap

The server and app are AGPL-3.0. The pieces you put inside your own software are MIT.

## Two licences, one line between them.

- **Server**: The API, the signing service and the worker
- **App**: The web app and this site
- **Asks**: Offer your changed version's source to people who use it over a network

- **SDKs**: @docustay2026/sdk and docustay for Python
- **Element**: <docustay-sign> and its React, Vue and Angular wrappers
- **Tools**: The MCP server, the agent skills, the CLI and the OpenAPI file

## Run it free, or pay for the extras.

Self-host Community is free: unlimited documents and templates, everything in the hosted Free plan, on your server. Self-host Pro adds the paid features for one business.

## Keep your copyright.

People who send changes keep their copyright and give the Docustay project a licence to use the change under any licence. That is what lets us offer a commercial licence next to the open one.

## What we are working on.

Passkey sign-in is behind a flag. Single sign-on through OpenID Connect is built for self-hosted installs.

The SDKs are built and tested and will move to the public registries; the changelog will say when.

## Every part and the licence it carries.

| Part | Licence | Where |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Server, worker, migrations, web app, this site | AGPL-3.0-or-later | LICENSE at the top of the repository |
| JavaScript SDK and Python SDK | MIT | sdk/js and sdk/python, each with its own LICENSE |
| The signing element and the React, Vue and Angular wrappers | MIT | sdk/embed, sdk/react, sdk/vue, sdk/angular |
| MCP server, Claude Code plugin, agent skills | MIT | sdk/mcp and sdk/claude-plugin |
| Command line | MIT | sdk/cli |
| OpenAPI file | MIT | sdk/openapi |

Every package carries its own LICENSE file, so a package you install is licensed on its own, wherever you install it from. This is general information, not legal advice.

## Four things a change has to have.

| Step | What happens |
| --- | --- |
| 1. Your agreement | Read the short contributor agreement. You keep your copyright, and you give the project a licence to use your change under any licence. Agree by adding a Signed-off-by line to the commit. |
| 2. A licence header | A new server or app file starts with a one-line SPDX header for the AGPL-3.0-or-later. A new file under sdk starts with the MIT one. |
| 3. A test that fails without it | Every change comes with a test that fails without the change. A test is never weakened to make it pass. Run the site check and the tests for the area you touched. |
| 4. Respect the Documents wall | The Documents code is a separate island. Nothing outside it names its tables or imports its files except through its two doors, and a gate fails on a new crossing. |

## Sign off a commit.

The sign-off line is how you agree to the contributor agreement. git adds it for you with the -s flag.

```
git commit -s -m "Fix the reminder wording"
```

## Welcome as it is, and talk first.

- **Bug fixes**: With a test that fails without the fix.
- **Documentation**: Documentation fixes.
- **Accessibility**: Accessibility fixes.
- **Templates**: New starters written in plain language, with every field placed on its blank.

- **New dependencies**: The licence must be MIT, ISC, BSD, Apache-2.0 or similar, and compatible with the AGPL-3.0.
- **Pricing, plans, limits**: Anything that changes what a plan includes.
- **Signing and sealing**: Anything that touches signing, sealing or the audit trail.
- **Security problems**: Do not open a public issue. Write to security@docustay.app.

## Read it, run it, and know what it sends.

| Point | In short |
| --- | --- |
| Nothing of ours inside | There is no key, certificate or password of ours in the self-hosted release. Every secret is created on your machine the first time it starts. |
| One daily ping | The worker sends one anonymous usage ping a day: a random install id, the version and five counts. Switch it off with DOCUSTAY_TELEMETRY=off. |
| A licence check on your machine | A Pro key is checked against a public key shipped with the install, on your machine, and keeps working up to 30 days offline. |

## Today, said plainly.

| Item | What to know |
| --- | --- |
| The repository | Opens with the self-hosted release. This site links to it then. |
| Packages | The SDKs, the signing element, the CLI and the MCP server are on the public package registries. |
| Single sign-on | OpenID Connect is built for self-hosted installs. |
| Passkeys | Behind a flag, with KEYSTONE_PASSKEYS=1. |
| Certifications | Docustay holds no security certification and claims none. |
| Protected health information | Docustay is not for protected health information yet. |

## The code is open; the name and logo are not.

The licences give you the right to use, change and share the code. They do not give you the right to use the name or the logo. You may say your product works with Docustay, uses the Docustay API or is compatible with it, in plain words, and you may run an unmodified copy and call it Docustay.

If you fork the code, choose your own name and logo, and do not use the name in a company, product, domain or app-store name. A commercial licence can include permission to use the name. This is how the project treats its name; it is not legal advice and not a registered-trademark claim.

## Three addresses for the AGPL-3.0 side.

| What | In short |
| --- | --- |
| Security | security@docustay.app. Include what you found, how to reproduce it and what you think it could do. We reply within three working days and credit you if you want. |
| Conduct | conduct@docustay.app. The code of conduct is short: discuss the work, not the person, and no harassment, personal attacks or sharing other people's private details. |
| Licensing | The contact form, with Licensing chosen, for a commercial licence, a question about the line between the two licences or permission to use the name. |

<!-- https://docustay.app/licensing -->
# Licensing: AGPL or commercial.

Docustay is open source under AGPL-3.0. Most people never need anything else. If AGPL does not fit how you ship, there is a commercial licence. General information, not legal advice.

## Which licence fits?

Self-host Pro is $390 a year per install; a commercial licence is from about $3,000 a year.

## Three ways to use it.

| Item | Detail |
| --- | --- |
| Hosted by us | Free and Pro, used under the Terms. There is no code to license. |
| Run it yourself | Self-host Community is free under the AGPL-3.0. Self-host Pro adds the paid features for your own business, per install. |
| Ship it in a product | A commercial licence covers embedding, white-label, resale and a private fork. |

## What each one asks and gives.

- **Use**: You may run, study, change and share the code
- **Change it**: If you change the code and let others use your version over a network, offer them the source of your version
- **Run it unchanged**: For your own business there is nothing to publish
- **The text**: The LICENSE file is the authority; this is a summary

- **Embed**: Ship Docustay inside a product you sell or offer to others
- **White-label**: Your name and logo
- **Resell**: Offer it to your customers
- **Private fork**: Keep your changes without publishing them

## Using the API is not copying the code.

A customer who calls the Docustay API over HTTP, or uses the SDKs, is not making a derivative work of the server, and their software does not become AGPL. A customer who copies or modifies server code and lets other people use it over a network is, and the AGPL applies to that code. Showing the signing page inside your site in a frame is using a service. The SDKs, the signing element, the MCP server and the CLI are MIT.

## The code is yours to use; the name is not.

“Docustay” and the logo are marks of the Docustay project. The licences give you the right to use the code, not the name or the logo. If you fork the code, choose your own name and logo.

## What you are doing, and what you need.

| You are | Licence you need | Why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Calling the API from your app | None to buy; the API is a service | Your code is not a derivative work of the server. |
| Using the SDKs or the CLI | MIT, nothing to buy | The pieces you put inside your own software carry the MIT licence. |
| Showing the signing page in a frame on your site | None to buy | It is using a service, not copying code. |
| Running Docustay for your own business | AGPL-3.0 (Community, free), or Self-host Pro | One install is one running Docustay with one database. |
| Changing the server code and letting others use it over a network | AGPL-3.0: offer them your version's source | That is what the AGPL asks. |
| Embedding Docustay in a product you offer to others | Commercial licence | Self-host Pro is for your own business only. |
| White-labelling or reselling it | Commercial licence | The name and logo are not covered by the code licences. |
| Keeping a private fork | Commercial licence | The AGPL would otherwise ask you to publish your changes to its users. |

## What counts as an install.

| Item | What to know |
| --- | --- |
| One install | One running Docustay with one database. |
| Staging or backup copy | A staging or backup copy of the same install is not a separate install. |
| Developer's machine | A development copy on a developer's own machine is not a separate install. |
| Two production databases | Two production databases are two installs, and each needs its own Pro key. |
| The key | One key covers one install and renews itself while the subscription is paid. |
| Where the check happens | On your machine, against the public key shipped with the install. |

## From card to running key.

| Step | What happens |
| --- | --- |
| 1. Pay on the Self-host page | Pay by card. When the payment is confirmed, a key is made and emailed once to the address on the payment. Only a fingerprint is kept, so it cannot be shown again. |
| 2. Add it to .env | Put DOCUSTAY_LICENSE_KEY in .env and run docker compose up -d. The install checks the key itself, on your machine. |
| 3. Renewal runs itself | A successful yearly payment extends the key to the end of the paid year plus 14 days of grace. An install with no route to the internet keeps working up to 30 days. |

## After you cancel.

| Item | What to know |
| --- | --- |
| Self-host Pro ends | The Pro items stop and the install keeps running as Community. Nothing is deleted. |
| Hosted Pro ends | The workspace moves to Free. Documents already sent or signed stay readable and downloadable. |
| Your data | You can export everything at any time. |
| Sending after a hosted cancel | Sending is limited by the Free limits. |

## Questions

**Does Self-host Pro cover embedding?**

No. It is for your own business. Embedding, white-labelling, resale and a private fork need a commercial licence.

**What if our server cannot reach yours?**

A Pro licence key keeps working for up to 30 days offline. It is a commercial honour system, not copy protection.

**Does using the API make my software AGPL?**

No. Calling the API or using the SDKs does not.

**Who owns contributions?**

Contributors keep their copyright and give the Docustay project a licence to use the change under any licence. That is what lets us offer a commercial licence next to the open one.

<!-- https://docustay.app/guides/how-to-sign-a-pdf -->
# How to sign a PDF

Three ways, from the quickest to the one that keeps proof.

## Pick the one that fits.

**Someone sent you a link.** Open it, fill in your fields, type or draw your signature, tick that you agree to sign electronically and finish. You do not need an account.

**You need to sign your own file.** Upload the PDF, place your signature field and sign it yourself, then send it on.

**You need others to sign.** Upload the PDF, name who signs, and send it. Everyone gets the sealed copy with its certificate.

## What a good signed PDF has.

**Every signature.** Each person's name and the time they signed, on the page.

**A seal.** A digital signature over the whole file, so a later change shows.

**A way to check.** Anyone can drop the file on the verify page with no account.

## Which one are you?

**Someone sent you a link.** Open it, fill in your fields, type or draw your signature, tick that you agree and finish.

**You need to sign your own file.** Upload the PDF, place your signature field and sign it yourself, then send it on.

**You need others to sign.** Upload the PDF, name the people, and each of them gets the link by email.

## A good signed PDF is sealed.

When the last person signs, the finished file gets a digital signature over the whole file, so a later change shows.

**Check it.** Anyone can drop the file on the verify page with no account.

## Which way to sign a PDF fits you.

The right one depends on who else has to sign.

**Only you.** Put a picture of your signature on a copy of the file with the free sign a PDF tool. It runs in your browser and the file is never uploaded, so it suits a form that only needs your name.

**You and others.** Upload the PDF, say who signs and in what order, and send it. Each person signs on their own device with no account, and everyone gets the sealed copy.

**From your own software.** If your system already holds the document, send it from code with a template and a list of signers, and hear about the result through a signed webhook.

## The record matters as much as the picture.

A signature image proves very little on its own.

**A seal over the whole file.** The finished PDF is sealed with a digital signature over the whole file, so any later change shows.

**A certificate of completion.** The last page lists who signed and when, the address each act came from, and a hash of the file.

**A check anyone can run.** The verify page checks a signed PDF in the browser with no account, so you can hand it to the other side or an adviser.

## Eight things people ask when a PDF will not cooperate.

Each answer is about what the free tool and the app actually do.

**It is a scan.** A scan is a picture of a page, so you place your signature on top of it like any other page. It works in the free tool and when sending.

**I am on a phone.** Choose the file, draw your signature with a finger and tap the page where it goes. Signers who receive a document sign the same way, with nothing to install.

**The file is large.** The free tool opens files up to 150 MB, because it never uploads them. When sending, uploads are limited to 25 MB on Free and 100 MB on Pro.

**It is not a PDF.** Docustay only accepts PDF files, so save or export a Word or image file as a PDF first. You can also write a document as HTML and make a template from it.

**Several people must sign.** Name each person and choose whether they sign one at a time or all at once. Each box on the page belongs to one person, so nobody fills in someone else's part.

**I need proof later.** Keep the sealed copy with its certificate. The audit log records every step and exports as a CSV if you are ever asked for the history.

**The form needs filling first.** Use the free fill a PDF tool to type into the form's own fields, then add your signature with the sign a PDF tool. Both run in your browser.

**I made a mistake.** Both tools write a new copy and never change the file you chose, so you can go back to the original and start again whenever you like.

## Questions

**Is a typed signature valid?**

It is a simple electronic signature with a record of intent. Whether it is enough for a given document depends on the document and the place. See legal validity.

**Can I sign on my phone?**

Yes. The signing page works on any phone or computer.

**Can I sign a Word file?**

Save it as a PDF first. Docustay only accepts PDF files.


## Keep reading

- [Sign a PDF](/tools/sign-pdf)
- [Signature generator](/tools/signature-generator)
- [Verify a PDF](/verify)
- [Legal validity](/trust/legal-validity)

<!-- https://docustay.app/legal/acceptable-use -->
# Acceptable use

What you may and may not do with Docustay. This text is general information, not legal advice.

## Anything you send or store.

These rules apply to every workspace, signer and API key. They sit beside the terms of service.

## Six things.

Do not use Docustay to send anything unlawful, to deceive a signer about what they are signing, or to forge a signature or an identity.

Do not send spam or bulk email to people who did not expect it.

Do not try to break, probe or overload the service, or reach another workspace's data.

Do not use another person's name or email to sign for them.

Do not upload malware or content you have no right to share.

Do not resell or embed the hosted service without a commercial licence.

## A warning first, when we can.

If a rule is broken we may pause a send, remove content, or end the account. Where we can, we say why first. To report a problem, write to abuse@docustay.app.

## Told before they apply.

When these rules change we update this page, and tell workspace owners when the change matters to them.

## Everyone who sends, signs or builds on Docustay.

These rules cover three kinds of people. Senders use Docustay to send documents. Signers receive them and never need an account. Developers call the API, the SDKs, the command line, the webhooks or the MCP server with a key. The rules for one group sit beside the rules for the others, and a sender is responsible for what their documents, emails and integrations do.

The short version: send things people expect, say truthfully what they are signing, keep the people you send to safe from tricks and spam, and do not use the service to harm it or anyone else. The rest of this page explains what that means in practice and what happens when a rule is broken.

## Content and purposes that are not allowed.

You may not use Docustay to create, send, store or collect anything that is unlawful where you or the signer are, or that you have no right to share. In particular:

## Not for protected health information yet.

Docustay is not for protected health information yet. Do not use a workspace, a form or an upload to collect or store it, and do not describe your use of Docustay to your own customers as suitable for it. If you are unsure whether a document counts, leave it out of Docustay until we say the product is ready for it.

## A signer should know what is happening and who is asking.

The person you send a document to is trusting an email from you. Keep that trust: use your own real name or organisation as the sender, say in the message what the document is, and give a way to reach you. Docustay lets a signer decline and records the steps of each document in an audit log; do not work around either.

Do not pressure people with false deadlines, and do not set an expiry that is meant to catch someone out. Do not ask a signer to sign a blank document or one with fields left open to be filled in later without their knowledge. If a signer declines, or says they did not expect the document, stop sending to them.

A signed document is a record. Do not void or replace a document to hide that it was signed, and do not ask Docustay to remove a signed record to deceive someone.

## Only to people who should receive it.

Docustay sends email only about a document your workspace made, to the people named on it. You may not add people to a document in order to send them something else, use the message field for advertising, or send to a list of addresses you bought or scraped.

Sending pauses on its own for a workspace when about 2 percent of its recent email bounces or about 0.05 percent is reported as spam, once at least 50 emails have gone out in 30 days. This protects your domain's name and ours. If it happens, look at the email log under Developers, remove the addresses that bounced, and write to us at abuse@docustay.app to restart sending. Do not respond by creating new workspaces to continue the same list.

A self-hosted install that sends from its own domain or mail server is also responsible for that domain's reputation and for keeping its records correct.

## Do not break it, probe it or get around it.

You may not try to reach another workspace's data, test the service for weaknesses on live customers' documents, overload it, or use it to attack anything else. You may not reverse-engineer the hosted service, or use automation to create accounts, bypass the bot check on the sign-up page, or avoid a plan limit by spreading one organisation's use over many free workspaces.

Limits exist so that one customer cannot harm the others: each API key may make 600 requests a minute, a request body to the API is limited to 1 MB, and uploaded files are limited by plan. When you meet a limit the API answers with a clear status and a retry time; wait and retry rather than opening more keys. The sign-in, public signing, download and verification pages are also limited per address.

If you find a weakness, please report it to security@docustay.app rather than using it. Reporting in good faith, without reading other customers' data or disrupting the service, is welcome.

## Your key is your responsibility.

A key can do what its scopes allow, so give each integration only the scopes it needs, keep keys out of public code and pages, set an expiry and an address allowlist where you can, and revoke a key you think has leaked. Do not share a key between unrelated organisations or sell access to one.

Use a test key for practice. A document made with a test key is emailed only to the sender and carries a TEST watermark; do not use test documents as real agreements, and do not use test mode to avoid the limits that apply to live use.

Webhook receivers must verify the signature on every delivery. If you build a service on Docustay for other organisations, you remain responsible for how it is used.

## A person stays in charge.

Scribe and Find fields with AI send the text or page pictures of a document to an AI model, only when someone uses the feature and only for that request. Do not use them to produce content that breaks these rules, to impersonate another person, or on documents you have no right to process.

An agent that acts through a key should use a draft-only key. With one, a request to send files an approval that a person decides in the app, and nothing is emailed until they approve. Do not build an agent that tries to get around that step, hides what it is doing from the person approving, or retries after a refusal or a rate-limit answer.

## A warning first, when we can give one.

We may take the smallest step that stops the problem. Depending on what happened, that can be: pausing a send, revoking a key, removing a document or a link, limiting a workspace, or ending the account. Where it is safe to do so we say what rule was broken and what to change, and we give you a chance to fix it. For serious or repeated cases, or where there is risk to a signer, to other customers or to the service, we may act first and explain afterwards.

We do not remove a signed document because a rule was broken. A record of what was signed stays what it is, and the Privacy Policy and Terms say how workspace data is exported and deleted if an account ends.

If you think we made a mistake, write to abuse@docustay.app with the workspace name and what you were doing, and we will look again.

## How to tell us.

If you received a document that looks like fraud or harassment, do not sign it, and write to abuse@docustay.app with the email you received and, if you have it, the document link. Do not forward the signing link to others, since it is meant for you. If you think someone is in danger, contact your local emergency services first.

For anything about your own information, see the Privacy Policy. For a security weakness, write to security@docustay.app.

## Plain language, not legal advice.

This page states the rules for using Docustay and describes what the product does when they are broken. It is general information and not legal advice, and it does not promise any particular legal outcome. It sits beside the Terms of Service, which govern in the same way for hosted use. Self-hosted installs run the AGPL-3.0 code under its licence, and the operator of an install sets the rules for their own users.

# What is next for Docustay.

Version 1 does one thing well: it gets your documents written, sent, signed and sealed, and it gives developers and self-hosters the whole platform. Here is what we are looking at for later versions. Nothing here is promised or dated; tell us what you would use first.

## Thirteen ideas. Five are next up.

**Reports.** Next up. See and export what was sent, signed and paid.

**Sign in person.** Next up. Kiosk mode and QR codes.

**Your own email domain.** Next up. Email from your own address.

**Public forms.** Next up. Share a link anyone can fill in and sign.

**Edit email wording.** Next up. Change the words of the emails Docustay sends for you.

**Automations.** Send the next document automatically when one is signed.

**More languages.** Signing pages, emails and certificates in other languages.

**Contract dates.** Key dates and renewal reminders.

**Smart fields.** Fields that appear on conditions, calculated fields and sections.

**Signing links on your domain.** Signers open links that carry your name.

**Payment plans.** Instalments and subscriptions inside a signed document.

**Custom roles and permissions.** Roles beyond owner, admin and member.

**Connections.** Cloud storage, calendars and chat apps.

## What you tell us decides the order.

We build what people use. Every message to hello@docustay.app is read, and the ideas that come up most often move up.

**Are these promised?**

No. Nothing on this page is promised or dated. It is a list of what we are looking at.

**Can I ask for something that is not here?**

Yes. Write to hello@docustay.app and say what you would use it for.

**Is anything here in the product today?**

No. Everything listed is not part of version 1.

<!-- https://docustay.app/help -->
# Help, in plain words.

How to send and sign, how plans and bills work, how to take payments, and who to write to when this is not enough.

## Four steps to your first signed document.

**Make an account.** Enter your email, then the code we send you. There is no card to give and nothing to install.

**Pick or write a document.** Start from one of 54 templates, upload a PDF, or tell Scribe what you need. Scribe drafts it; you read it.

**Say who signs and send.** Add names and emails, choose the order and press send. A document counts when it is sent.

**Keep the sealed copy.** Everyone gets the sealed PDF with its certificate. Anyone can check a copy on the verify page.

## What happens after you press send.

**Reminders.** Reminders go out until each person signs, on every plan. Reminders are never charged.

**Sending to a list.** Upload a spreadsheet and each row gets its own copy. Free sends to up to 15 at a time.

**Signing.** The signer opens the link on a phone or a computer and signs. No account, no app.

## What you pay, and how to keep it in check.

**What counts.** A document counts when it is sent. Reminders, drafts, signers and test mode never count. Free includes 15 a month.

**Your budget.** $50 a month unless you change it. You get an email at 50%, 80% and 100%. At 100% sending and AI drafting pause until you raise it. Nothing is deleted.

**Cancel any time.** Cancel from the Billing page. Your plan stays on until the end of the period you paid for. Docustay does not give refunds.

## Take money as part of signing.

**Set up payments.** In Billing, Payments, choose Set up payments and Stripe creates an account in your name, or choose I already have Stripe and sign in to the one you use.

**What it costs.** Stripe's own fees go to Stripe. Docustay adds 2% on Free and Pay as you go and 0% on Pro and Lifetime.

**Refunds are yours.** Refunds and disputes are handled in your own Stripe account. Docustay never holds the money.

## Make it yours, and add the people who send.

**Logo and colour.** Add your logo, colour, welcome note, sender name and reply-to address under Settings, Branding. It is on every plan.

**Team members.** Free is for one team member. On Pay as you go each team member you add is $5 a month; Pro and Lifetime have unlimited team members. Signers are free on every plan.

**Roles.** Owner, admin and member roles decide who can send and who can change settings.

## Questions

**A signer did not get the email**

Ask them to check their spam folder, then open the document and send a reminder. A reminder is free. If the address was wrong, void the document and send it again to the right one.

**Sending says it is paused**

Your monthly budget has been reached, or the Free limit of 15 documents has. Open Billing: raise the budget, or switch to Pay as you go. Nothing is lost.

**I need my documents out of Docustay**

Open any document and download the sealed PDF and its audit log. You can export everything at any time, also after you cancel.

**Is a signature from Docustay legal?**

It is a simple electronic signature with a strong record and a digital seal. Whether it is enough depends on the document and the place. Read the legal validity page.

**I forgot how I signed in**

Docustay signs you in with an emailed code, a passkey or a password. Choose Sign in and ask for a code.

**I need a person**

Write to hello@docustay.app, or support@docustay.app if something is broken. Include what you did and what you saw. We read every message.

<!-- https://docustay.app/features/payments -->
# Get paid inside the signature.

Add a payment field to a document. The signer signs, then pays by card on the same page. Payments are powered by Stripe, and the money goes straight to your own Stripe account. Docustay never holds it.

## From the signer to your Stripe account.

1. **Signer**: Signs, then pays by card
2. **Docustay**: Works out the amount on the server
3. **Your Stripe account**: Takes the money

## Start from nothing, or bring your Stripe account.

Only Admins and Owners set up payments. It is under Billing, Payments.

- **Stripe account**: You do not need one. Stripe makes it for you at the end.
- **The form**: Company or individual, your name, what you will collect for, and your country. The form shows United States.
- **Then**: Stripe's own secure page asks for the rest.
- **You need**: A photo ID, a bank account, and an EIN or the last 4 of an SSN.
- **How long**: Setup takes about 5 minutes. You can stop and come back.
- **Privacy**: Docustay never sees your ID or your bank details.

- **Choose**: I already have a Stripe account. Connect it instead.
- **What happens**: You sign in at Stripe and allow Docustay to take payments for you.
- **Your money**: Stays in the account you already use.
- **Your dashboard**: The same Stripe dashboard you know.

## Six states, and what each one means.

| State | What it means | What you do |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Ready | Stripe is connected and can take payments. | Nothing. |
| Verifying | Stripe is checking your details. It usually takes a few minutes and sometimes up to a day. | Wait. Stripe emails you when it is done. |
| Needs attention | Stripe needs a little more from you. It shows a deadline when it has one. | Choose Continue on Stripe. |
| Restricted | Stripe has restricted the account until it has what it asked for. | Choose Continue on Stripe. |
| Paused by you | You turned Take payments off. Payment boxes say payments are paused and people can still sign. Nothing is refunded. | Turn it back on whenever you like. |
| Disconnected | Docustay no longer has access to a Stripe account. Payment boxes cannot be paid until you connect again. | Reconnect. Your Stripe account stays yours. |

## Pause it, disconnect it, open your dashboard.

**Pause payments.** Payment boxes say payments are paused, and people can still sign. Nothing is refunded. Turn it back on when you want.

**Disconnect.** The Stripe account stays yours. Payment boxes cannot be paid until you connect again, and your history stays visible.

**Open your Stripe dashboard.** One link from Billing, Payments takes you to your own Stripe dashboard, where payouts and the bank details live.

## One amount, one currency, one card payment.

| You set | Options |
| --- | --- |
| Amount | One fixed amount, from 0.50 to 999,999.99. A deposit is just a smaller amount. |
| Currency | USD, EUR, GBP, CAD, AUD, NZD, CHF, SEK, NOK or DKK. |
| Who pays | One of the people on the document. |
| What it is for | A line of text the signer sees next to the amount. |
| A Stripe Price or Payment Link | Instead of typing an amount, point the field at a one-time Price or a Payment Link on your own Stripe account. |
| Instalments | Write them in the document as a note. They are a note, not a charge: the field takes one payment. |

## They sign, then pay on the same page.

The link opens on any device, with no account. The signer signs, then pays by card as the last step. The amount is worked out on the server and never taken from the browser.

**Held for 7 days.** Their signature is held for 7 days while they pay. If the payment does not arrive in time, the signature is not kept, and you and the signer are told.

**The receipt.** The receipt comes with the signed copy. If your Stripe account already emails receipts, signers may get two.

## Every payment in one place.

Billing, Payments shows your balance and payouts, who paid for which document, Stripe's fees, and this month's money in, fees and refunds.

- Refund in full or in part, with a reason the payer sees.
- A dispute opens in Stripe, where you answer it.
- Owners get an email when Stripe asks for more information, when a payout fails and when a payment is disputed.
- Switch on Payments in your notification settings to hear when a payment arrives or one does not go through, in the app and by email.

- **Free and Pay as you go**: 2% fee on top of Stripe's
- **Pro and Lifetime**: 0% fee on top of Stripe's
- **Stripe's own fees**: Go to Stripe, from your Stripe account

## Say what you are collecting. Review what Scribe drafts.

Once Stripe is connected, Scribe's wizard asks for the amount, the currency, who pays and what it is for. The terms are written around your values, and you review everything before it is sent.

- Scribe never decides an amount. The one you typed is the one that is charged.

## The demo has no Stripe. Test mode does.

**The demo.** The demo has no Stripe account, so it cannot take a payment. You can still see a payment box in a document.

**With a test card.** Where a server is in Stripe's test mode, Docustay says so, and a Stripe test card pays without moving real money.

**For developers.** The technical side: the API, webhooks, the command line and test mode.

## Questions

**Does Docustay hold my money?**

No. The payment goes to your own Stripe account, and Stripe pays your bank on the schedule you see in Billing, Payments.

**What does it cost?**

Stripe's own fees go to Stripe. Docustay adds 2% on Free and Pay as you go and 0% on Pro and Lifetime.

**Which countries can set up payments?**

The guided setup makes a United States Stripe account, and its form shows United States. If you already have a Stripe account, you can connect it instead. A payment can be in USD, EUR, GBP, CAD, AUD, NZD, CHF, SEK, NOK or DKK.

**What if Stripe needs more information?**

The state changes to Needs attention, and Owners get an email. Choose Continue on Stripe and give it what it asks for.

**Can I take a deposit?**

Yes. A deposit is a payment field with a smaller amount. A payment field takes one amount, so a balance later is a second document or an invoice from your own Stripe.

**Can I refund a payment?**

Yes, in full or in part, from Billing, Payments or the API. Give a reason; the payer sees it.

**What about disputes?**

A dispute opens in Stripe, in your own account, and you answer it there. Owners get an email when one is opened.

**Who can set it up?**

Admins and Owners. Members can see who runs payments.

- [Payments when you self-host](/self-host/payments)
- [Scribe](/features/scribe)
- [Pricing](/pricing)

<!-- https://docustay.app/features/signing -->
# Signing that needs no account.

The person you send to opens a link on a phone or a computer, reads the document, signs and is done. They do not make an account.

## Open the link. Sign. Done.

**Any device.** The link opens in the browser on a phone, a tablet or a computer. Nothing to install and no account to make.

**Draw or type.** A signature is drawn with a finger or a mouse, or typed. Initials and dates are fields on the page.

**Keep going later.** A signer can save their place and come back to the same link.

## Sign, decline, or pass it on.

**Remember my signature.** On the same browser, a signature can be remembered under the signer's name, so the next one takes a tap. A different name on that browser is never offered someone else's.

**Decline.** A person can decline. You can ask them to say why, and you are told at once. The decline is part of the record.

**Pass it to someone else.** A signer who is not the right person can pass the document to another name and email.

**A reason for signing.** You can ask each signer to say why they are signing, for example their role. The reason is kept with the signature.

**Check who is signing.** Ask for an email code or an access code you share before the document opens.

**Payment, if you added one.** If the document has a payment field, the signer pays as the last step.

## Reminders and a deadline.

| You choose | Options |
| --- | --- |
| Reminders | None; after 3 and 7 days; every week for three weeks; every day for three days; or after 2, 5 and 10 days. |
| Expiry | Never, or in 7, 14, 30, 60 or 90 days. The sender is told when a document lapses unsigned. |
| Stopping | Reminders stop once everyone has signed. A reminder is never charged. |

## Questions

**Does the signer need an account?**

No. They need the link, and an email code or access code if you asked for one.

**Can a signer decline?**

Yes. They can decline and say why, and you are told at once.

**Can I remind someone by hand?**

Yes. Open the document and send a reminder. Reminders are free.

**What proves who signed?**

Every signed copy carries a certificate with the record of each signature. See Proof.

- [Templates and sending](/features/templates-and-sending)
- [Proof](/features/proof)
- [How it works](/features/how-it-works)

<!-- https://docustay.app/features/templates-and-sending -->
# Make a template once. Send it as often as you like.

Put fields in with a text tag or let Docustay find them. Keep the result as a template, send it to one person or a list, and choose the order, the reminders and the deadline.

## A field is a line of text.

Write the field where it belongs. The first part is its name; the rest are key=value pairs.

```
{{Buyer signature;type=signature;role=Buyer}}
```

## Upload a PDF. Press Find fields.

Uploading never places boxes by itself. Press Find fields and Docustay reads the page the way a person would, then proposes signature lines, dates, initials and text lines. Nothing is placed until you accept it.

- A scanned page is read by character recognition on the server, in English.
- The optional Find fields with AI button is shown only where AI is turned on.

## A library, your own templates, or a sentence.

**The template library.** More than 50 free templates, from an NDA to a lease addendum. Make your own copy and change it.

**Your templates.** Keep a document as a template with its people and fields in place. Send it again with one click or one API call.

**Scribe.** Describe the document in plain words and review what Scribe builds.

## One person, many people, in order or all at once.

**Send to a list.** Upload a spreadsheet and each row gets its own copy and its own signed record. Free sends to up to 15 at a time.

**Signing order.** Name each person and choose whether they sign one at a time or all at once. Each box belongs to one person.

**Reminders and expiry.** Pick when reminders go out and when the document expires. Reminders stop once everyone has signed.

## Questions

**Do I have to use text tags?**

No. You can place boxes by hand in the editor, or press Find fields. Tags are for when you write the document yourself or send it from code.

**Can the sender fill in a box before sending?**

Yes. A box marked filled by sender is answered before you send, and the signer sees the answer and cannot change it.

**Is sending to a list on every plan?**

Yes. Free sends to up to 15 at a time.

- [Signing](/features/signing)
- [Scribe](/features/scribe)
- [Free templates](/free-templates)

<!-- https://docustay.app/features/team-and-roles -->
# Give people the right access.

A workspace has three roles. You invite people, put them in teams, and the price is simple: Pay as you go is per person, and Pro is one price for the whole workspace.

## Owner, Admin, Member.

| Role | What it can do |
| --- | --- |
| Owner | Everything, including deleting the workspace and resetting a teammate's two-step sign-in. An Owner can make someone else an Owner. |
| Admin | Everything except deleting the workspace and resetting a teammate's two-step. Admins set up and manage payments. |
| Member | Makes, sends and tracks their own documents, and uses the templates and plays that are switched on. |

## Invite, group, change a role.

**Invites.** Invite a person by email and choose their role. You can change a role later or remove the person.

**Organise into teams.** Put people into teams so a team sees its own documents.

**Sign-in.** An Owner can require two-step sign-in for the whole team.

- **Free**: One person, the Owner
- **Pay as you go**: $5 per team member a month
- **Pro**: One price for the whole workspace, with unlimited team members

## Questions

**Do signers count as team members?**

No. A signer is anyone you send to, and signers are free on every plan.

**Is Pro really one price for everyone?**

Yes. Pro is one price for the whole workspace, with unlimited team members, signers and documents.

**Who can set up payments?**

Admins and Owners.

<!-- https://docustay.app/developers/payments -->
# Payments, from code.

Read the state of Stripe, list the payments taken through documents and refund them. Three events tell you when a payment arrives, fails or runs out of time.

## GET /api/v1/payments/status

Answers whether payments can be taken now. A document with a payment field can only be sent when it is connected.

```
curl https://app.docustay.app/api/v1/payments/status \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $DOCUSTAY_API_KEY"
```

## GET /api/v1/payments

Payments taken through documents, newest first: who paid, for which document, the amount and the status (paid, waiting, started, refunded, partially_refunded or disputed), and this month's figures. Page with before and limit.

```
curl "https://app.docustay.app/api/v1/payments?limit=20" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $DOCUSTAY_API_KEY"
```

## A payment, as GET /api/v1/documents/{id} shows it.

Each payment on a document carries its status, the amount in the smallest unit of its currency, the Stripe receipt, what was refunded and the Docustay fee.

```
{ "id": "6f1c1f0e-7a0c-4d1d-9b5e-2f0a7b1c3d4e",
  "fieldId": null,
  "person": "Rosa Alvarez",
  "status": "partially_refunded",
  "amountMinor": 15000,
  "currency": "usd",
  "paidAt": "2026-10-26T17:04:11Z",
  "receiptUrl": "https://pay.stripe.com/receipts/…",
  "refundedMinor": 500,
  "fee": { "basisPoints": 200, "amountMinor": 300, "refundedMinor": 10, "plan": "docustay_free" },
  "test": false }
```

## What a key needs.

| Operation | Scope |
| --- | --- |
| GET /api/v1/payments/status | account:read |
| GET /api/v1/payments | documents:read |
| POST /api/v1/payments/{id}/refund | documents:write |

## POST /api/v1/payments/{id}/refund

Refund in full or in part. The reason is required, and the payer sees it. Leave out amountMinor to refund the rest. Needs an Idempotency-Key.

```
curl -X POST "https://app.docustay.app/api/v1/payments/$DOCUSTAY_PAYMENT_ID/refund" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $DOCUSTAY_API_KEY" \
  -H "Idempotency-Key: $(uuidgen)" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{ "amountMinor": 500, "reason": "Charged twice" }'
```

## Three payment events.

| Event | Means |
| --- | --- |
| documents.payment.received | A payment arrived. |
| documents.payment.failed | A payment attempt failed. |
| documents.payment.hold_lapsed | A payment hold ran out before the signer paid. |

## docustay payments

**list.** Lists the payments taken while signing.

**refund.** Refunds one payment. It moves money, so it asks you to confirm, or you add --yes.

## An MCP tool, and test mode.

**MCP.** The get_payments_status tool reports whether Stripe is ready. It needs the account:read scope.

**Test mode.** A seat with a payment field cannot be test-signed. Pay it with a Stripe test card.

**Fees.** Each payment carries the Docustay fee decided when it started: 200 basis points on Free, 0 on Pro. Stripe's fees are separate.

## Questions

**Can the API set up Stripe?**

No. Setup is in the app, under Billing, Payments, by an Admin or Owner. The API reads the state.

**Does a payment field work from the send call?**

Yes, when the template has one and Stripe is connected. The amount is worked out on the server.

- [Payments for businesses](/features/payments)
- [Payments when you self-host](/self-host/payments)
- [Webhooks](/developers/webhooks)
- [Test mode](/developers/test-mode)

<!-- https://docustay.app/self-host/payments -->
# Payments on your own server.

Put your own Stripe keys in the settings file and payment fields work. The money goes to your Stripe account, and no Docustay fee applies to it.

## Four settings for payments.

| Setting | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| KEYSTONE_STRIPE_SECRET_KEY | Your own Stripe secret key. Needed for payment fields. |
| KEYSTONE_STRIPE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY | The matching publishable key. With it the signer pays inside the signing page; without it, on Stripe's own page, and comes back. |
| KEYSTONE_STRIPE_CHARGES_ENABLED | Off by default. Live charges are refused until it is on. |
| KEYSTONE_ENVIRONMENT | Set to staging and the server refuses live Stripe keys. |

## What is and is not the same.

**No Docustay fee.** A self-hosted install has no Docustay plan, so no Docustay fee is added to a payment. Stripe's own fees still apply.

**No guided setup.** The hosted Set up payments and Stripe connect pages are not available. The app says Connecting is not switched on for this server yet. You use your own keys.

**Every payment is checked.** A payment counts only when Stripe says it is paid. Docustay reads it back from Stripe before it records it.

## Questions

**Does Docustay trust the browser about a payment?**

No. When the payer comes back to the signing page, Docustay asks Stripe whether the payment was made and records it only if Stripe says it was paid.

**How do I try it without real money?**

Use Stripe test keys. The app then says the server is in Stripe's test mode, and a Stripe test card pays without moving real money.

**Can I use live keys on a staging server?**

No. With KEYSTONE_ENVIRONMENT set to staging, live Stripe keys are refused.


## Keep reading

- [Payments for businesses](/features/payments)
- [Payments for developers](/developers/payments)
- [Install and run](/self-host)

<!-- https://docustay.app/templates/nda-template -->
# NDA template

Two sides share private information and each agrees to protect the other’s: what counts, what they may do with it, how long it lasts.

Use it before you share plans, prices, code or client names with someone you may work with. It runs both ways, so each side is bound by the same promise.

## Who signs

- Party A
- Party B

## Before you send

- Name what counts as confidential, in your own words.
- Set how long the promise lasts.
- Check the state whose law should apply.

## The facts

- 3 pages
- 25 fields
- About 8 minutes to fill in

---

# Offer letter template

A full offer of employment: role, start date, pay, hours, benefits, conditions, notice and confidentiality, accepted by signing.

Use it when you have chosen someone and want their yes on paper. It states what you are offering and asks for one signature to accept.

## Who signs

- Employer
- Candidate

## Before you send

- Fill in pay, hours and start date exactly.
- Say whether the offer depends on a background check.
- Set an expiry so the offer cannot be accepted months later.

## The facts

- 3 pages
- 26 fields
- About 10 minutes to fill in

- Contractor

- State the rate and when it is paid.
- Check whether your state treats this person as a contractor.

## The facts

- 4 pages
- 31 fields
- About 10 minutes to fill in

# Appointment request

Request an appointment: the service, preferred dates and times, how to reach you and anything to prepare.

Collect appointment requests with real choices, then confirm a time.

## About you

- Full name (text)
- Email (email)
- Phone (phone, optional)

## Your appointment

- Service or reason (text)
- First choice of date (text)
- Second choice of date (text, optional)
- Preferred time (choice)
- In person or online (choice)
- Notes (text, optional)

## Before your visit

- I will let you know as soon as I can if I need to change or cancel. (tick box)
- I understand that what I enter here is stored by the organization that published this form and used only for the purpose (tick box)

## Signature

- Visitor signature (signature)
- Visitor date signed (date signed)

# Room or facility booking request

Request a room or facility: date and times, the purpose, the number of people, the layout and equipment, and agreement to the house rules.

Receive complete booking requests and approve them with a signature.

- Full name (text)
- Email (email)
- Phone (phone, optional)

## The booking

- Organization or group (text, optional)
- Room or facility (text)
- Date (text)
- Start time (text)
- End time (text)
- Repeat (choice)
- Purpose (text)
- Number of people (text)
- Layout (choice, optional)
- Equipment (choose any, optional)
- I will follow the house rules, leave the space as I found it, and pay for any damage my group causes. (tick box)

## Signature

- Requester signature (signature)
- Requester date signed (date signed)

## For facilities use

- Note (text, optional)
- Facilities signature (signature)
- Facilities date signed (date signed)

Collect ideas with enough detail to act on them.

- Who it helps (choose any, optional)
- Effort (choice, optional)
- Supporting file (file (PDF or picture), optional)

## Next steps

- I would like to help make this happen. (tick box, optional)
- The organization may use, change and share this idea without paying me. (tick box)

## Signature

- Contributor date signed (date signed)

# Vehicle inspection checklist

A pre- or post-use check of a vehicle: mileage, fuel, lights, tires, fluids, damage, with photos and a supervisor's sign-off.

Record each check the same way, with evidence, before a vehicle goes out.

## The vehicle and driver

- Driver's name (text)
- Email (email)
- Vehicle (text)
- Check type (choice)
- Odometer reading (text)
- Fuel or charge (choice)

## The check

- Lights (choice)
- Tires (choice)
- Brakes (choice)
- Mirrors and windows (choice)
- Fluids and warning lights (choice)
- Seat belts (choice)
- Safety kit (choice)
- Damage or problems (text, optional)
- Photos (file (PDF or picture), optional)
- To the best of my knowledge the answers above are correct, and I have reported every problem I found. (tick box)

## Signature

- Driver signature (signature)
- Driver date signed (date signed)

## For supervisor use

- Decision (choice)
- Note (text, optional)
- Supervisor signature (signature)
- Supervisor date signed (date signed)

<!-- https://docustay.app/pricing -->
# Pricing

Start free. Pay as you go is $5 per person a month if you only send a few. Pro is $35 a month for your whole team, with no seats. Every price is on this page, and a monthly budget means the bill never surprises you.

- **Free**: 15 documents a month, 10 AI drafts, 5 new templates a month, 15 different signers a month, one team member. A 2% fee on payments taken while signing.
- **Pay as you go**: $5 per team member per month, signers free. 25 new templates a month. 15 documents free, then $0.50 each. 10 AI drafts free, then $0.30 each. Budget of $50 by default with alerts at 50, 80 and 100%.
- **Pro**: $35 a month for the whole workspace, unlimited team members, signers, documents and templates, 100 AI drafts a month, your own Plays and no fee on payments.
- **Lifetime**: $299 once, for any workspace. Unlimited documents, 50 AI drafts a month and everything in Pro, for as long as Docustay runs the hosted service.
- **Self-host**: free under the AGPL-3.0. Self-host Pro is $390 a year per install, for your own business.
- **Commercial licence**: from about $3,000 a year, to embed, white-label, resell or keep a private fork.

See [licensing](/licensing) and [self-host](/self-host).
