<!-- https://docustay.app/verify -->
# Verify a signed PDF

Drop a signed PDF into the page. The check runs in your browser and the file is not uploaded. It reads the seal and the fingerprint from the file and says whether it is intact.

---

<!-- https://docustay.app/tools/sign-pdf -->
# Sign a PDF

Add your signature, initials, a date or text to a PDF. It happens in your browser and the file is never uploaded.

---

<!-- https://docustay.app/tools/fill-pdf -->
# Fill a PDF

Type into the fields of a PDF form, or add text, check marks and dates to any PDF. It happens in your browser and the file is never uploaded.

---

<!-- https://docustay.app/tools/signature-generator -->
# Signature generator

Draw or type a signature and save it as an image. It is made in your browser and nothing is uploaded.

<!-- https://docustay.app/changelog -->
# Changelog

## Version 0.2.2: Pro at $35, packages and the public repository (October 2026)

- Pro is $35 a month for the whole workspace: unlimited team members, signers, documents and templates.
- Every package is at 0.2.2: the SDK, embed, React, Vue, Angular, MCP server and CLI on npm, Python on PyPI, PHP on Packagist, C# on NuGet and Go. The SDKs, the signing element, the MCP server and the CLI are MIT; the server and app are AGPL-3.0.
- The public repository starts fresh at v0.2.2, with images built by its release workflow and scanned for known vulnerabilities before they are published.
- Known issues: the demo workspace opens with one sample document instead of three and no sample forms; the Choose stop reminders control in the signer's view is not covered by a test yet; a self-host builder or Scribe embed answers 409 until the workspace lists its website under Settings, Developers, Embedding; under very heavy load, reminder and schedule sweeps wait behind email and webhook deliveries.

## Pricing in plain words (October 2026)

- Two words now cover everyone: a team member has a Docustay login and is the only person who ever costs money (Pay as you go, $5 each a month); a signer is anyone you send to, and signers are free.
- Free includes 15 different signers a month and Pay as you go 25 new templates a month, from 1 November 2026. Sending again to someone you already sent to never counts, and a workspace already past either number keeps everything it has.
- People in the app is now Contacts, and a signing group shares one signing spot. No price changed.

## Version 1: simpler, and pay for what you use (October 2026)

- New plans: Free, Pay as you go ($5 per team member a month, then $0.50 a document after 15 and $0.30 an AI draft after 10), Pro and a one-time Lifetime offer. Set a budget (default $50), get alerts at 50, 80 and 100%, and sending pauses at the budget. Documents are never deleted.
- Scribe now uses one model and shows the price of a draft before it runs. A failed or empty draft is never charged.
- Signing documents is the whole product again. Removed: forms with public links, automations, contract key dates, reports, the kiosk and QR sign-in, your own signing domain and mailbox, editable email wording, the translated signing pages, conditional fields and formulas, and recurring payments. Your documents and signed copies are untouched.
- Payments inside signing take one fixed amount. Connect an existing Stripe account with a sign-in, or create one.
- The API is twelve scopes and 61 operations; webhooks gain documents.usage.threshold. Templates and former form templates are now one library of ready-made templates.

## Self-hosting: rebuild your images (October 2026)

- Images built from this repository before this version contained the install's .env file (its master key, sign-in secret and database password). Upgrade as usual (git pull, docker compose build, docker compose up -d), then delete the old images with docker image prune. If you ever pushed or copied an image you built, treat the secrets in that .env as known to whoever has the image.
- An install that sends through its own mail server or a connected mailbox now gets its notices (someone signed, everyone has signed), which were skipped before.
- A fresh install says plainly that email is not set up on the Email settings and the Check step, before you press Send.

## Payments inside a document (October 2026)

- Add a payment field and the signer pays through Stripe's hosted page, to the Stripe account you connect. The amount can be fixed, typed by the signer, a formula, a Stripe price or a payment link.
- Docustay charges 2% on the Free plan and nothing on Pro, on top of Stripe's own fees.

## A new look and a board for your documents (October 2026)

- Paper-and-ink design with a dark mode.
- Documents as a board of three lanes, with the list still one click away.
- Settings grouped by purpose; a developer console with API keys, webhooks with a delivery log and replay, and an embedding snippet builder.
- A signing page built for the phone first.

## Developers (October 2026)

- A complete OpenAPI 3.1 file and a Postman collection.
- Embedded signing, text tags, HTML to template, test keys and test mode.
- A Model Context Protocol server and agent skills.

## Security (October 2026)

- Security headers on every response, two-step sign-in for workspaces that require it, a list of active sessions, and a daily backup of the database to a separate location.

Self-hosted e-signature: the same software as the hosted service, on a machine you control. Licensed under the AGPL-3.0. Community is free. Self-host Pro is $390 a year per install, for your own business. A commercial licence, from about $3,000 a year, covers embedding, white-label and resale.

Three commands: `cd docustay`, `./init.sh`, `docker compose up -d`, then open http://localhost:8080/setup. A running install idles at about 1 GiB of memory; building the image needs more than 3.8 GB.

<!-- https://docustay.app/legal/refunds -->
# Refunds and cancellation

## Who publishes Docustay

Docustay is a product of GLRS LLC.

## In short

Docustay does not give refunds. You can cancel at any time, and a cancelled paid plan keeps working until the end of the period you have already paid for. Usage up to the day the plan ends is still billed (Pay as you go bills usage at the end of the month), and nothing is charged after that. Lifetime is a single payment and is not refunded either. The one exception to "keeps working until the end of the period" is deleting the whole workspace: the plan then ends at once, the owner is told beforehand how many paid days will be lost, and nothing is refunded or credited.

## How to cancel

A workspace owner opens Billing in the app, chooses Manage plan, and then cancels the plan. The cancellation is set to take effect at the end of the current paid period, not at once.

## Refunds

Docustay does not refund a payment that has been taken, in whole or in part, including for time left in a period you cancelled, for usage that has already happened, and for Lifetime. (When you move up to a higher plan, the unused part of what you paid is credited against the new plan instead, as the Terms describe; that credit is not paid out as cash.) The Free plan costs nothing, so there is nothing to refund on it. The few legal rights a country gives a buyer cannot be removed by this page, and nothing here limits them.

## Payments your signers make

If you collect payments through a payment field, the money goes into your own Stripe account. Refunding a signer is your decision, made through Stripe from your Docustay workspace; Docustay does not refund them on your behalf. See the [Terms](/legal/terms) for the Docustay fee on the Free and Pay as you go plans.

## A note

This page is general information about how billing works. It is not legal advice.

---

<!-- https://docustay.app/legal/renewal -->
# Renewal terms

## Who publishes Docustay

Docustay is a product of GLRS LLC.

## In short

Paid plans renew monthly until you cancel (Lifetime is a one-time payment and does not renew). You are told the price when you subscribe, and you can cancel at any time from Billing.

## Pro, hosted by us

Pro costs $35 a month for the whole workspace, however many people use it. It is billed in advance through Stripe and renews each month.

## Pay as you go

Pay as you go is $5 per team member per month, billed through Stripe and renewed each month, plus usage (documents and AI drafts beyond the included amounts), which is billed at the end of the month. Team members added or removed during a month are charged or credited for the rest of that month. You set a monthly budget; sending and AI drafting pause when it is reached.

## Lifetime

Lifetime is one payment of $299 for one workspace, offered to any workspace. It does not renew. It lasts for as long as Docustay runs the hosted service, and for that whole time it keeps its 0% platform fee on payments collected through payment fields; if we ever stop running it, we will tell you and give you time to export your documents. AI drafts beyond the 50 included each month are billed at the price shown, up to your budget.

## Stopping a renewal

Cancel from Billing, then Manage plan, then cancel. The plan runs to the end of the paid period and does not renew. See [Refunds and cancellation](/legal/refunds).

## Self-host Pro

A self-host Pro licence key is $390 a year per install. The licence terms are on the [Licensing](/licensing) page.

## Price changes

If the price of a plan changes, the new price is shown on the [Pricing](/pricing) page before you subscribe. This page is general information, not legal advice.

<!-- https://docustay.app/sign-pdf/javascript -->
# Send a document for signature from JavaScript

Sign PDF API in JavaScript: a short program that sends a template for signature, run against Docustay with a test key before it was published. Set DOCUSTAY_API_KEY and DOCUSTAY_TEMPLATE_ID.

`npm install @docustay2026/sdk`

The package has no dependencies and needs Node 18 or newer. It makes one Idempotency-Key for each call and reuses it on every retry, so a network retry never sends the document twice. It is an ES module, so use import, or a .mjs file.

```
import { Docustay } from "@docustay2026/sdk";

const docustay = new Docustay(process.env.DOCUSTAY_API_KEY, process.env.DOCUSTAY_URL ? { baseUrl: process.env.DOCUSTAY_URL } : {});
const doc = await docustay.sendDocument({
  templateId: process.env.DOCUSTAY_TEMPLATE_ID,
  parties: [{ seat: "signer_1", name: "Rosa Alvarez", email: "rosa@example.com" }],
});
console.log(doc.id, doc.state);
```

---

<!-- https://docustay.app/sign-pdf/typescript -->
# Send a document for signature from TypeScript

Sign PDF API in TypeScript: a short program that sends a template for signature, run against Docustay with a test key before it was published. Set DOCUSTAY_API_KEY and DOCUSTAY_TEMPLATE_ID.

`npm install @docustay2026/sdk`

The types ship inside the package: SendRequest describes what you send and the answer is typed too, so a wrong field name fails in your editor and not at 2 a.m. The program runs as it stands on Node 22 and newer with --experimental-strip-types; elsewhere compile it with tsc as usual.

```
import { Docustay, type SendRequest } from "@docustay2026/sdk";

const docustay = new Docustay(process.env.DOCUSTAY_API_KEY!, process.env.DOCUSTAY_URL ? { baseUrl: process.env.DOCUSTAY_URL } : {});
const request: SendRequest = {
  templateId: process.env.DOCUSTAY_TEMPLATE_ID!,
  parties: [{ seat: "signer_1", name: "Rosa Alvarez", email: "rosa@example.com" }],
};
const doc = await docustay.sendDocument(request);
console.log(doc.id, doc.state);
```

<!-- https://docustay.app/sign-pdf/python -->
# Send a document for signature from Python

Sign PDF API in Python: a short program that sends a template for signature, run against Docustay with a test key before it was published. Set DOCUSTAY_API_KEY and DOCUSTAY_TEMPLATE_ID.

`pip install docustay`

The package has no dependencies and needs Python 3.9 or newer. Calls are synchronous and return plain dictionaries. Every POST gets an idempotency key made for it and reused on retries. Pass base_url only when you point at a self-hosted install.

```
import os
from docustay import Docustay

kw = {"base_url": os.environ["DOCUSTAY_URL"]} if os.environ.get("DOCUSTAY_URL") else {}
docustay = Docustay(os.environ["DOCUSTAY_API_KEY"], **kw)
doc = docustay.send_document(
    os.environ["DOCUSTAY_TEMPLATE_ID"],
    [{"seat": "signer_1", "name": "Rosa Alvarez", "email": "rosa@example.com"}],
)
print(doc["id"], doc["state"])
```

---

<!-- https://docustay.app/sign-pdf/go -->
# Send a document for signature from Go

Sign PDF API in Go: a short program that sends a template for signature, run against Docustay with a test key before it was published. Set DOCUSTAY_API_KEY and DOCUSTAY_TEMPLATE_ID.

`go get github.com/docustay/docustay-go/docustay@v0.2.2`

The module needs Go 1.23 or newer and has no dependencies beyond the standard library. Every call that creates something takes an idempotency key: build one per attempt and reuse it when you retry. Pass the server only when you point at a self-hosted install. The client is generated from the OpenAPI document, so every operation is there.

```
package main

import (
	"context"
	"fmt"
	"os"
	"time"

	docustay "github.com/docustay/docustay-go/docustay"
)

func main() {
	cfg := docustay.NewConfiguration()
	server := "https://app.docustay.app"
	if u := os.Getenv("DOCUSTAY_URL"); u != "" {
		server = u
	}
	cfg.Servers = docustay.ServerConfigurations{{URL: server}}
	client := docustay.NewAPIClient(cfg)
	ctx := context.WithValue(context.Background(), docustay.ContextAccessToken, os.Getenv("DOCUSTAY_API_KEY"))

	request := *docustay.NewSendRequest(os.Getenv("DOCUSTAY_TEMPLATE_ID"), []docustay.SendRequestPartiesInner{
		*docustay.NewSendRequestPartiesInner("signer_1", "Rosa Alvarez", "rosa@example.com"),
	})
	doc, _, err := client.DocumentsAPI.SendDocument(ctx).SendRequest(request).IdempotencyKey(fmt.Sprintf("send-%d", time.Now().UnixNano())).Execute()
	if err != nil {
		fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, err)
		os.Exit(1)
	}
	fmt.Println(doc.GetId(), doc.GetState())
}
```

---

<!-- https://docustay.app/sign-pdf/php -->
# Send a document for signature from PHP

Sign PDF API in PHP: a short program that sends a template for signature, run against Docustay with a test key before it was published. Set DOCUSTAY_API_KEY and DOCUSTAY_TEMPLATE_ID.

`composer require docustay/docustay-php`

The package needs PHP 7.4 or newer with the curl and json extensions, and uses Guzzle. The first argument of each call that creates something is an idempotency key: build one per attempt and reuse it when you retry. Pass the host only when you point at a self-hosted install.

```
<?php
require __DIR__ . '/vendor/autoload.php';

$config = Docustay\Configuration::getDefaultConfiguration()->setAccessToken(getenv('DOCUSTAY_API_KEY'));
if ($url = getenv('DOCUSTAY_URL')) {
    $config->setHost($url);
}
$api = new Docustay\Api\DocumentsApi(new GuzzleHttp\Client(), $config);

$request = new Docustay\Model\SendRequest([
    'template_id' => getenv('DOCUSTAY_TEMPLATE_ID'),
    'parties' => [new Docustay\Model\SendRequestPartiesInner([
        'seat' => 'signer_1', 'name' => 'Rosa Alvarez', 'email' => 'rosa@example.com',
    ])],
]);
$doc = $api->sendDocument(bin2hex(random_bytes(16)), $request);
echo $doc->getId(), ' ', $doc->getState(), PHP_EOL;
```

---

<!-- https://docustay.app/sign-pdf/csharp -->
# Send a document for signature from C#

Sign PDF API in C#: a short program that sends a template for signature, run against Docustay with a test key before it was published. Set DOCUSTAY_API_KEY and DOCUSTAY_TEMPLATE_ID.

`dotnet add package Docustay.Api`

The package targets .NET 8. Every call that creates something takes an idempotency key as its first argument: build one per attempt and reuse it when you retry. Set BasePath only when you point at a self-hosted install.

```
using Docustay.Api.Api;
using Docustay.Api.Client;
using Docustay.Api.Model;

var config = new Configuration { BasePath = Environment.GetEnvironmentVariable("DOCUSTAY_URL") ?? "https://app.docustay.app" };
config.AccessToken = Environment.GetEnvironmentVariable("DOCUSTAY_API_KEY");
var api = new DocumentsApi(config);

var request = new SendRequest(
    templateId: Guid.Parse(Environment.GetEnvironmentVariable("DOCUSTAY_TEMPLATE_ID")!),
    parties: new List<SendRequestPartiesInner> { new SendRequestPartiesInner(seat: "signer_1", name: "Rosa Alvarez", email: "rosa@example.com") });
var doc = api.SendDocument(Guid.NewGuid().ToString(), request);
Console.WriteLine($"{doc.Id} {doc.State}");
```
