# Docustay developer documentation

Docustay sends documents for signature. Everything you can do in the app you can also do from code, within the permissions of an API key you create.

| You want to | Start here |
|---|---|
| Send your first document in ten minutes | [Quickstart](/docs/quickstart.md) |
| Understand keys, scopes and test keys | [Authentication](/docs/authentication.md) |
| Make a document from words and people, answer a template's questions, collect a payment | [Documents from words and people](/docs/documents-from-words.md) |
| Turn HTML or a tagged PDF into a template | [Templates and text tags](/docs/templates-and-text-tags.md) |
| Show the signing form inside your own app | [Embedded signing](/docs/embedding.md) |
| Start from a ready-made template | [The template library](/docs/template-library) |
| Search the workspace, list and refund payments | [Search and payments](/docs/search-and-payments) |
| List the built-in templates, draft from one, customize one, switch packs on | [The template library](/docs/template-library.md) |
| Get told when a document is signed | [Webhooks](/docs/webhooks.md) |
| Practise without sending anything real | [Test mode](/docs/test-mode.md) |
| Handle failures and limits | [Errors, retries and limits](/docs/errors-and-limits.md) |
| Use a generated client | [SDKs](/docs/sdks.md) |
| Let an AI assistant do it | [MCP server and agent skills](/docs/mcp-and-skills.md) |
| Look up an operation | [API reference](/docs/api-reference.md) |

Every page here is also served as plain Markdown at the same address with `.md` on the end, and `/llms.txt` lists them all for tools that read documentation.

## What you can build

A typical integration is small. Your system decides a document is needed, calls the API with a template and the people's names and emails, and waits for a webhook. When the webhook says the document is completed, your system downloads the signed copy and files it. Everything between is Docustay's job: emailing, reminders, the signing page, the certificate and the seal.

```bash
curl -X POST https://docustay.app/api/v1/documents/send \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $DOCUSTAY_API_KEY" -H "Idempotency-Key: $(uuidgen)" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{ "templateId": "'"$DOCUSTAY_TEMPLATE_ID"'", "parties": [{ "seat": "signer_1", "name": "Rosa Alvarez", "email": "rosa@example.com" }] }'
```

## Where to start

New to it: do the quickstart with a test key, which emails only you. Already sending: read Webhooks and Errors, retries and limits before you go live, because retries and repeat deliveries are where integrations go wrong. Building a product: read Embedded signing.

## What is included

The API, webhooks and embedding are in every plan, within your monthly allowance. Test mode is free and uncounted. The SDKs and the MCP server run on your own machine with your own key.

```js
import { Docustay } from "@docustay2026/sdk";
const docustay = new Docustay(process.env.DOCUSTAY_API_KEY);
```

## Conventions every page assumes

- **Authentication:** `Authorization: Bearer <key>` on every call. Keys start `dsk_live_` or `dsk_test_`, carry only the scopes you ticked, and are shown once.
- **Retries:** requests that create a document or template need an `Idempotency-Key` of 8 to 200 characters; repeating the same key and body returns the first answer.
- **Limits:** each key may make 600 requests a minute; past that the answer is `429` with a `Retry-After` header.
- **Errors:** always `{ "error": { "kind", "message", "requestId", "retryable" } }`. Quote the `requestId` when you ask for help.
- **Webhooks:** events use `event.topic` (for example `documents.document.executed`) and `event.subject_id`, with three signature headers you must verify.
- **Command line:** `npx docustay listen` forwards real signed events to your laptop, and `docustay send --test` sends a practice document from a template.


---

# Quickstart

## Time to first signature

The goal is a first signed document within 30 minutes. In order: make a key (below), make a template (step 1), send it to yourself (step 2), open the signing email and sign, then read the executed document (step 3). Use a test key first, then a live one. In a scripted run on our test environment (sign-up, key, template, send, email, sign) the product's own waiting time was about 20 seconds, so almost all of your time is reading and writing the template.

You need a Docustay workspace and a key. In the app open **Settings → Developers → API keys** and make a key with the scopes `documents:read` and `documents:write`. Make a **test** key first (it starts `dsk_test_`): everything it does is a practice run.

> A test key works in any workspace, whether or not test mode is switched on: everything it sends is a practice run, emailed only to you and stamped TEST. If your first request answers `401`, check that you copied the whole key and that it is a key of this workspace.

> The examples use `https://app.docustay.app`. A self-hosted install or a practice server has its own address: put that address in the commands instead, and pass it to the SDKs as `baseUrl` (JavaScript) or `base_url` (Python).

## 1. Make a template

A template is a document with places for people to sign. The quickest way is HTML with text tags (see [Templates and text tags](/docs/templates-and-text-tags.md)):

```bash
curl -X POST https://app.docustay.app/api/v1/templates/html \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $DOCUSTAY_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "Idempotency-Key: $(uuidgen)" \
  -d '{"name":"Simple NDA","html":"<h1>Mutual NDA</h1><p>Both parties keep each other'"'"'s information private.</p><p>Signed: {{Sign here;type=signature;role=Partner}}</p>"}'
```

The answer holds the `templateId` and how many `fields` were placed.

## 2. Send it

```bash
curl -X POST https://app.docustay.app/api/v1/documents/send \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $DOCUSTAY_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "Idempotency-Key: $(uuidgen)" \
  -d '{"templateId":"'"$DOCUSTAY_TEMPLATE_ID"'","title":"NDA with Acme","parties":[{"seat":"signer_1","name":"Alex Rivera","email":"alex@example.com"}]}'
```

`seat` is the template's seat key. Seats appear in the order roles first appear in the document: the first role is `signer_1`, the next `signer_2`. `GET /api/v1/templates/{id}` lists them.

## 3. Follow it

```bash
curl https://app.docustay.app/api/v1/documents/$DOCUSTAY_DOCUMENT_ID -H "Authorization: Bearer $DOCUSTAY_API_KEY"
```

`state` moves `sent` → `partially_signed` → `executed` (or `declined`, `expired`, `void`). When it is `executed`, `GET /api/v1/documents/{id}/signed.pdf` returns the sealed copy. The sealed PDF is made a few seconds after the last signature (the document says `signedCopyAvailable: true` once it exists); until then the call answers 404 "the sealed copy is being made", so ask again after a moment, or wait for the `documents.document.executed` webhook.

## The same in code

Install the SDK first. Node 18 or later: `npm install @docustay2026/sdk`. Python 3.9 or later, in a virtual environment:

```bash
python3 -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate
pip install docustay
```

```js
import { Docustay } from "@docustay2026/sdk";
const docustay = new Docustay(process.env.DOCUSTAY_API_KEY);
const { templateId } = await docustay.createTemplateFromHtml({ name: "Simple NDA", html: "<p>Signed: {{Sign here;type=signature;role=Partner}}</p>" });
const { id } = await docustay.sendDocument({ templateId, parties: [{ seat: "signer_1", name: "Alex Rivera", email: "alex@example.com" }] });
console.log((await docustay.getDocument(id)).state);
```

```python
import os
from docustay import Docustay
d = Docustay(os.environ["DOCUSTAY_API_KEY"])
t = d.create_template_from_html("Simple NDA", "<p>Signed: {{Sign here;type=signature;role=Partner}}</p>")
doc = d.send_document(t["templateId"], [{"seat": "signer_1", "name": "Alex Rivera", "email": "alex@example.com"}])
print(d.get_document(doc["id"])["state"])
```

Next: [get told when it is signed](/docs/webhooks.md) instead of asking.

The same first call in Go, PHP and C# is on the [SDKs page](/docs/sdks.md#other-languages).

## Check your key before you start

Two ways to confirm a key works without sending anything. The command line saves it and asks the API who it belongs to:

```bash
npx docustay login --key "$DOCUSTAY_API_KEY"
npx docustay whoami
```

Or send a practice document from a template in one line, with your own address as the signer (a test key emails only you):

```bash
npx docustay send --test $DOCUSTAY_TEMPLATE_ID --party "signer_1=Alex Rivera <you@example.com>"
```

## If a step fails

- `401` on any call: one answer covers a missing, wrong, revoked or out-of-scope key. Check the whole key was copied and that it has `documents:write` for steps 1 and 2.
- `400` on step 2: the message names the field. A `seat` that is not on the template is the usual cause; read the seats with `GET /api/v1/templates/{id}`.
- `403` on step 1 or 2: the Free plan has a monthly allowance for new templates and sent documents, and the error carries `plan_template_limit` or `plan_document_limit`. Test-mode documents are never counted.


---

# Authentication

Send `Authorization: Bearer <key>` on every request. Keys are made in **Settings → Developers → API keys** and shown once; if you lose one, make another and revoke the old.

## Scopes

A key carries only the scopes you tick when you make it. The two broad scopes (`documents:read` and `documents:write`) open everything about documents; the narrower ones let you make a key that does one job and nothing else, for example one that only reads teams and plan usage. A Docustay workspace is offered 12 scopes, and the table lists all of them.

| Scope | Lets the key |
|---|---|
| `documents:read` | list and read documents and templates, read the audit log, download signed copies, read teams |
| `documents:write` | send documents, make templates, remind, void, start an embedded signing session |
| `templates:read` | list and read templates |
| `templates:write` | make and change templates and their defaults |
| `account:read` | read plan usage, payment status and teams |
| `webhooks:read` | list your webhook addresses and what was sent to them |
| `webhooks:write` | add, change, test and remove webhook addresses, and make a new signing secret |
| `embedded:write` | start an embedded signing session for a seat you marked as embedded |
| `plays:read` | read skills and playbooks |
| `plays:write` | make and change skills and playbooks |
| `drafts:write` | make drafts only; nothing in it sends a document |
| `people:read` | list the people in your workspace by name |

A key can only carry scopes its creator holds. A request without the scope gets the same `401` answer as a wrong key, on purpose: nothing tells a guesser which half was right.

## Test keys and live keys

`dsk_test_…` keys act on test data only: documents sent with one are practice runs. `dsk_live_…` keys act on real documents. See [Test mode](/docs/test-mode.md).

## What a key can never do

No response contains a signing link or an access code, and a key cannot sign for anyone. The one exception is [embedded signing](/docs/embedding.md): for seats **you** mark as embedded when you send, a key can ask for a one-hour session to show your own signer the form on a website you listed.

## Keeping a key safe

- Keep it on your server. Never put a key in a web page or a mobile app.
- Give it only the scopes it needs, and make one key per integration so one can be revoked alone.
- Every use of a key is in the audit log with the key's name, and revoking takes effect at once.

## A request, start to finish

List your executed documents with a key that has `documents:read`:

```bash
curl https://docustay.app/api/v1/documents?state=executed \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $DOCUSTAY_API_KEY"
```

The same call from JavaScript, using the SDK, which adds the header for you:

```js
import { Docustay } from "@docustay2026/sdk";
const docustay = new Docustay(process.env.DOCUSTAY_API_KEY);
const page = await docustay.listDocuments({ state: "executed", limit: 20 });
```

## When a key stops working

A `401` after it used to work means the key was revoked, expired or lost a scope. Make a new key, update the one integration that used it, and the audit log will show which key made which call, so you can see whether the old one is still being used somewhere.


---

# Templates and text tags

A **text tag** is written inside the document's own text where a field should go:

```
{{Buyer signature;type=signature;role=Buyer}}
```

The first part is the name. After it come `key=value` pairs separated by semicolons. A tag needs at least one `key=value`; `{{signer.name}}` with none is a merge field and is left alone.

| Key | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `type` | `signature`, `initials`, `date_signed`, `stamp`, `text` (default), `number`, `date`, `email`, `phone`, `zip`, `checkbox`, `dropdown` (or `select`), `multiselect`, `image`, `file`, `payment` |
| `role` | Who fills it in, any words. The first role written is `signer_1`, the next `signer_2`, and so on |
| `required` | `true` (default) or `false`. A required checkbox must be TICKED to sign, so give a box the signer may leave empty (a choice, such as "you may use my name") `required=false` |
| `default` | A starting value. Not allowed on signature, initials, date_signed or stamp |
| `options` | A comma list for dropdown and multiselect: `options=Monthly,Yearly` |
| `label` | The caption the signer sees (default: the name) |
| `width`, `height` | Size in points (1/72 inch); each type has a default |
| `max_length` | Most characters a text field takes |
| `filled` | `signer` (default) or `sender`. `filled=sender` is a box you fill in before sending: your organisation's own details and the terms you set (the trip on a permission slip, the fee in an agreement). The person signing sees your answer and cannot change it. It goes on text, dropdown and multiselect boxes; it makes no seat of its own. A required one with no answer stops the send, and a form with one cannot go live until it has its answer |
| `from` | With `filled=sender`, where the first answer comes from: `org.name`, `org.email`, `sender.name` or `sender.email`, worked out when you send. You can still type over it before sending |
| `amount`, `currency` | For `payment`: a fixed amount, `amount=150.00;currency=usd`. A payment takes a fixed `amount` (see Payments below) |

A value that holds a semicolon or an equals sign goes in double quotes: `default="Smith; Jones"`.

## From HTML

`POST /api/v1/templates/html` with `{ "name", "html", "paper" }` prints your HTML to a PDF and places a field wherever a tag sits. Scripts, styles that load anything, frames, forms and remote addresses are removed before printing; pictures must be `data:` addresses; the whole request, pictures included, may be up to 2 MB (a larger one gets `413` "request body too large"). The answer is `{ templateId, fields, warnings }`. A tag that could not be read comes back in `warnings`, naming that tag.

## From a document source

`POST /api/v1/templates/source` with `{ "name", "source", "profile", "paper" }` keeps a document written in the shared editor's JSON format (`{ "type": "doc", "content": [...] }`) as a template. `profile` is `typeset` (default) or `contract`; `paper` is `letter` or `a4`. Needs the `documents:write` scope and an `Idempotency-Key`. Answers 201 with `{ templateId, profile, version, hash, warnings }`.

```bash
curl -X POST https://docustay.app/api/v1/templates/source \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $DOCUSTAY_API_KEY" -H "Idempotency-Key: $(uuidgen)" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{ "name": "Notice", "source": { "type": "doc", "content": [{ "type": "paragraph", "content": [{ "type": "text", "text": "Hello" }] }, { "type": "signatureBlock", "attrs": { "slots": [{ "role": "Client", "label": "Client signature" }] } }] } }'
```

## Ask for an AI draft

AI drafting is off by default; it is refused plainly while it is off for your workspace or when a limit is reached. A draft is a suggestion for a person to read: nothing is saved or sent.

`POST /api/v1/documents/ai/draft` with `{ "prompt", "mode" }` (`mode` is `template` or `document`) answers 202 with `{ jobId, state }`.

```bash
curl -X POST https://docustay.app/api/v1/documents/ai/draft \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $DOCUSTAY_API_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{ "prompt": "A one-page services agreement with a client signature", "mode": "template" }'
```

`GET /api/v1/documents/ai/jobs/{id}` returns `{ id, state, message, source, patches }`. `state` is `queued`, `running`, `done`, `failed` or `cancelled`; poll until it is not queued or running. When done, `source` is the draft and `patches.notes` lists what to check.

```bash
curl https://docustay.app/api/v1/documents/ai/jobs/$JOB_ID -H "Authorization: Bearer $DOCUSTAY_API_KEY"
```

## From a file

`POST /api/v1/templates/file` with `{ "name", "fileName", "file" }` where `file` is the base64 of a PDF file with tags written in it. Tags are found in the file's text, covered with a white box and replaced by the field. The box covers the tag on the page, but its characters stay in the file's hidden text layer, so a search or a copy of the signed PDF can still find them. If that matters, set the tags in white in your source file, or make the template from HTML, which never prints them.

## Check the seats

`GET /api/v1/templates/{id}` returns the template's `seats`. Send with one `parties` entry per seat: `{ "seat": "signer_1", "name": "…", "email": "…" }`.

## Payments

A `payment` field makes the signer pay on Stripe's own page before their signature completes. The money goes to **the Stripe account you connect** (Settings → Payments → Connect Stripe; Stripe's own sign-up page creates it in your name, separate from any Stripe account you already have). Docustay's fee is 2% of each payment on the Free plan and 0% on Pro, on top of Stripe's own fees, which Stripe charges to that Stripe account as usual. Card details are typed on Stripe's page; Docustay never receives or stores them.

A payment field takes one fixed amount. To charge a different amount for each document, use `amount=custom.key` and give the amount when you send:

| Amount | Tag | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Fixed | `amount=150.00` | 0.50 to 999,999.99 |

## A tag in an HTML file, sent through the API

```bash
curl -X POST https://docustay.app/api/v1/templates/html \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $DOCUSTAY_API_KEY" -H "Idempotency-Key: $(uuidgen)" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{ "name": "Services agreement", "html": "<p>Client: {{Client signature;type=signature;role=Client}}</p>" }'
```


---

# Embedded signing

Show the signing form inside your own page, so the signer never leaves your app.

## How it fits together

1. **List your website.** In **Settings → Developers → Embedding** add each website that will show the form, one per line, for example `https://app.example.com`. While developing, add `http://localhost:3000` (or your own port) to the same list: localhost is the one plain `http` address it takes. Nothing else (no path, no other plain `http`) is. An address that is not on the list gets `409` with the address in the message.
2. **Send with embedded seats.** On your server add `embedded: ["signer_1"]` to the send request. Nobody is emailed for those seats.
3. **Ask for a session.** On your server call `POST /api/v1/documents/{id}/embed-session` with `{ "seat": "signer_1", "origin": "https://app.example.com" }`. The answer is `{ url, expiresAt }`. The link works for one hour; ask again each time the page loads. Asking again does not end a session that is already open: the five newest links for a seat keep working until their hour is up, so a page that loads twice or a second tab is fine.
4. **Show it.** Give the `url` to the element.

The API key stays on your server. The `url` is the only thing the browser sees.

## The element

```html
<script type="module" src="https://docustay.app/embed/index.js"></script>
<!-- on your own install, use your own address: https://YOUR-HOST/embed/index.js -->
<docustay-sign url="https://…/sign/pdf?t=…&embed=1&parent=https%3A%2F%2Fapp.example.com" height="720"></docustay-sign>
```

The script address above is the hosted one. On a self-hosted install or the sandbox, use your own address instead: your install's web address followed by `/embed/index.js`.


Attributes: `url`, `height` (pixels or any CSS length), `auto-height` (follow the form's own height), `title`. Events, each with `detail.documentId`:

| Event | When |
|---|---|
| `ready` | the form has loaded |
| `waiting` | it is not this person's turn yet |
| `completed` | the signer finished |
| `declined` | the signer declined |
| `error` | the link was refused (expired, wrong, or the website is not on the list). A refused frame cannot speak, so the element raises this itself when nothing has arrived from the frame after 15 seconds (`detail.message` says the form did not load) |
| `resize` | the form's height changed (`detail.height`) |

The `docustay` event carries all of them as `{ type, … }`. Events do not bubble.

## React, Vue, Angular

Install the wrapper for your framework together with the web component it wraps:

```bash
npm install @docustay2026/react @docustay2026/embed     # React 17 or later
npm install @docustay2026/vue @docustay2026/embed       # Vue 3.3 or later
npm install @docustay2026/angular @docustay2026/embed   # Angular 17 or later
```

```jsx
import { DocustaySign } from "@docustay2026/react";
<DocustaySign url={session.url} onCompleted={({ documentId }) => confirmOnServer(documentId)} />
```

```vue
<DocustaySign :url="session.url" @completed="done" />
```

```html
<docustay-sign-form [url]="session.url" (completed)="done($event)"></docustay-sign-form>
```

## What keeps it safe

- The form can be framed only by the websites you listed. Docustay sends a `frame-ancestors` header naming exactly those, and only for a link made for an embedded seat. An ordinary emailed link is never frameable, even with `embed=1` added.
- The form sends its events to one parent origin, the one in the link, and only if it is on your list. The element accepts a message only from its own frame and the form's own origin.
- Treat `completed` as a prompt, not proof: confirm with `GET /api/v1/documents/{id}` on your server (`state: executed`).

## Let your people build templates inside your own page

The builder is the same editor Docustay uses, in a frame on your website. Your server asks for a session; your page shows it.

1. **On your server** (never in a browser), with a key that has the `embedded:write` scope:

   ```bash
   curl -X POST "${DOCUSTAY_URL:-https://docustay.app}/api/v1/embedded/builder-session" \
     -H "Authorization: Bearer $DOCUSTAY_API_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
     -d '{ "origin": "https://app.example.com", "name": "Services agreement" }'
   ```

   The answer is a `url` that works for one hour. The website must already be on your allowed list (Settings → Developers → Embedding); anything else gets a 409.
2. **In your page**, show it:

   ```html
   <script type="module" src="https://docustay.app/embed/index.js"></script>
   <docustay-builder url="…the url…" height="760"></docustay-builder>
   ```

3. **Listen** for `ready`, `saved` (`{ templateId, name, fields }`) and `error`. Use the `templateId` to send documents from your server as usual.

What keeps it safe: the key inside the link is created for this session only, lives in the `#fragment` (so no server log sees it), expires in an hour, and can read and write templates and nothing else — it cannot send a document. The link names the one website that may frame it and is signed; change the website and it will not frame anywhere.


---

# Field detection

Uploading never places boxes by itself. Only exact sources appear on their own: the form fields already inside the PDF, text tags, a template, or a form you have sent before. For anything else, press **Find fields** in the editor and Docustay looks at the page the way a person would and places the boxes it would draw by hand: signature lines, "Date:" blanks, initials, text lines, empty boxes and table cells, tick boxes, and highlighted "sign here" bars. It reads the words beside each blank (in English, Spanish, French, German, Italian, Portuguese, Dutch, Polish, Russian, Turkish, Japanese, Korean, Chinese and Arabic), works out which person each box belongs to ("Participant", "Witness", "Case Manager", "Landlord"…), and says how sure it is of each one.

Nothing is placed until you accept it. In the editor the boxes appear dashed in each person's colour, with a line such as "Found 14 fields, 3 signers; 2 not sure about". **Accept all**, or fix them one at a time. A form you have sent before comes back with the boxes you finally placed.

A scanned PDF page has no text, so it is read by character recognition on the server (English). A page in another script is read by shape alone.

Detection by the program is free. The optional **Find fields with AI** button (shown only where AI is turned on) hands the pages to the model in the background, one page at a time in parallel, with a progress line such as "Finding fields 3 of 12 pages". The model is shown each page and a numbered list of the boxes the program drew, and it only picks numbers and says what each one is and whose it is: it never draws a box of its own, so nothing can land off the page. It costs 0.25 credit a page, at most 20 pages a file and a dollar cap per file; if the AI is unavailable the program's own result stays and a plain message says so. Nothing is placed until you accept it.

## How it decides

Each blank is judged by the words printed beside it and the shape it makes on the page. A line next to "Signature", "Initials", "Date", "Email" or "Phone" becomes that kind of field. A line with no useful label becomes a plain text field. Words like "Landlord", "Witness" or "Parent or guardian" next to a blank decide which person it belongs to, and "Borrower signature" makes a new role called Borrower.

The program marks a box "not sure" when the label and the shape disagree, when two readings fit, or when a blank sits in dense running text. The AI look sees all of them, weak ones included; without it nothing leaves the server. Sensitive blanks (a social security or account number, a date of birth) are marked sensitive: the signing page masks what the signer types and turns off browser autofill for them.

## Over the API

`POST /api/v1/documents/detect-fields` takes a file and stores nothing:

```bash
curl https://app.docustay.app/api/v1/documents/detect-fields \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $DOCUSTAY_API_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d "{\"fileName\":\"intake.pdf\",\"file\":\"$(base64 -i intake.pdf)\"}"
```

Each field has `type`, `page`, `x`, `y`, `w`, `h` (fractions of the page, origin top left), `confidence` (0 to 1), `source` (`native`, `line`, `text`, `box`, `table`, `checkbox`, `highlight`, `remembered`, `vision`), the printed `label`, the `role` (a seat key from `signers`), `sensitive` (an SSN, a date of birth, an account number) and `group` (tick boxes that answer one question). Fields under `minConfidence` (default 0.6) are marked `uncertain`. `pages` says which pages are forms and which are reference pages; `documents` says how a packet splits.

To make a template and place the sure fields in one call, upload with `fields: "auto"`:

```bash
curl https://app.docustay.app/api/v1/templates/file -H "Idempotency-Key: $(uuidgen)" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $DOCUSTAY_API_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d "{\"name\":\"Intake\",\"fileName\":\"intake.pdf\",\"file\":\"$(base64 -i intake.pdf)\",\"fields\":\"auto\"}"
```

The answer's `detected` says how many fields were found, how many seats, how many it was unsure of and how many were placed. A `documents.template.fields_detected` webhook event is sent with the same numbers.

From the command line: `docustay detect intake.pdf`. From an assistant: the MCP tool `detect_fields`. In Node, `docustay.detectFields({ file, fileName })`; in Python, `client.detect_fields(file, file_name)`.

## What it will not do

Through the API the file goes in the body as base64 and may be as large as your plan's upload limit (25 MB on Free and Pay as you go, 100 MB on Pro and Lifetime). A bigger file is refused with `400` and the code `too_big`, which says the limit.

It does not read ID, card or bank numbers out of a picture, and it never sends a page to the AI unless you pressed Find fields with AI. Files are checked first: scripts, launch actions and embedded files are removed from the copy that is kept, and at most the first 100 pages are read, within a time limit. A file that cannot be read simply has no suggestions.


---

# Documents from words and people

Everything the screens do, a key can do. A document is **words** (a source) plus **people** (a name, an email, a role word). Roles are words from the text, such as `Client` and `Provider`, never seat numbers.

## Make a document

```bash
curl -X POST https://app.docustay.app/api/v1/documents \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $DOCUSTAY_API_KEY" -H "Idempotency-Key: $(uuidgen)" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "title": "Retainer agreement",
    "source": { "type": "doc", "content": [
      { "type": "heading", "attrs": { "level": 1 }, "content": [{ "type": "text", "text": "Retainer agreement" }] },
      { "type": "paragraph", "content": [{ "type": "text", "text": "The studio works for " },
        { "type": "variableChip", "attrs": { "name": "custom.p_client_name", "label": "Client name" } }, { "type": "text", "text": "." }] },
      { "type": "paragraph", "content": [{ "type": "fieldTag", "attrs": { "name": "Client signature", "type": "signature", "role": "Client" } }] }
    ] },
    "people": [{ "name": "Dana Whitfield", "email": "dana@example.com", "role": "Client" }],
    "send": { "subject": "Please sign", "reminderDays": [3, 7], "expiryDays": 30 }
  }'
```

The answer is `{ "id", "state": "draft", "roles": [...] }`. The document stays a **draft** until you send it with `POST /api/v1/documents/{id}/send` (or set `sendNow: true`). The same checks as the screen's Send apply.

* **People.** `{ name, email, role?, action?, order? }`. `action` is `signer`, `approver`, `viewer`, `assistant` or `cc`. Each person's own name and email are available to the words as merge text: a `custom.p_<role>_name` chip (for example `custom.p_client_name`) prints that role's person.
* **Smart fields.** A `fieldTag` can fill itself from the person (`autofill: "name"` or `"email"`), allow or forbid changes (`editable`), carry a `placeholder` and `tooltip`, or be filled by you and locked (`locked` with a `default`).
* **Sender only sections.** A heading with `audience: "sender"` hides itself and everything below it up to the next heading of the same or higher level. It is in nothing a signer sees, signs or receives. A signer field inside such a section is refused.
* **Check first.** `POST /api/v1/documents/check` tells you what a person would be told: errors, warnings and the roles in the text. Nothing is saved.
* **Read and change a draft.** `GET /api/v1/documents/{id}/source` returns the words, people and choices. `POST /api/v1/documents/{id}/revise` prints new words into a **new** draft that takes the people and choices; the old draft is deleted, so **the id changes**.

## Templates with questions

A `custom.<key>` merge chip in a template is a **question** the sender answers when using it (`kind` is `text`, `number`, `money` or `date`; `default` and `help` are optional). The template's questions are shown where you build and send it in the app; through the API you pass an answer for each question's key in `variableValues`. Use the template (its id is in `GET /api/v1/documents/templates`; put it in `$TEMPLATE` first):

```bash
TEMPLATE=$(curl -s https://app.docustay.app/api/v1/documents/templates -H "Authorization: Bearer $DOCUSTAY_API_KEY" | jq -r '.templates[0].id')
curl -X POST https://app.docustay.app/api/v1/templates/$TEMPLATE/documents \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $DOCUSTAY_API_KEY" -H "Idempotency-Key: $(uuidgen)" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{ "people": [{ "name": "Dana Whitfield", "email": "dana@example.com" }], "variableValues": { "fee": "750", "client_company": "Harbor Traders" } }'
```

Every question must have an answer (or a starting answer). `POST /api/v1/templates/{id}/defaults` sets what a document made from the template starts with: its description, the signer-facing text, the message and the send choices.

## The assistant

* **Draft.** `POST /api/v1/documents/ai/draft` takes a plain `prompt` or the wizard's `brief`. `GET /api/v1/ai/wizard` returns the same questions the screen asks, the payment questions and the currencies offered.
* **Change.** `POST /api/v1/documents/ai/edit` takes `request` and `source` and returns **proposed changes**, never an edited document: `patches.applied` lists `replace_text`, `insert_block`, `replace_block` and `remove_block` operations for a person to accept. With `variables` (the template's questions) it also proposes answers in `patches.values`.
* **Progress.** Read `GET /api/v1/documents/ai/jobs/{id}`: `stage` moves `queued`, `writing`, `checking`, `ready` (or `failed`), and `state` is `queued`, `running`, `done`, `failed` or `cancelled`. `POST /api/v1/documents/ai/jobs/{id}/cancel` stops it. A job whose worker died is put back and finished by itself.
* The assistant never sends, never pays and never signs.

## Collect a payment at signing

Put the payment in the brief: `"payment": { "collect": true, "amount": "1500", "currency": "usd", "payer_role": "Client", "description": "the first month" }`. The **amount comes only from the person**: the assistant drafts around it, the worker (plain code) checks every amount it proposes against yours and places one Payment field for the payer, and the payment terms are written in the text from your own values. Later payments are written as text (`schedule_note`).

The signer pays on Stripe's hosted page and cannot sign until Stripe says it is paid. `GET /api/v1/payments/status` says `connected` (details submitted, charges on, nothing due), `needs_attention` or `not_connected`. **A document with a payment field can only be sent when it says `connected`**; otherwise Send answers with a plain reason. Currencies offered: usd, eur, gbp, cad, aud, nzd, chf, sek, nok, dkk.

## From an SDK or MCP

| API | JavaScript | Python | MCP tool |
|---|---|---|---|
| `POST /documents` | `createDocument` | `create_document` | `create_document` |
| `POST /documents/check` | `checkDocument` | `check_document` | `check_document` |
| `GET /documents/{id}/source` | `getDraftSource` | `get_draft_source` | `get_draft_source` |
| `POST /documents/{id}/revise` | `reviseDocument` | `revise_document` | `revise_document` |
| `POST /documents/{id}/send` | `sendDraft` | `send_draft` | `send_draft` (asks first) |
| `POST /templates/{id}/documents` | `useTemplate` | `use_template` | `use_template` |
| `POST /templates/{id}/defaults` | `setTemplateDefaults` | `set_template_defaults` | `set_template_defaults` |
| `POST /documents/ai/draft` | `draftWithAi` | `draft_with_ai` | `draft_document_with_ai` |
| `POST /documents/ai/edit` | `editWithAi` | `edit_with_ai` | `edit_document_with_ai` |
| `GET /ai/wizard` | `getWizard` | `get_wizard` | `get_wizard` |
| `GET /payments/status` | `paymentsStatus` | `payments_status` | `get_payments_status` |

Over MCP, nothing emails anyone until `send_draft` is called again with `confirm: true`, and there is no tool that signs, pays or deletes.


---

# Webhooks

Register an endpoint in **Settings → Developers → Webhooks**, choose the events, and Docustay posts a JSON event to it each time one happens. Each endpoint has a secret that starts `whsec_`, shown once.

## Verify every delivery

Deliveries carry the [Standard Webhooks](https://www.standardwebhooks.com) headers `webhook-id`, `webhook-timestamp` and `webhook-signature` (`v1,<base64 HMAC-SHA256 of "id.timestamp.body">`). Verify against the **raw** body, not re-serialised JSON.

Deliveries also carry three older headers, `keystone-event-id`, `keystone-timestamp` and `keystone-signature`, kept for receivers built before the Standard Webhooks ones. New code should ignore them and verify with the `webhook-*` headers above. An event's `data` can also hold fields this page does not show; rely only on the documented ones, since others may change or go without notice.

```js
// npm install @docustay2026/sdk  ·  DOCUSTAY_WEBHOOK_SECRET=whsec_… node receiver.mjs
import http from "node:http";
import { verifyWebhook } from "@docustay2026/sdk";

http.createServer(async (req, res) => {
  let rawBody = ""; for await (const chunk of req) rawBody += chunk;   // the raw text, before any JSON parser
  try {
    const event = await verifyWebhook(process.env.DOCUSTAY_WEBHOOK_SECRET, req.headers, rawBody);
    console.log(event.topic, event.subject_id);
    res.writeHead(204).end();
  } catch { res.writeHead(400).end("bad signature"); }
}).listen(4000, () => console.log("listening on http://localhost:4000"));
```

```python
# pip install docustay  ·  DOCUSTAY_WEBHOOK_SECRET=whsec_… python receiver.py
import os
from http.server import BaseHTTPRequestHandler, HTTPServer
from docustay import verify_webhook

class Receiver(BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
    def do_POST(self):
        raw_body = self.rfile.read(int(self.headers.get("content-length", 0)))   # the raw bytes, before any JSON parser
        try:
            event = verify_webhook(os.environ["DOCUSTAY_WEBHOOK_SECRET"], self.headers, raw_body)
            print(event["topic"], event["subject_id"])
            self.send_response(204); self.end_headers()
        except ValueError:
            self.send_response(400); self.end_headers(); self.wfile.write(b"bad signature")

HTTPServer(("localhost", 4000), Receiver).serve_forever()
```

Both refuse a changed body, a wrong secret and a timestamp more than five minutes old.
A receiver using any Standard Webhooks library passes `whsec_` plus the secret with `-` swapped for `+` and `_` for `/`.

## Trying it from your laptop

Docustay can only send to a public `https://` address: `localhost`, `127.0.0.1` and office or home network addresses are refused when you add the endpoint, and the message says so. While you build the receiver, give your laptop a public address with a tunnel tool, add that address as the endpoint, and use **Send again** in the delivery log to replay an event as often as you like. When the receiver is deployed, replace the address.

## Delivery

Answer with any `2xx` quickly. A delivery that fails is tried again after 1 minute, 5 minutes, 30 minutes, 2 hours and 12 hours, which is six attempts in all. After the sixth failure it is marked as given up. Every attempt is in the delivery log under the endpoint, where a delivery can be replayed. Deliveries can arrive more than once and out of order: use the `webhook-id` to ignore a repeat, and fetch the document (`GET /api/v1/documents/{id}`) rather than trusting the event as the final word.

The events carry facts about the document, never a signing link or a code.

## What a delivery looks like

The body is one JSON object, exactly as signed:

```json
{
  "id": "01a1362b-5187-7ab3-a070-9abc82270c04",
  "topic": "documents.document.executed",
  "subject_type": "document",
  "subject_id": "7a1c6f0e-…",
  "payload": { "externalId": "crm-123", "metadata": { "deal": "42" }, "parties": {}, "test": false, "source": "sent", "form": null, "executed_at": "2026-10-13T17:02:11.000Z" },
  "emitted_at": "2026-10-13T17:02:11.412Z"
}
```

- `id` is the event's id and is the same value as the `webhook-id` header. It is **time-ordered** and it does not change when a delivery is retried or replayed, so use it to ignore a delivery you already handled.
- **Order is not promised.** If the first try of one event fails and a later event arrives first, the later one is delivered first. Put events in order by `emitted_at` (or by `id`), not by arrival.
- `payload.test` is `true` on every event of a test-mode document and `false` otherwise, so a receiver can ignore practice runs.
- `payload.parties` holds the references **you** gave for each person when you sent the document (`{}` when you gave none). It is not a list of signers.
- Events carry no internal person ids. Who did what is in the document's audit log.

## Which events

There are 29 events in all. You choose per endpoint which ones to receive:

- `documents.document.created`
- `documents.document.sent`
- `documents.document.opened`
- `documents.document.signed`
- `documents.document.declined`
- `documents.document.changes_requested`
- `documents.document.delegated`
- `documents.document.executed`
- `documents.document.voided`
- `documents.document.expired`
- `documents.document.reminder_due`
- `documents.document.bounced`
- `documents.document.downloaded`
- `documents.approval.requested`
- `documents.approval.decided`
- `documents.payment.hold_lapsed`
- `documents.payment.received`
- `documents.payment.failed`
- `documents.template.created`
- `documents.email.delivered`
- `documents.email.bounced`
- `documents.email.complained`
- `documents.email.paused`
- `documents.template.fields_detected`
- `documents.ai.allowance_low`
- `documents.usage.threshold`
- `documents.team.created`
- `documents.team.updated`
- `documents.team.deleted`

You choose per endpoint. The ones most receivers want are `documents.document.sent`, `documents.document.opened`, `documents.document.signed` (one person signed), `documents.document.executed` (everyone signed and the sealed copy exists), `documents.document.declined`, `documents.document.expired` and `documents.document.voided`. A receiver that only cares about finished documents subscribes to `documents.document.executed` and nothing else. If a document takes payment, `documents.payment.received` says a signer paid (the document, the payment id, the amount and currency) and `documents.payment.failed` says a payment plan's charge failed; `GET /api/v1/webhooks/topics` lists every event.

Every document event carries `source` (always `"sent"`) and `form` (always `null`). Both stay in the payload so receivers written before version 1 keep working.

Two more come from the workspace rather than a document: `documents.template.fields_detected` (a template was made from an uploaded file and the fields were looked for; the payload says how many were found, how many signers, how many it was unsure of and how many were placed) and `documents.ai.allowance_low` (the workspace's AI drafts reached 80% of the plan's allowance; sent once per period) and `documents.usage.threshold` (the workspace's bill passed 50%, 80% or 100% of its budget, or an early invoice or monthly summary is ready; `kind` is `budget` or `summary`).

## A receiver, step by step

1. Read the **raw** request body as bytes before any JSON parser touches it.
2. Verify the three headers against that body with the SDK, as above. If verification throws, answer `400` and stop.
3. Look at `webhook-id`. If you have processed it, answer `200` and stop; this is a repeat.
4. Queue the work (fetch the document, save the signed copy) and answer `200` at once. Do slow work after you have answered.

```bash
curl https://docustay.app/api/v1/documents/$DOCUSTAY_DOCUMENT_ID/signed.pdf \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $DOCUSTAY_API_KEY" -o signed.pdf
```

## The delivery log

Each endpoint's page shows a delivery log with the event, the result your server gave and which try it was. **Send again** replays a delivery, so you can fix your receiver and try again without making another document. Repeats carry the same `webhook-id`, which is why your receiver should ignore ids it has already handled.


---

# Test mode

A document made in test mode is a practice run:

- It is emailed **only to the person who sent it**, with `[TEST]` in the subject.
- Its pages carry a TEST watermark.
- It is left out of usage and billing.
- Signing it records nothing as a real signature event.

## Three ways in

1. Use a `dsk_test_` API key.
2. Send with `send_options.test: true` from the app's own send step.
3. Turn on **Settings → Documents → Test mode** so everything the workspace sends is a practice run.

Documents carry `test: true` in the API, and the app marks them with a Test chip and a banner on the signing page. Switch back to a live key (or turn the setting off) to send real documents.

## What it is good for

Use test mode to check your whole flow before anything real is sent: that your template places fields where you expect, that your webhook receiver verifies a delivery, that your page handles the embedded form's events, and that your own screens show a finished document. Because a test document is emailed only to you, you can send one to a made-up person and read the email yourself.

## A short run-through

Put your test key (it starts `dsk_test_`) in `DOCUSTAY_API_KEY`, the same variable every other page uses, and the id of one of your templates in place of `$DOCUSTAY_TEMPLATE_ID` (`GET /api/v1/documents/templates` lists them). Send, and open the email:

```bash
curl -X POST https://app.docustay.app/api/v1/documents/send \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $DOCUSTAY_API_KEY" \
  -H "Idempotency-Key: $(uuidgen)" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{ "templateId": "'"$DOCUSTAY_TEMPLATE_ID"'", "parties": [{ "seat": "signer_1", "name": "Practice Person", "email": "someone@example.com" }] }'
```

The answer is the same shape as a live send (it does not carry a `test` field); fetching the document afterwards shows `"test": true`. The email arrives in your own inbox, not the address you put on the seat. Sign it, then fetch the document, with the `id` the send answered in place of `$DOCUSTAY_DOCUMENT_ID`:

```bash
curl https://app.docustay.app/api/v1/documents/$DOCUSTAY_DOCUMENT_ID -H "Authorization: Bearer $DOCUSTAY_API_KEY"
```

## What test mode does not do

It does not test payments against real cards. A document made in test mode is marked as a practice run on its pages and in the API (`test: true`), and it is left out of your usage, so you can practise as much as you like.

## Checking your webhook receiver without a real signature

Test documents fire the same webhooks as live ones, so you can prove your receiver end to end. From your laptop, forward events to your own server and ask for a sample:

```bash
npx docustay listen --forward-to http://localhost:3000/webhooks --events documents.document.executed
npx docustay trigger --topic documents.document.executed
```

`listen` prints the secret to use and forwards real, signed events. To check one signature by hand, save the delivery's exact body to `body.json` and give `verify` that file, the three `webhook-*` headers of the same delivery and the secret `listen` printed:

```bash
npx docustay verify --secret whsec_… --id MSG_ID --timestamp TIMESTAMP --signature "v1,…" --body body.json
```

The recent email log is also available from the command line with `docustay logs --emails`, and in the app under Developers → Email events.

## Moving to live

When the practice run works, change one thing: the key. Nothing in the request changes. Live documents count toward your monthly allowance on Free and are emailed to the real signers.


---

# Errors, retries and limits

## Errors

Every error is `{ "error": { "kind", "message", "requestId", "retryable" } }`. `kind` is one of `validation`, `unauthenticated`, `forbidden`, `not_found`, `conflict`, `unprocessable`, `rate_limited`, `dependency`, `timeout`, `internal`. Quote `requestId` when you ask for help.

| Status | Usually means |
|---|---|
| 400 | A field is not valid; `message` says which and why |
| 401 | The key is missing, wrong, revoked or lacks the scope (one answer for all four) |
| 403 | The workspace's plan or a setting does not allow this |
| 404 | No such document, template or seat |
| 409 | The request is fine but the state is wrong (for example, voiding a finished document) |
| 429 | Over the rate limit; wait the `Retry-After` seconds |
| 5xx | Our side; safe to retry with the same `Idempotency-Key` |

## Idempotency

Requests that create a document or a template (send a document, make a template from HTML, make a template from a file) need an `Idempotency-Key` header of 8 to 200 characters. Repeating a request with the same key and the same body returns the first answer instead of doing it again. Reusing a key with a different body is an error. Other requests, such as a reminder, a void or an embedded session, do not need one. The SDKs make a key for you and reuse it on every retry.

## Rate limits

Each key has its own per-minute budget; over it you get `429` with a `Retry-After` header. See [API limits](#api-limits). Sign-in, public signing, download and verification pages also have a per-address limit shared by every server of the install.

## What counts as a document

A document is a **sent** document. A package of several documents sent together counts once. Drafts, signers, reminders, resends and test-mode documents never count.

The count is per workspace. On Free it is per calendar month in UTC and resets on the 1st. On Pay as you go, Pro and Lifetime it follows your billing month: it starts the day you subscribe (or buy Lifetime) and resets on the same day each month, the same window Stripe invoices. `GET /api/v1/usage` returns it as `periodStart` and `periodEnd`.

- **Free:** 15 documents a month. At the limit, sending is blocked with a `403` whose `error.detail.code` is `plan_document_limit` (with `used`, `limit` and `resetsAt`) and whose message says the plan allows 15 documents a month and to switch to Pay as you go or Pro. Free is never billed.
- **Pay as you go:** 15 documents each billing month are free, then $0.50 each, counted toward your budget. When the budget (default $50) is reached, sending is paused with a `403` and `error.detail.code` `budget_reached`; raise the budget in Billing to go on.
- **Pro and Lifetime:** no monthly document limit.

## Signer limits

A Free workspace can send to 15 different signers a month. A signer is anyone you send a document to, counted once a month by email address however many documents they get. Sending to your own team does not count, sending again to someone you already sent to this month never counts, and reminders and resends are free. At 12 you get a soft warning and at 14 a note that one is left; a 16th new person is refused with a `403` whose `error.detail.code` is `plan_signer_limit` (`used`, `limit`, `newSigners`, `resetsAt`). Everything already made keeps working. Pay as you go, Pro and Lifetime have no signer limit. This limit starts on 1 November 2026.

## Template limits

A Free workspace can make 5 new templates a month, however they are made: written, uploaded, customized from a built-in template, duplicated, described in words, made by Scribe or created through the API, SDKs, CLI or MCP. A new version of a template you already have does not count, and nor does sending straight from a built-in template (the built-in is read-only; only "Customize" makes your own copy, and that counts). Deleting a template does not give one back. The count is per calendar month in UTC and resets on the 1st.

- **Free:** 5 new templates a month. Every template you already have stays usable and editable. At the limit, making a new one is refused with a `403` whose `error.detail.code` is `plan_template_limit`:

```json
{
  "error": {
    "kind": "forbidden",
    "message": "Your Free plan includes 5 new templates a month and you have made 5. …",
    "requestId": "req_123",
    "retryable": false,
    "detail": { "code": "plan_template_limit", "used": 5, "limit": 5, "resetsAt": "2026-11-01T00:00:00Z" }
  }
}
```

- **Pay as you go:** 25 new templates a month from 1 November 2026, refused with the same `plan_template_limit` code (the prompt offers Pro, not a per-template charge).
- **Pro and Lifetime:** no template limit.
- **Self-hosted:** no template limit.

## Email limits

Each workspace can send 25 emails a day on Free and 500 a day on every paid plan. In a workspace's first 7 days the lines are lower (10 a day on Free, 100 a day on a paid plan), because a brand-new workspace that mails many people on day one is the usual shape of misuse; they go back to the plan's number on day 8. Signing requests, reminders and completed copies sent to signers count. Alerts to the workspace owner, sign-in emails and the usage warning emails do not count and are never blocked. A self-hosted install has no limit. The day is a UTC day and the count resets at midnight UTC. When the limit is reached the send is refused with a plain message.

Hosted email is sent by Docustay with your name and reply-to. A self-hosted install sends from its own domain or SMTP server: see [Email setup](/docs/email-setup).

## API limits

Each API key may make 600 requests per minute. Over that, the API answers `429` with a `Retry-After` header (in seconds). Three limits can answer `429`, and the message says which one: `rate limit exceeded for this API key` (the key's 600 a minute), `rate limit exceeded for <bucket>` (one kind of call, such as `documents` for field detection), and `too many requests from this address` (all callers from one IP address). Each answer carries its own wait in both `Retry-After` and `error.detail.retryAfterSeconds`, always the same number; two different `429`s can name different waits. Nothing is lost if you wait and retry. Retried `POST` requests with the same `Idempotency-Key` never send twice. There are no per-call or per-API-document fees on any plan.

## Fair use on Pro and Lifetime

Pro and Lifetime are unlimited for one organisation's own documents. A login belongs to one person. We look at, and may ask you about, a workspace with more than 50 team members or more than 2,000 documents sent in a month. On any plan we also look at a workspace that stores more than 10 GB. We contact you first and agree a plan; we do not pause or bill extra charges automatically for volume alone. Sending that draws spam complaints is different: the email guard pauses it (see the email section) and we look at it with you.

## Other plan rules and their errors

- **Using your own AI provider key** is part of Pay as you go, Pro and Lifetime. You save it in the app under **Settings → AI drafting** (the API has no route that takes a provider key). On Free, saving a key is refused with `own_key_needs_plan` (403).
- **Switching plans** from Billing credits the unused, already-paid time against the new plan when you move up; the confirm box shows the amount first. If the amount changed while you looked, the switch is refused with `switch_numbers_changed` (400) and the new amount is returned. A declined card is `switch_card_declined`; nothing is changed.
- **A lost dispute** on a plan payment pauses sending and AI drafting in that workspace: sends are refused with `workspace_on_hold` (403) until we lift it.
- **A spam-report pause** (the email guard) cannot be resumed from the app: `email_paused_for_spam` (403). Contact support.
- **Free workspaces** may be signed in on three devices at once; a fourth sign-in signs out the oldest.

## Usage and alerts

The Billing page shows documents sent this month, new templates made this month and emails sent today. We email the workspace owner once when 80% and once when 100% of the Free monthly document limit is used (the 12th and the 15th document). On Pay as you go the alerts come at 50%, 80% and 100% of your budget, and arrive as the `documents.usage.threshold` webhook too, and once a day when 80% and 100% of the daily email limit is used (Free: the 20th and the 25th email; paid plans: the 400th and the 500th).

`GET /api/v1/usage` returns the same numbers. It needs an API key with `documents:read`.

```bash
curl https://app.docustay.app/api/v1/usage -H "Authorization: Bearer $DOCUSTAY_API_KEY"
```

```json
{
  "plan": "free",
  "period": { "start": "2026-10-01T00:00:00Z", "end": "2026-11-01T00:00:00Z" },
  "documents": { "used": 4, "limit": 15 },
  "templates": { "used": 2, "limit": 5, "resetsAt": "2026-11-01T00:00:00Z" },
  "emails": { "usedToday": 6, "limitPerDay": 25, "resetsAt": "2026-10-07T00:00:00Z" }
}
```

`emails.limitPerDay` is the most this workspace may send **today**. For a workspace's first 7 days it is lower than the plan's `limits.emailsPerDay`: 10 a day on Free and 100 on a paid plan. After that the two are the same.

## Pagination

Lists take `limit` (1 to 200) and `cursor`. The answer carries `page.nextCursor` (null on the last page).

## Upload limits

Files uploaded for signing in the app are limited to 25 MB on Free and Pay as you go, and 100 MB on Pro and Lifetime.

Through the API most request bodies are limited to 1 MB (`413` above that); written documents and HTML templates take up to 3 MB. The two routes that take a file, `POST /api/v1/templates/file` and `POST /api/v1/documents/detect-fields`, take a file up to your plan's upload limit (sent as base64); a bigger file is refused with `400` and the code `too_big`.

## A retry loop that is safe

Always send the same `Idempotency-Key` on every retry of one logical request, and wait for `Retry-After` on a `429`:

```js
async function sendWithRetry(body) {
  const key = crypto.randomUUID();
  for (let attempt = 0; attempt < 5; attempt += 1) {
    const r = await fetch("https://docustay.app/api/v1/documents/send", {
      method: "POST", body: JSON.stringify(body),
      headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${process.env.DOCUSTAY_API_KEY}`, "Idempotency-Key": key, "Content-Type": "application/json" },
    });
    if (r.status !== 429 && r.status < 500) return r;
    await new Promise((ok) => setTimeout(ok, (Number(r.headers.get("retry-after")) || 2 ** attempt) * 1000));
  }
  throw new Error("still failing after five tries");
}
```

## Reading an error

```json
{ "error": { "kind": "validation", "message": "Parties: signer_2 is not a seat on this template.", "requestId": "req_123", "retryable": false } }
```

`retryable: false` means sending the same thing again will fail the same way: fix the request. `retryable: true` means try again with the same key.

## Finding fields through the API

`POST /api/v1/documents/detect-fields` runs on our server and does not use an AI model, so it is not counted as an AI draft and costs nothing. To keep one workspace from using all of it, each workspace may make 30 calls an hour; past that the answer is a `429` with `Retry-After`.


---

# Email setup

## On the hosted service

Nothing to set up. Docustay sends your signing requests, reminders and completed copies from its own verified sending domain, with **your name** as the sender and your address as the reply-to, so a reply goes to you. Hosted workspaces cannot send from their own domain, mailbox or SMTP server. The rest of this page is for a **self-hosted** install, which sends from your own domain.

## On a self-hosted install

Signing requests only help if they arrive. Mail sent from your own domain is far more likely to reach the inbox when the domain publishes three DNS records: SPF, DKIM and DMARC. Docustay shows the exact values to use; this page explains what they are. Every record below uses `example.com`: replace it with your domain.

## The three records

**SPF** says which servers may send for your domain. It is a `TXT` record on the sending domain. For a provider, it looks like this:

```
example.com.  TXT  "v=spf1 include:<provider's include> ~all"
```

A domain may have only **one** SPF record. If you already have one, add the provider's `include:` to it instead of adding a second record.

**DKIM** signs each message. The provider gives you a selector and a public key. Add them as a `TXT` or `CNAME` record exactly as shown:

```
selector1._domainkey.example.com.  TXT  "v=DKIM1; k=rsa; p=<public key from your provider>"
```

**DMARC** tells receivers what to do when SPF and DKIM fail, and where to send reports. Start by only watching:

```
_dmarc.example.com.  TXT  "v=DMARC1; p=none; rua=mailto:dmarc@example.com"
```

When the reports look clean, move to `p=quarantine`.

## Verify in Docustay

1. Open **Settings → Email**.
2. Add the domain.
3. Add the records it shows at your DNS host.
4. Press **Verify**.

The state shows **pending** until DNS answers. DNS can take minutes to hours.

## Test it

Send a test email to a mailbox you control. In the message's headers (often "Show original") look for `spf=pass`, `dkim=pass` and `dmarc=pass`.

## Self-hosting

The self-host environment file (`docustay/.env.example`) takes one of two options:

- `RESEND_API_KEY`: your own Resend API key.
- Your own SMTP server: leave `RESEND_API_KEY` empty and enter the server in **Settings → Email** after you sign in. Amazon SES works this way too: SES gives you SMTP credentials (in the SES console, “SMTP settings”); enter that server, port 587 and those credentials, and your sending goes through your SES account and never through ours.

`KEYSTONE_MAIL_SENDER` is the default From address used until you verify your own domain, and `KEYSTONE_PUBLIC_URL` is the address used for links in emails. If neither option is set, Docustay says email isn't set up and will not invite signers.

## Common mistakes

- **Two SPF records.** Merge them into one with all the `include:` entries.
- **A mistyped DKIM selector.** The record name must match the selector exactly.
- **A trailing dot.** Some DNS hosts add your domain for you; a name entered with a trailing dot, or with the domain repeated, ends up in the wrong place.
- **Cached answers.** A long TTL on an old record keeps the old answer until it expires; wait, then press Verify again.


---

# SDKs

Both clients cover every operation in the [API reference](/docs/api-reference.md), add an `Idempotency-Key` to every POST and reuse it on retries, retry `429` and `5xx` honouring `Retry-After`, throw a typed error with `status`, `kind` and the request id, page through lists for you and verify webhooks.

| Language | Package | Needs |
|---|---|---|
| JavaScript / TypeScript | `@docustay2026/sdk` | Node 18+, a browser, Deno or Bun; no dependencies |
| Python | `docustay` | Python 3.9+; standard library only |

```js
import { Docustay } from "@docustay2026/sdk";
const docustay = new Docustay(process.env.DOCUSTAY_API_KEY);
for await (const d of docustay.eachDocument({ state: "executed" })) console.log(d.id, d.title);
```

```python
import os
from docustay import Docustay
d = Docustay(os.environ["DOCUSTAY_API_KEY"])
for doc in d.each_document(state="executed"): print(doc["id"], doc["title"])
```

Other languages: the API is described by an OpenAPI 3.1 file at `/api/openapi.json` and a Postman collection at `/api/docustay.postman_collection.json`.
Frameworks: [`@docustay2026/react`, `@docustay2026/vue`, `@docustay2026/angular`](/docs/embedding.md).

## Pointing at your own server

Both clients talk to `https://app.docustay.app` unless you say otherwise. A self-hosted install, or any other Docustay address, goes in the constructor:

```js
import { Docustay } from "@docustay2026/sdk";
const docustay = new Docustay(process.env.DOCUSTAY_API_KEY, { baseUrl: process.env.DOCUSTAY_URL });   // your install, for example https://sign.example.com
const { templates } = await docustay.listTemplates();
console.log(templates.length, "templates on that install");
```

```python
import os
from docustay import Docustay
d = Docustay(os.environ["DOCUSTAY_API_KEY"], base_url=os.environ["DOCUSTAY_URL"])   # your install, for example https://sign.example.com
print(len(d.list_templates()["templates"]), "templates on that install")
```

If the address is wrong and answers with a web page instead of the API, the client throws a `DocustayError` of kind `bad_response` that names the address and this option; it does not show a JSON parse error.

## Installing

Install from the registries: `npm install @docustay2026/sdk` (JavaScript and TypeScript), `pip install docustay` (Python), `go get github.com/docustay/docustay-go/docustay`, `composer require docustay/docustay-php`, `dotnet add package Docustay.Api`. In a new TypeScript project for Node, also run `npm install --save-dev typescript @types/node` so `process.env` compiles. The source is at https://github.com/Docustay/docustay.

## Sending a document

```js
import { Docustay } from "@docustay2026/sdk";
const docustay = new Docustay(process.env.DOCUSTAY_API_KEY);
const doc = await docustay.sendDocument({ templateId: process.env.DOCUSTAY_TEMPLATE_ID, parties: [{ seat: "signer_1", name: "Rosa Alvarez", email: "rosa@example.com" }] });
console.log(doc.id, doc.state);
```

```python
doc = d.send_document(template_id=os.environ["DOCUSTAY_TEMPLATE_ID"], parties=[{"seat": "signer_1", "name": "Rosa Alvarez", "email": "rosa@example.com"}])
print(doc["id"], doc["state"])
```

## Which client to use

Use the JavaScript and TypeScript client for anything that runs in Node, a serverless function, Deno or Bun, and keep the key on the server. Use the Python client for scripts, back-office jobs and notebooks. Neither needs extra packages, so adding one does not pull a tree of dependencies into your project. If you work in another language, call the REST API directly or use a client generated from the OpenAPI file; every client sends the same requests, so the API reference applies to all of them.

## Keys, test mode and retries

Create a key under Developers and pass it to the constructor. A key that starts with `dsk_test_` works in test mode: it sees only test documents and emails only you (stamped TEST), never the people on the document, so use one while you are building. Because every POST carries an `Idempotency-Key`, a request that times out can be sent again without creating a second document. Let the client do the retrying; add your own loop only for failures it reports as final.

## Handling errors

Both clients throw a typed error with `status`, `kind`, `message` and `requestId`. Catch it, look at `kind`, and decide: `validation` means fix the request, `rate_limited` and `dependency` are retried for you up to a limit, and `conflict` means the document is not in a state that allows what you asked.

## Other languages

Any language can call the REST API directly. The OpenAPI 3.1 file describes every operation. Clients generated from it for Go, PHP and C# (every operation) are published: `go get github.com/docustay/docustay-go/docustay`, `composer require docustay/docustay-php` and `dotnet add package Docustay.Api`. A generated client sends an idempotency key as an argument of each call that creates something, and its answers may carry new fields as the API grows. The Postman collection lets you try each call by hand.

A first call in each (make a template, send it to one person, read it back). Set `DOCUSTAY_API_KEY` first; a `dsk_test_` key makes it a practice run. To use your own install, change the host where shown.

```go
package main

import (
	"context"
	"fmt"
	"os"
	"time"

	docustay "github.com/docustay/docustay-go/docustay"
)

func main() {
	cfg := docustay.NewConfiguration() // hosted: app.docustay.app. Own install: cfg.Servers = docustay.ServerConfigurations{{URL: "https://sign.example.com"}}
	c := docustay.NewAPIClient(cfg)
	ctx := context.WithValue(context.Background(), docustay.ContextAccessToken, os.Getenv("DOCUSTAY_API_KEY"))
	html := "<h1>Mutual NDA</h1><p>Signed: {{Sign here;type=signature;role=Partner}}</p>"
	t, _, err := c.TemplatesAPI.CreateTemplateFromHtml(ctx).IdempotencyKey(fmt.Sprint("t-", time.Now().UnixNano())).HtmlTemplateRequest(*docustay.NewHtmlTemplateRequest("Mutual NDA", html)).Execute()
	if err != nil { fmt.Println(err); return } // the error says what the API said, e.g. "400 Bad Request: validation: ..."
	p := docustay.NewSendRequestPartiesInner("signer_1", "Alex Rivera", "alex@example.com")
	d, _, err := c.DocumentsAPI.SendDocument(ctx).IdempotencyKey(fmt.Sprint("d-", time.Now().UnixNano())).SendRequest(*docustay.NewSendRequest(t.TemplateId, []docustay.SendRequestPartiesInner{*p})).Execute()
	if err != nil { fmt.Println(err); return }
	fmt.Println("sent", d.Id, d.State)
}
```

```php
<?php
require __DIR__ . '/vendor/autoload.php';
$config = Docustay\Configuration::getDefaultConfiguration()
    ->setAccessToken(getenv('DOCUSTAY_API_KEY')); // own install: ->setHost('https://sign.example.com')
$templates = new Docustay\Api\TemplatesApi(new GuzzleHttp\Client(), $config);
$documents = new Docustay\Api\DocumentsApi(new GuzzleHttp\Client(), $config);
try {
    $t = $templates->createTemplateFromHtml(bin2hex(random_bytes(16)), new Docustay\Model\HtmlTemplateRequest([
        'name' => 'Mutual NDA',
        'html' => '<h1>Mutual NDA</h1><p>Signed: {{Sign here;type=signature;role=Partner}}</p>',
    ]));
    $d = $documents->sendDocument(bin2hex(random_bytes(16)), new Docustay\Model\SendRequest([
        'template_id' => $t->getTemplateId(),
        'parties' => [new Docustay\Model\SendRequestPartiesInner(['seat' => 'signer_1', 'name' => 'Alex Rivera', 'email' => 'alex@example.com'])],
    ]));
    echo 'sent ', $d->getId(), ' ', $d->getState(), "\n";
} catch (Docustay\ApiException $e) {
    echo $e->getCode(), ': ', $e->getResponseBody(), "\n";
}
```

```csharp
using Docustay.Api.Api;
using Docustay.Api.Client;
using Docustay.Api.Model;

var cfg = new Configuration { AccessToken = Environment.GetEnvironmentVariable("DOCUSTAY_API_KEY") }; // own install: BasePath = "https://sign.example.com"
try
{
    var t = new TemplatesApi(cfg).CreateTemplateFromHtml(Guid.NewGuid().ToString(), new HtmlTemplateRequest(
        name: "Mutual NDA", html: "<h1>Mutual NDA</h1><p>Signed: {{Sign here;type=signature;role=Partner}}</p>"));
    var d = new DocumentsApi(cfg).SendDocument(Guid.NewGuid().ToString(), new SendRequest(templateId: t.TemplateId,
        parties: new List<SendRequestPartiesInner> { new(seat: "signer_1", name: "Alex Rivera", email: "alex@example.com") }));
    Console.WriteLine($"sent {d.Id} {d.State}");
}
catch (ApiException e) { Console.WriteLine($"{e.ErrorCode}: {e.ErrorContent}"); }
```

# MCP server and agent skills

`@docustay2026/mcp` is a Model Context Protocol server. It runs on your own computer with your own API key and gives an assistant 39 tools. The main ones are `list_templates`, `get_template`, `list_documents`, `get_document`, `get_audit_log`, `save_signed_pdf`, `send_document`, `remind`, `void_document`, `create_template_from_html`, `detect_fields`, `search_documents`, `list_payments`, `list_plays`, `list_playbooks` and `get_ai_usage`. The rest are listed below.

```json
{ "mcpServers": { "docustay": { "command": "npx", "args": ["-y", "@docustay2026/mcp"], "env": { "DOCUSTAY_API_KEY": "dsk_test_…" } } } }
```

A server other than `https://app.docustay.app` (a self-hosted install or a practice server) is named with `DOCUSTAY_BASE_URL`, in the same `env` block.

## Safety

- **Preview first.** `send_document`, `send_draft`, `remind` and `void_document` do nothing the first time: they return a plain-words preview of who would be emailed. Only a second call with `confirm: true` acts.
- **Read-only mode.** Set `DOCUSTAY_READ_ONLY=1` and every tool that changes anything is removed.
- **Your key, your scopes.** The key decides what is possible; use a `dsk_test_` key to practise.
- **No links, no keys.** No tool returns a signing link, a code or the key.

## Words and people, and the assistant

Besides sending a template, the server can make a **draft** from written words and people (`create_document`, `use_template`), check it (`check_document`), read and change it (`get_draft_source`, `revise_document`), set a template's defaults (`set_template_defaults`), ask the Docustay assistant to draft or to propose changes (`draft_document_with_ai`, `edit_document_with_ai`, `cancel_ai_job`), read the wizard's questions (`get_wizard`) and ask whether Stripe is ready for a payment (`get_payments_status`). It can also search the workspace (`search_documents`), list payments (`list_payments`) and list the playbooks (`list_playbooks`). Refunds and switching a playbook on are left to a person: see [Search and payments](/docs/search-and-payments). Making or changing a draft emails nobody: `send_draft` is the only step that does, and it previews first. The assistant's edits come back as proposals for a person to accept. See [Documents from words and people](/docs/documents-from-words.md).

## Claude Code plugin and skills

The `docustay` plugin bundles the server and five skills: sending for signature, text tags, embedded signing, webhooks and agent safety. The skills are plain Markdown files, so any agent that reads skill files can use them.

## A conversation, step by step

You ask the assistant to send the mutual NDA to Sam, and give it Sam's email address. It calls `list_templates`, finds the NDA, then calls `send_document` without `confirm`. The preview says who would be emailed and from which template. You say yes; it calls `send_document` again with `confirm: true`. Nothing is sent until that second call.

```json
{ "name": "send_document", "arguments": { "templateId": "6f1c1f0e-7a0c-4d1d-9b5e-2f0a7b1c3d4e", "parties": [{ "seat": "signer_1", "name": "Sam", "email": "sam@example.com" }], "confirm": true } }
```

## Reading and saving

`get_document` returns the state and each person's status. `save_signed_pdf` downloads a finished copy to a folder you name on your own computer.

## Running it read-only

```bash
# start the server with only the tools that read (a command; or put DOCUSTAY_READ_ONLY=1 in the env block of your MCP config)
DOCUSTAY_READ_ONLY=1 DOCUSTAY_API_KEY=dsk_test_… npx -y @docustay2026/mcp
```

With that variable set, `send_document`, `remind`, `void_document` and `create_template_from_html` are not offered at all, so an assistant cannot call them even by mistake.


## Which key scopes each tool needs

The table is derived from the server's own route table and checked by a test, so it cannot drift: `sdk/mcp/SCOPES.md` in the repository. A key without the scope gets the same plain 401 as any bad key. For assistants that cannot run a program on your computer, use the hosted [connector](/docs/connector).


---

# Connect ChatGPT, Claude or any assistant

The hosted connector lets an AI assistant work on **drafts** in your workspace without anyone copying an API key around. You add one address to the assistant, sign in once, and say Allow.

**Address to add:** `https://app.docustay.app/mcp` (on a self-hosted install, your own address plus `/mcp`).

## What happens
1. The assistant finds the sign-in details at `/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server`, registers itself, and opens Docustay's consent page.
2. You sign in if you are not already, read what it can and cannot do, and press Allow.
3. Docustay makes a key for that assistant. It is **draft-only**, lasts 90 days, allows 100 drafts a day, and appears in Settings → Developers → API keys as “Connector: <the assistant's name>”. Revoke it there and the connector stops at once.

## What it can do
List templates (the built-in library and your own) and skills, read documents, start a draft from a built-in template (it asks you a few questions with 2 to 4 options), make a draft from a template, read a draft, and **ask** for a draft to be sent.

## What it cannot do
Send a document. “Ask to send” files a request; a person approves it in Settings → Developers → Approvals. It cannot remind, void or sign, change settings or keys, or see billing.

## Tools
`list_templates`, `get_template`, `list_documents`, `get_document`, `list_plays`, `get_play`, `start_draft`, `answer_questions`, `use_template`, `get_draft_source`, `request_send`. Every tool is one call to the same `/api/v1` routes the SDKs use, carrying the assistant's own key, so scopes, limits and the draft-only rule apply exactly as they do anywhere else.

## How the sign-in is protected
OAuth with PKCE (S256 only) and dynamic client registration; no client secret is stored. The one-time code lasts two minutes and is sealed with the install's own pepper. Return addresses must be https, or http on localhost, and must be the ones the assistant registered. The key is minted only when the code is exchanged, with the rank of the person who pressed Allow, and a person can only hand over scopes they could mint themselves.

## Your own key instead
If you would rather not use sign-in, send `Authorization: Bearer <key>` to `/mcp` with a key from Settings → Developers → API keys. The same tools and rules apply. The local server `@docustay2026/mcp` (see [MCP server and agent skills](/docs/mcp-and-skills)) has more tools, including sending with a preview step.

## Look at it from a terminal

The connector speaks the standard MCP and OAuth discovery documents, so you can see what an assistant sees before you connect it. The first call names the resource and its sign-in server; the second lists what a client may ask for.

```bash
curl -s https://app.docustay.app/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource
curl -s https://app.docustay.app/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server
```

An assistant registers itself, sends you to a Docustay page to approve, and exchanges the one-time code for a draft-only key. You can see that key afterwards under Developers with its limits:

```bash
curl -s https://app.docustay.app/api/v1/documents \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $DOCUSTAY_API_KEY"   # the draft-only key the approval made
```
